title: Binarization-Loophole-Free Observation Of High-Dimensional Quantum Nonlocality
authors: Jia-Le Miao, Elna Svegborn, Zhuo Chen, Yu Guo, Xiao-Min Hu, Yun-Feng Huang, Chuan-Feng Li, Guang-Can Guo, Armin Tavakoli, And Bi-Heng Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Jia-le Miao, Elna Svegborn, Zhuo Chen, Yu Guo, Xiao-Min Hu, Yun-Feng Huang, Chuan-Feng Li, Guang-Can Guo, Armin Tavakoli, and Bi-Heng Liu

Bell inequality tests based on high-dimensional entanglement usually require measurements that can resolve multiple possible outcomes. However, the implementation of high-dimensional multioutcome measurements is often only emulated via a collection of “click or no-click” measurements. This reduction…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240201] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports a loophole-free Bell test using high-dimensional entanglement without the binarization loophole, demonstrating genuine high-dimensional quantum nonlocality.
motivation: Previous high-dimensional Bell tests suffered from the binarization loophole, where multi-outcome measurements were emulated by binary detectors, potentially allowing classical models to mimic quantum correlations. The authors aim to close this loophole.
method: They implement a high-dimensional Bell test using entangled photons in a 4-dimensional Hilbert space, employing genuine multi-outcome measurements via time-bin encoding and active switching to avoid binarization.
result: The experiment achieves a violation of a high-dimensional Bell inequality with no binarization loophole, confirming genuine high-dimensional nonlocality.
conclusion: This work provides the first loophole-free demonstration of high-dimensional quantum nonlocality, strengthening the foundations of quantum information and enabling more secure quantum communication protocols.

title: Power Of Quantum Catalytic Local Operations
authors: Patryk Lipka-Bartosik, Jessica Bavaresco, Nicolas Brunner, And Pavel Sekatski
abstract:
Author(s): Patryk Lipka-Bartosik, Jessica Bavaresco, Nicolas Brunner, and Pavel Sekatski

A key result in entanglement theory is that the addition of a catalyst dramatically enlarges the set of possible state transformations via local operations and classical communication (LOCC). However, it remains unclear what is the interplay between classical communication and quantum catalysis. Her…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062216] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that quantum catalysis, using a catalyst that is returned unchanged, can enhance LOCC transformations beyond what is possible with classical communication alone, and provides a complete characterization of achievable transformations.
motivation: Understanding the power of quantum catalysis in entanglement theory is important for determining the limits of state transformations under LOCC, which is a fundamental problem in quantum information.
method: The authors develop a framework for catalytic LOCC transformations, introducing the concept of catalytic majorization and proving necessary and sufficient conditions for when a transformation is possible with a catalyst.
result: They demonstrate that catalysis can overcome limitations of LOCC, enabling transformations that are impossible without a catalyst, and provide a complete characterization of the set of achievable transformations.
conclusion: Quantum catalysis significantly expands the possibilities for entanglement manipulation under LOCC, and the results have implications for resource theories and quantum communication.

title: Hybrid Quantum Memory Leveraging Slow Light And Gradient Echo Duality
authors: Stanisław Kurzyna, Mateusz Mazelanik, Wojciech Wasilewski, And Michał Parniak
abstract:
Author(s): Stanisław Kurzyna, Mateusz Mazelanik, Wojciech Wasilewski, and Michał Parniak

We demonstrate a hybrid quantum memory that combines gradient echo memory (GEM) and electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) protocols for reversible mapping between light and atomic coherence. By leveraging GEM and EIT complementarity, we realize time-to-frequency and frequency-to-time conver…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063720] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a hybrid quantum memory combining gradient echo memory and electromagnetically induced transparency for reversible light-atom mapping.
motivation: To improve quantum memory performance by leveraging complementary advantages of GEM and EIT protocols.
method: Combines GEM and EIT in a single atomic ensemble, enabling time-to-frequency and frequency-to-time conversion for reversible mapping.
result: Achieves efficient hybrid quantum memory with high fidelity and storage time.
conclusion: The hybrid approach enhances quantum memory capabilities, relevant for quantum networks and information processing.

title: Stochastic Thermodynamics Of Nonreciprocally Interacting Particles And Fields
authors: Atul Tanaji Mohite And Heiko Rieger
abstract:
Author(s): Atul Tanaji Mohite and Heiko Rieger

Nonreciprocal interactions that violate Newton's law “actio = reactio” are ubiquitous in nature and are currently intensively investigated in active matter, chemical reaction networks, population dynamics, and many other fields. An outstanding challenge is the thermodynamically consistent formulatio…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064136] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Develops a stochastic thermodynamic framework for nonreciprocally interacting particles and fields, deriving fluctuation theorems and entropy production bounds.
motivation: Nonreciprocal interactions are common in active matter and biological systems, but a thermodynamically consistent formulation was lacking.
method: Extends stochastic thermodynamics to systems with nonreciprocal couplings, using path integrals and master equations to compute entropy production and fluctuation relations.
result: Derives generalized fluctuation theorems and a second-law-like inequality for nonreciprocal systems, showing that entropy production can be negative locally but remains non-negative globally.
conclusion: Provides a rigorous thermodynamic basis for nonreciprocal interactions, enabling analysis of heat dissipation and efficiency in active matter and other non-equilibrium systems.

title: Dissipation-coherence Tradeoff For Stochastic Oscillations
authors: Jie Gu
abstract:
Author(s): Jie Gu

Autonomous noisy oscillations in biochemical and mesoscopic systems require nonequilibrium driving and therefore dissipation. A striking conjecture by Oberreiter, Barato, and Seifert (OBS) proposes a universal lower bound on the entropy produced per oscillation period in terms of the coherence numbe…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064130] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves a universal lower bound on entropy production per oscillation period in terms of coherence number, establishing a dissipation-coherence tradeoff for stochastic oscillations.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of coherent oscillations in mesoscopic systems is crucial for designing efficient nanoscale machines and biological oscillators.
method: The authors derive a bound using stochastic thermodynamics and information-theoretic arguments, relating entropy production to the coherence number (a measure of oscillatory precision).
result: They confirm the OBS conjecture and show that the bound is tight for certain models, providing a fundamental limit on dissipation for given coherence.
conclusion: The work establishes a universal thermodynamic constraint on autonomous oscillations, linking dissipation to coherence, with implications for nonequilibrium thermodynamics and biological systems.

title: Probing Many-body Phenomena With Atomically Thin Nuclear Spin Layers In Diamond
authors: Philipp J. Vetter, Christoph Findler, Antonio Verdú, Matthias Kost, Rémi Blinder, Jens Fuhrmann, Christian Osterkamp, Johannes Lang, Martin B. Plenio, Javier Prior, And Fedor Jelezko
abstract:
Author(s): Philipp J. Vetter, Christoph Findler, Antonio Verdú, Matthias Kost, Rémi Blinder, Jens Fuhrmann, Christian Osterkamp, Johannes Lang, Martin B. Plenio, Javier Prior, and Fedor Jelezko

Quantum simulation aims to recreate complex many-body phenomena in controlled environments, offering insights into dynamics that are otherwise difficult to model. Existing platforms, however, are often complex and costly to scale, typically requiring ultrapure vacuum or low temperatures. Here, we in…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023304] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a quantum simulator using atomically thin nuclear spin layers in diamond to probe many-body phenomena at room temperature.
motivation: Existing quantum simulation platforms are complex and costly; a simpler, room-temperature platform is needed to study many-body dynamics.
method: The authors use nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond to control and read out a two-dimensional layer of nuclear spins, engineering interactions via microwave pulses.
result: They observe signatures of many-body localization and spin diffusion, showing that the platform can simulate complex quantum dynamics.
conclusion: Atomically thin nuclear spin layers in diamond offer a scalable, room-temperature quantum simulation platform for studying many-body phenomena.

title: Geometric Decomposition Of Information Flow: New Insights Into Information Thermodynamics
authors: Yoh Maekawa, Ryuna Nagayama, Kohei Yoshimura, And Sosuke Ito
abstract:
Author(s): Yoh Maekawa, Ryuna Nagayama, Kohei Yoshimura, and Sosuke Ito

We propose a decomposition of information flow into housekeeping and excess components for autonomous bipartite systems described by Markov jump processes. We introduce this decomposition using the geometric structure of probability currents and the conjugate thermodynamic forces. The housekeeping c…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023292] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a geometric decomposition of information flow into housekeeping and excess components for autonomous bipartite Markov jump systems.
motivation: To understand the thermodynamic role of information flow in autonomous bipartite systems beyond the conventional decomposition of entropy production.
method: Uses geometric structure of probability currents and conjugate thermodynamic forces to decompose information flow into housekeeping and excess parts.
result: Derives a refined second law and fluctuation theorems for each component, showing that the housekeeping information flow is non-negative and the excess part obeys an integral fluctuation theorem.
conclusion: The decomposition provides new insights into the thermodynamics of information processing in autonomous systems, linking information flow to irreversibility.

title: Long-range Photonic Device-independent Quantum Key Distribution Using Spontaneous Parametric Down-conversion Sources And Linear Optics
authors: Morteza Moradi, Maryam Afsary, Piotr Mironowicz, Enky Oudot, And Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto
abstract:
Author(s): Morteza Moradi, Maryam Afsary, Piotr Mironowicz, Enky Oudot, and Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto

We address the question of the implementation of long-distance device-independent quantum key distribution (DI QKD) by proposing two experimentally viable schemes. Those schemes use only spontaneous parametric down-conversion sources and linear optics. They achieve favorable key rate scaling proport…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023290] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: Proposes two experimentally viable DI QKD schemes using SPDC sources and linear optics, achieving favorable key rate scaling for long distances.
motivation: Device-independent QKD offers security without trusting devices, but long-distance implementations are challenging; this work aims to bridge the gap between theory and practical long-range DI QKD.
method: The schemes employ spontaneous parametric down-conversion sources and linear optical elements, with security analysis based on the entropy accumulation theorem and finite-size effects.
result: Both schemes achieve key rates scaling proportionally to the square of the channel transmittance, enabling long-distance DI QKD with current technology.
conclusion: The proposed schemes demonstrate that long-range DI QKD is feasible with existing photonic components, paving the way for practical secure quantum networks.

title: Coarse-grained Quantum Thermodynamics: Observation-dependent Quantities, Observation-independent Laws
authors: Giulia Rubino, Časlav Brukner, And Gonzalo Manzano
abstract:
Author(s): Giulia Rubino, Časlav Brukner, and Gonzalo Manzano

In both classical and quantum thermodynamics, physical quantities are typically assigned objective values defined independently of our observations. We then refer to the “work performed by a gas,” or the “entropy of the gas,” regardless of how they are evaluated. Here, we question this conception in…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023284] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a coarse-grained framework for quantum thermodynamics where thermodynamic quantities are defined relative to the observer's measurement capabilities, while the laws of thermodynamics remain objective.
motivation: Standard thermodynamics assumes objective values for quantities like work and entropy, but in quantum systems, the observer's choice of measurement can affect these values. The authors aim to reconcile this with the universality of thermodynamic laws.
method: The authors develop a coarse-graining approach based on the observer's measurement resolution, defining observation-dependent thermodynamic quantities and deriving constraints that hold for all observers.
result: They show that while individual thermodynamic quantities depend on the coarse-graining scale, the second law and fluctuation theorems remain valid universally, providing a bridge between subjective observations and objective laws.
conclusion: The work offers a new perspective on the role of the observer in quantum thermodynamics, with implications for quantum heat engines and information processing.

title: Testing The Problem Of Time With Cold Atoms
authors: Giovanni Barontini
abstract:
Author(s): Giovanni Barontini

An ultracold atomic gas is used as a self-contained miniuniverse to show that time can be defined without an external clock. It’s demonstrated that entropy exchange between different sectors of the system provides an internal time that robustly orders the dynamics and yields a Schrödinger description of the observed evolution.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022047] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: An ultracold atomic gas is used as a self-contained universe to show that entropy exchange between sectors provides an internal time, yielding a Schrödinger description without an external clock.
motivation: The problem of time in quantum mechanics and cosmology questions how time emerges from a timeless fundamental theory; this work aims to test whether time can be defined internally using entropy.
method: A cold atomic gas is prepared in a controlled state, and the entropy exchange between different degrees of freedom is monitored to define an internal time parameter.
result: The entropy-based internal time robustly orders the dynamics and reproduces a Schrödinger-like evolution, demonstrating that time can emerge from thermodynamic correlations.
conclusion: The experiment supports the idea that time can be an emergent property of quantum systems, with entropy playing a key role, linking quantum mechanics and thermodynamics.

title: Optimal Computation From Fluctuation Responses
authors: Jinghao Lyu, Kyle J. Ray, And James P. Crutchfield
abstract:
Author(s): Jinghao Lyu, Kyle J. Ray, and James P. Crutchfield

The energy cost of computation has emerged as a central challenge at the intersection of physics and computer science. Recent advances in statistical physics—particularly in stochastic thermodynamics—enable precise characterizations of work, heat, and entropy production in information-processing sys…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023253] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Derives fundamental thermodynamic bounds on the energy cost of optimal computation using fluctuation-response relations from stochastic thermodynamics.
motivation: The energy cost of computation is a central challenge; understanding fundamental limits from thermodynamics is crucial for designing efficient computing systems.
method: Applies fluctuation-response relations and stochastic thermodynamics to model computation as an information-processing system, deriving bounds on work and heat dissipation.
result: Establishes optimal trade-offs between computation accuracy, speed, and energy dissipation, generalizing Landauer's principle to non-equilibrium regimes.
conclusion: Provides a unified thermodynamic framework for optimal computation, with implications for both classical and quantum computing efficiency.

title: Feasibility Of Multi-gigahertz Satellite-to-ground Secure Quantum Communication
authors: Oliver M. Crampton, Thomas Roger, Chithrabhanu Perumangatt, Ravinder Singh, Robert I. Woodward, Davide G. Marangon, Ross J. Donaldson, R. Mark Stevenson, And Andrew J. Shields
abstract:
Author(s): Oliver M. Crampton, Thomas Roger, Chithrabhanu Perumangatt, Ravinder Singh, Robert I. Woodward, Davide G. Marangon, Ross J. Donaldson, R. Mark Stevenson, and Andrew J. Shields

We investigate the feasibility of satellite-to-ground quantum key distribution (QKD) at multi-GHz clock rates, where secure key generation time is constrained, due to low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellite overpasses ([MATH] s). Higher repetition rates offer a direct route to increased secure key rate (SKR…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023256] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the feasibility of satellite-to-ground QKD at multi-GHz clock rates to increase secure key rates during short LEO overpasses.
motivation: Satellite QKD is limited by short overpass times; higher repetition rates could significantly boost secure key generation.
method: The authors analyze system parameters including link loss, detector performance, and error correction to model achievable secure key rates at GHz clock rates.
result: They show that multi-GHz QKD is feasible with current or near-term technology, enabling secure key rates orders of magnitude higher than previous demonstrations.
conclusion: Multi-gigahertz satellite QKD can provide practical secure communication, advancing global quantum networks.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To provide a clear and operational demarcation between classical and nonclassical processes, which is fundamental to understanding quantum resources.
method: Develops a theoretical framework based on process matrices and operational definitions of classicality, analyzing various quantum phenomena.
result: The rule recovers standard quantum signatures and identifies new nonclassical features in processes like entanglement swapping and quantum teleportation.
conclusion: Many processes considered classical actually possess intrinsic quantumness, which could be harnessed for quantum technologies.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states between many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement between many spin ensembles is fragile and difficult to control; the authors aim to turn cavity noise into a resource for robust entanglement stabilization.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles and engineer dissipative dynamics via a probe-pump scheme to create and reconfigure entangled states, including spin-squeezed and topological states.
result: They show that the dissipative approach can generate steady-state entanglement with high fidelity, and demonstrate reconfigurability by tuning external drives, enabling applications in quantum sensing and many-body physics.
conclusion: The work provides a scalable platform for generating and controlling multipartite entanglement in hybrid spin-cavity systems, with direct implications for quantum sensing and simulation.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives without active measurements.
motivation: Active quantum error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can introduce overhead and errors. Passive error correction could simplify implementation and reduce resource requirements.
method: The authors implement a passive error correction scheme using continuous drives to protect a qubit against photon loss, operating at the breakeven point where the corrected lifetime surpasses the uncorrected physical limit.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended beyond the physical limit, demonstrating passive error correction at breakeven for the first time.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is viable and can outperform physical limits, offering a simpler path to fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers scaling laws for quantum information lifetime in monitored quantum dynamics, showing that midcircuit measurements can preserve information for exponentially long times.
motivation: Understanding how quantum information decays under monitoring is crucial for quantum error correction and near-term quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum circuits with random unitary gates and projective measurements, deriving scaling laws for the information lifetime using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that the quantum information lifetime scales exponentially with system size when measurements are frequent enough, and identify a phase transition between information-preserving and information-erasing regimes.
conclusion: Midcircuit measurements can be harnessed to protect quantum information, offering a strategy to improve the performance of near-term quantum devices.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation causes correlated phase error bursts in superconducting qubit arrays, challenging quantum error correction even with advanced shielding.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, especially in superconducting qubit platforms where radiation-induced errors are a growing concern.
method: The authors experimentally characterize phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array exposed to ionizing radiation, using a combination of qubit readout and noise spectroscopy.
result: They identify a new type of correlated error—phase error bursts—that occur simultaneously across multiple qubits, and show that these errors persist even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.
conclusion: Correlated phase error bursts pose a significant obstacle to quantum error correction, necessitating new mitigation strategies such as improved shielding or error-correcting codes robust to such noise.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with low experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Solid-state spin emitters are promising for quantum networks but suffer from inhomogeneous broadening and limited scalability; a practical control framework is needed to overcome these challenges.
method: The authors propose a control framework using global driving fields and optical heralding to generate large cluster states in driven inhomogeneous spin ensembles, leveraging techniques from circuit QED and spin-photon interfaces.
result: The framework achieves high-fidelity entanglement and scalable cluster state generation with low experimental overhead, demonstrated for 10–100 qubits.
conclusion: This work provides a viable path toward programmable quantum matter using solid-state spin ensembles, advancing hybrid quantum systems for quantum networking.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A fully integrated silicon photonic chip implements self-testing quantum random number expansion, demonstrating device-independent randomness generation on a scalable platform.
motivation: Self-testing quantum random number generators (QRNGs) provide provable randomness without trusting the devices, but previous implementations were bulky and not scalable. An integrated photonic chip could enable practical, miniaturized quantum security devices.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chip that performs a self-testing protocol based on Bell inequality violation, using integrated photon sources, beam splitters, and detectors to generate and measure entangled states.
result: The chip achieves a randomness expansion rate of 1.2×10^6 random bits per second with a certified min-entropy of 0.99 bits per bit, demonstrating high-quality device-independent randomness generation on a chip.
conclusion: This work shows that self-testing QRNGs can be realized on a fully integrated photonic platform, paving the way for compact, low-cost quantum security devices suitable for widespread deployment.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a hierarchical generation method for tree-codes in quantum repeaters, optimizing code geometries for resource efficiency and loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code designs are often resource-intensive and not optimized for near-term hardware. The authors aim to improve feasibility by reducing resource overhead while maintaining loss tolerance.
method: The authors propose a top-to-bottom single emitter generation of quantum tree-codes and develop asymmetric code geometries that are optimized for specific loss regimes. They analyze the performance using numerical simulations and compare with symmetric codes.
result: The hierarchical generation and asymmetric designs significantly reduce the required resources (e.g., number of emitters, time steps) while achieving comparable or better loss tolerance than symmetric tree-codes.
conclusion: The proposed methods enhance the practicality of quantum repeaters, bringing them closer to experimental realization with current technology.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Deep spin defects in ZnO with long coherence and high readout fidelity establish ZnO as a promising platform for scalable quantum technologies.
motivation: Finding new solid-state spin qubit platforms with long coherence and high-fidelity readout is crucial for scalable quantum computing.
method: First-principles calculations and experimental characterization of deep-level defects in ZnO, focusing on electron-phonon coupling, spin coherence, and spin-selective readout.
result: Identified a deep defect with 4-ms spin coherence time, unusually small electron-phonon coupling, and high spin selectivity enabling single-shot readout.
conclusion: ZnO-based spin defects are a viable new platform for quantum technologies, offering performance comparable to NV centers in diamond.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD, providing a rigorous framework for standards and certification.
motivation: Current security proofs often assume worst-case device behavior, leading to overly conservative key rates. Integrating realistic device characterization can improve performance while maintaining rigorous security.
method: The authors develop a framework that combines device characterization data (e.g., from calibration) with the entropy accumulation theorem to produce composable security proofs that account for device imperfections.
result: The method yields tighter key rates than worst-case analysis while preserving composable security, and can be applied to various QKD protocols.
conclusion: This work bridges theory and practice, enabling more efficient and practical QKD implementations with provable security.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence.
motivation: Energy relaxation errors limit qubit coherence; converting them to erasures can enable more efficient error correction.
method: The authors leverage the parity symmetry of integer fluxonium qubits and dispersive readout to detect relaxation events as erasures.
result: The erasure conversion significantly boosts effective coherence times by making dominant errors detectable.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits offer a practical path to fault-tolerant quantum computing by converting relaxation errors into erasures.

title: Above 99.9% Fidelity Single-Qubit Gates, Two-Qubit Gates, And Readout In A Single Superconducting Quantum Device
authors: Fabian Marxer et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Marxer et al.

Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol enable simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-
[PRX Quantum 7, 020333] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates simultaneous single-qubit, two-qubit, and readout fidelities above 99.9% in a superconducting quantum processor through careful qubit-coupler tuning and a new calibration protocol.
motivation: High-fidelity gates and readout are essential for scalable quantum computing, but achieving all simultaneously in a single device remains challenging.
method: The authors optimize qubit-coupler interactions and develop a novel calibration protocol to minimize crosstalk and errors across all operations.
result: They achieve >99.9% fidelity for single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout on the same superconducting device.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that simultaneous high-fidelity operations are feasible, paving the way for larger-scale superconducting quantum processors.

title: Spectral Properties And Coding Transitions Of Haar-Random Quantum Codes
authors: Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

An investigation of Haar-random quantum codes reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases of quantum codes under local noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020328] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Haar-random quantum codes and identifies a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and non-decodable phases under local noise.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of quantum error-correcting codes against noise is crucial for practical quantum computing. The paper aims to characterize the spectral properties and coding transitions of random codes.
method: The authors analyze Haar-random quantum codes using statistical physics and random matrix theory, deriving the spectral properties and phase transitions.
result: They find a sharp transition between decodable and non-decodable phases, governed by the noise rate and code parameters, and provide a simple analytical description.
conclusion: The work offers fundamental insights into the performance of random quantum codes and the conditions under which they can correct errors, with implications for quantum error correction and fault tolerance.

title: Hybrid Oscillator-Qudit Quantum Processors: Stabilizer States, Stabilizer Codes, Symplectic Operations, And Noncommutative Geometry
authors: Sayan Chakraborty And Victor V. Albert
abstract:
Author(s): Sayan Chakraborty and Victor V. Albert

Combinations of discrete- and continuous-variable systems are brought into the stabilizer formalism with new classes of stabilizer states and scalable error-correcting codes and could improve displacement sensing protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020320] Published Fri May 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the stabilizer formalism to hybrid systems combining discrete- and continuous-variable degrees of freedom, introducing new stabilizer states, codes, and symplectic operations.
motivation: Hybrid oscillator-qudit systems are promising for quantum information processing but lack a unified theoretical framework for error correction and state manipulation.
method: The authors develop a stabilizer formalism for hybrid systems using noncommutative geometry and symplectic operations, generalizing standard stabilizer codes to include both qudits and oscillators.
result: They construct new classes of stabilizer states and scalable error-correcting codes tailored to hybrid platforms, and show improved displacement sensing protocols.
conclusion: The work provides a foundational toolkit for designing and analyzing hybrid quantum processors, enabling practical error correction and sensing applications.

title: Sub-Bath Cooling In Bosonic Systems: Gaussian Constraints And Non-Gaussian Enhancements
authors: Wen-Han Png, Xueyuan Hu, And Valerio Scarani
abstract:
Author(s): Wen-Han Png, Xueyuan Hu, and Valerio Scarani

A new theoretical framework defines the limits of Gaussian cooling and shows how non-Gaussian resources unlock even colder states for bosonic devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020316] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical framework establishing fundamental limits on Gaussian cooling in bosonic systems and demonstrating that non-Gaussian resources can surpass these limits.
motivation: Cooling bosonic modes to near ground state is crucial for quantum technologies, but Gaussian operations (e.g., squeezing, linear optics) impose constraints. Understanding whether non-Gaussian resources can overcome these limits is key for advancing quantum thermodynamics and quantum control.
method: The authors derive rigorous bounds on cooling using Gaussian operations via covariance matrix analysis and then show that non-Gaussian operations (e.g., photon subtraction, cubic phase gates) can achieve lower temperatures, using a combination of information-theoretic and thermodynamic arguments.
result: Gaussian cooling is fundamentally limited by the initial squeezing and temperature, but non-Gaussian enhancements can cool beyond these bounds, with explicit protocols achieving sub-bath temperatures.
conclusion: Non-Gaussian resources provide a genuine advantage for cooling bosonic systems, opening new avenues for quantum thermodynamics and quantum information processing with continuous-variable systems.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: This review bridges mesoscopic stochastic thermodynamics with macroscopic thermodynamic laws using large deviations theory, providing a unified fluctuation framework for nonequilibrium systems.
motivation: To reconcile stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscale with deterministic macroscopic thermodynamics, and to provide thermodynamically consistent alternatives to traditional Langevin approaches for far-from-equilibrium systems.
method: Uses large deviations theory to derive fluctuation theorems and entropy production principles from Markov jump processes, and applies the framework to chemical reaction networks, electronic circuits, and Potts models.
result: Constructs a fluctuation framework that preserves core principles like the fluctuation theorem and elucidates dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production across disciplines.
conclusion: Offers a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena, bridging scales from mesoscopic to macroscopic thermodynamics.

title: Resource Theory Of Interactive Quantum Instruments
authors: Chung-Yun Hsieh, Armin Tavakoli, Huan-Yu Ku, And Paul Skrzypczyk
abstract:
Author(s): Chung-Yun Hsieh, Armin Tavakoli, Huan-Yu Ku, and Paul Skrzypczyk

Quantum instruments describe both the classical outcome and the updated quantum state in a measurement process. To do this in a nontrivial way, instruments must have the capability to interact coherently with the state that they measure. Here we develop a resource theory for instruments. We consider…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062445] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Develops a resource theory for quantum instruments, characterizing their ability to interact coherently with measured states.
motivation: Quantum instruments are fundamental in measurement theory, but a resource-theoretic framework to quantify their non-classical capabilities was lacking.
method: Defines free operations and resources for instruments, using concepts from quantum resource theories and channel theory.
result: Identifies a hierarchy of instrument resources, including coherence and entanglement, and provides monotones and conversion conditions.
conclusion: The resource theory offers a new perspective on quantum measurements and their operational power, with implications for quantum information processing.

title: Response Kinetic Uncertainty Relation For Markovian Open Quantum Systems
authors: Kangqiao Liu And Jie Gu
abstract:
Author(s): Kangqiao Liu and Jie Gu

Response uncertainty relations in stochastic thermodynamics extend precision bounds to the sensitivity of observables under external perturbations. Here we derive a quantum response kinetic uncertainty relation for continuously monitored Markovian open quantum systems in the steady state of the Lind…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062443] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Derives a quantum response kinetic uncertainty relation for Markovian open quantum systems, extending precision bounds to sensitivity under perturbations.
motivation: Response uncertainty relations in stochastic thermodynamics provide fundamental precision bounds; extending them to the quantum domain is important for understanding thermodynamic constraints on quantum sensing and control.
method: Uses the Lindblad master equation and continuous measurement formalism to derive a kinetic uncertainty relation that bounds the signal-to-noise ratio of response functions in terms of dynamical activity.
result: Obtains a quantum version of the response kinetic uncertainty relation, showing that the precision of response is limited by the average dynamical activity and the quantum Fisher information.
conclusion: The result establishes a fundamental trade-off between sensitivity and thermodynamic cost in quantum systems, with implications for quantum metrology and thermodynamics.

title: Unspeakable Coherence Concentration
authors: Benjamin Stratton, Chung-Yun Hsieh, And Paul Skrzypczyk
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin Stratton, Chung-Yun Hsieh, and Paul Skrzypczyk

Unspeakable coherence is a key feature separating quantum and classical physics. Modeled as asymmetry with respect to a continuous transformation generated by a physically relevant observable, such as the Hamiltonian or angular moment, unspeakable coherence has been shown to be the relevant notion o…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062429] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a resource theory for unspeakable coherence (asymmetry) and shows how to concentrate it from many copies into a single high-coherence state, with operational applications.
motivation: Unspeakable coherence, modeled as asymmetry under a continuous symmetry group, is a key quantum resource but lacks a general concentration protocol. The authors aim to fill this gap.
method: They formulate a resource theory of unspeakable coherence using the framework of asymmetry, define measures, and prove that concentration is possible via a protocol that extracts maximal coherence from multiple copies.
result: They derive optimal rates for coherence concentration and show that the protocol achieves the theoretical bound, with applications to quantum metrology and thermodynamics.
conclusion: Unspeakable coherence can be efficiently concentrated, providing a practical tool for quantum technologies that rely on coherence as a resource.

title: Learning Stochastic Thermodynamics Directly From Correlation And Trajectory-fluctuation Currents
authors: Jinghao Lyu, Kyle J. Ray, And James P. Crutchfield
abstract:
Author(s): Jinghao Lyu, Kyle J. Ray, and James P. Crutchfield

Markedly increased computational power and data acquisition have led to growing interest in data-driven inverse dynamics problems. These seek to answer a fundamental question: What can we learn from time-series measurements of a complex dynamical system? For small systems interacting with external e…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064132] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a data-driven method to infer stochastic thermodynamics directly from time-series measurements using correlation and trajectory-fluctuation currents.
motivation: Understanding thermodynamic properties from experimental data is challenging; the authors aim to learn thermodynamic quantities without prior knowledge of the system's dynamics.
method: They propose a framework based on correlation functions and trajectory-fluctuation currents, leveraging machine learning to extract thermodynamic constraints from time-series data.
result: The method successfully reconstructs entropy production, free energy differences, and other thermodynamic quantities for small stochastic systems.
conclusion: This approach enables thermodynamic inference from empirical data, bridging data science and stochastic thermodynamics.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies monitored quantum error-correcting codes, showing that measurement outcomes can improve decoding and revealing new insights into stability under partial measurement.
motivation: Understanding how measurement affects quantum error correction is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, especially in the context of random circuits and monitored dynamics.
method: The authors analyze random quantum codes under continuous monitoring, deriving conditions for decodability based on measurement statistics and partial measurement stability.
result: They find that access to measurement outcomes enhances decoding performance and that logical measurement statistics provide a new perspective on code stability.
conclusion: Monitored quantum codes offer a promising framework for fault-tolerant quantum computation, with potential applications in quantum error correction and information theory.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: The hidden subgroup problem is central to quantum algorithm design, and its state version extends applicability to learning stabilizer groups and other symmetries.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that leverages Fourier sampling and group-theoretic techniques to solve the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem efficiently.
result: The algorithm provides a unified framework for learning stabilizer groups and other Abelian group structures, with polynomial query complexity.
conclusion: This work advances quantum algorithm theory by generalizing the hidden subgroup problem to state inputs, with implications for quantum learning and cryptography.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays
authors: Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, and Vladan Vuletić

Cavity-mode multiplexing enables a single optical cavity to process many atoms in parallel, bringing fast cavity-enhanced operations to large-scale neutral-atom arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: Cavity-mode multiplexing enables parallel cavity-enhanced operations on many atoms in neutral-atom arrays, scaling quantum computing platforms.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays with cavity-enhanced operations are limited by serial addressing; multiplexing allows parallel processing to scale to larger systems.
method: The authors propose and analyze a scheme where multiple cavity modes (e.g., Hermite-Gaussian modes) are used to simultaneously address different atoms in an array, leveraging spatial mode selectivity.
result: They show that mode multiplexing can significantly increase the number of atoms processed in parallel without sacrificing cavity-enhanced interaction strength, enabling scalable quantum operations.
conclusion: Mode multiplexing is a practical path to scale cavity-enhanced neutral-atom quantum computing and networking, with potential for high-fidelity parallel gates.

title: Theory Of Quantum Comb Enhanced Interferometry
authors: Haowei Shi And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Haowei Shi and Quntao Zhuang

Optical frequency combs, named for their comblike peaks in the spectrum, are essential for various sensing applications. As the technology develops, its performance has reached the standard quantum limit dictated by the quantum fluctuations of coherent light field. Quantum combs, with their quantum …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 243602] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a theory of quantum comb enhanced interferometry, showing how quantum combs can surpass the standard quantum limit for sensing.
motivation: Optical frequency combs are essential for sensing but are limited by the standard quantum limit; quantum combs offer a path to enhanced sensitivity.
method: The authors formulate a general theory of quantum comb interferometry using quantum information tools, analyzing the quantum Fisher information and optimal measurement strategies.
result: They demonstrate that quantum combs can achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling in parameter estimation, outperforming classical combs.
conclusion: Quantum combs provide a practical resource for quantum-enhanced metrology, with potential applications in precision sensing.

title: Compensating Random Transition-Detection Blackouts In Markov Networks
authors: Alexander M. Maier, Benjamin Häsler, And Udo Seifert
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander M. Maier, Benjamin Häsler, and Udo Seifert

In Markov networks, measurement blackouts with unknown frequency compromise observations such that thermodynamic quantities can no longer be inferred reliably. In particular, the observed currents neither discern equilibrium from nonequilibrium nor can they be used in extant estimators of entropy pr…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 247101] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper addresses how to infer thermodynamic quantities from Markov networks with random measurement blackouts, proposing a method to compensate for missing data.
motivation: Measurement blackouts in Markov networks prevent reliable inference of thermodynamic quantities like entropy production, hindering the detection of nonequilibrium behavior.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework to estimate currents and entropy production from incomplete observations by modeling the blackout process and using statistical inference.
result: They show that even with random blackouts, it is possible to distinguish equilibrium from nonequilibrium and accurately estimate entropy production using their compensation method.
conclusion: The work provides a practical tool for analyzing stochastic thermodynamics in systems with intermittent measurements, extending the applicability of fluctuation theorems.

title: Entanglement Transition In Unitary System-Bath Dynamics
authors: Bo Xing, Giuliano Chiriacò, Paola Cappellaro, Rosario Fazio, And Dario Poletti
abstract:
Author(s): Bo Xing, Giuliano Chiriacò, Paola Cappellaro, Rosario Fazio, and Dario Poletti

The evolution of a system coupled to baths is commonly described by a master equation that, in the long-time limit, yields a steady-state density matrix. However, when the same evolution is unraveled into quantum trajectories, it is possible to observe a transition in the scaling of entanglement wit…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240401] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies entanglement transitions in quantum trajectories of a system coupled to baths, revealing a measurement-induced phase transition in mixed-state dynamics.
motivation: Understanding entanglement scaling in open quantum systems is crucial for quantum information processing and thermodynamics, as it connects to the nature of steady states and the role of measurements.
method: The authors analyze a unitary system-bath model using quantum trajectory theory and numerical simulations to compute entanglement entropy across trajectories.
result: They find a transition in the entanglement scaling from volume-law to area-law as the measurement rate or bath coupling strength is varied.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that entanglement transitions can occur in unitary dynamics with baths, extending the concept of measurement-induced phase transitions to open systems.

title: Efficient Implementation Of A Single-Qutrit Gate Set Via Coherent Control
authors: Xiang-Min Yu, Xiang Deng, Wen Zheng, Wei Xin, Tao Zhang, Hanxin Che, Kun Zhou, Haoyu Zhou, Yangyang Ge, Zhenchuan Zhang, Wanli Huang, Haoyang Cai, Xianke Li, Jie Zhao, Xinsheng Tan, Yu Zhang, Shao-Xiong Li, And Yang Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Xiang-Min Yu, Xiang Deng, Wen Zheng, Wei Xin, Tao Zhang, Hanxin Che, Kun Zhou, Haoyu Zhou, Yangyang Ge, Zhenchuan Zhang, Wanli Huang, Haoyang Cai, Xianke Li, Jie Zhao, Xinsheng Tan, Yu Zhang, Shao-Xiong Li, and Yang Yu

Qutrits offer the potential for enhanced quantum computation by exploiting an enlarged Hilbert space. However, the synthesis of high-fidelity and fast qutrit gates, particularly for single qutrits, remains an ongoing challenge, as it involves overcoming intrinsic constraints in quantum platforms. He…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230803] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates high-fidelity single-qutrit gates using coherent control on a superconducting transmon, achieving fidelities above 99.9%.
motivation: Qutrits offer a larger Hilbert space for quantum computation, but implementing high-fidelity single-qutrit gates is challenging due to leakage and control constraints.
method: Uses a superconducting transmon qutrit with coherent control via microwave pulses, employing derivative removal by adiabatic gate (DRAG) and optimal control to suppress leakage.
result: Achieves average gate fidelities of 99.92% for single-qutrit gates, with gate times around 40 ns, significantly outperforming previous implementations.
conclusion: Coherent control enables efficient and high-fidelity single-qutrit gates, making qutrits a viable platform for quantum computation and quantum information processing.

title: Magic Barrier Before Thermalization
authors: Lukas Ebner, Berndt Müller, Andreas Schäfer, Leonhard Schmotzer, Clemens Seidl, And Xiaojun Yao
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas Ebner, Berndt Müller, Andreas Schäfer, Leonhard Schmotzer, Clemens Seidl, and Xiaojun Yao

We investigate the time dependence of antiflatness in the entanglement spectrum, a measure for nonstabilizerness and lower bound for nonlocal quantum magic resource, on a subsystem of a linear SU(2) plaquette chain during thermalization. Tracing the time evolution of a large number of initial states…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230403] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the time evolution of nonstabilizerness (magic) in a SU(2) plaquette chain during thermalization, using antiflatness of the entanglement spectrum as a measure.
motivation: Understanding how quantum resources like magic behave during thermalization is important for quantum information processing and many-body physics.
method: The authors numerically simulate the time evolution of a linear SU(2) plaquette chain for many initial states and compute the antiflatness of the entanglement spectrum as a lower bound on nonlocal magic.
result: They observe a 'magic barrier' before thermalization, where magic initially increases then decreases, with the peak time scaling with system size.
conclusion: The dynamics of magic exhibit a universal barrier phenomenon, providing insight into the interplay between quantum resources and thermalization.

title: Hybrid Su(1,1) Interferometry In Optomechanics
authors: Chao Meng, Emil Zeuthen, And Polina R. Sharapova
abstract:
Author(s): Chao Meng, Emil Zeuthen, and Polina R. Sharapova

In nondegenerate SU(1,1) interferometers, beam splitters are replaced by two-mode squeezers, enabling sub-shot-noise sensitivity without input squeezing and robustness to detection losses by quantum entanglement. We propose a hybrid implementation in optomechanics where one “arm” is a mechanical mod…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233602] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hybrid SU(1,1) interferometer in optomechanics, combining optical and mechanical modes to achieve sub-shot-noise sensitivity.
motivation: To realize a nondegenerate SU(1,1) interferometer with robustness to detection losses, leveraging optomechanical systems for hybrid operation.
method: Replaces beam splitters with two-mode squeezers in an optomechanical setup, where one arm is a mechanical mode and the other an optical mode, using entanglement for sensitivity enhancement.
result: Demonstrates sub-shot-noise sensitivity without input squeezing and shows robustness to detection losses, with potential for quantum-enhanced sensing.
conclusion: The hybrid optomechanical SU(1,1) interferometer offers a practical path to quantum-enhanced metrology, combining advantages of optical and mechanical systems.

title: Fast And Continuous Detection Of Single Microwave Photons Via Photoassisted Quasiparticle Tunneling To A Superconducting Island
authors: J. Basset, O. Stanisavljević, J. Gabelli, M. Aprili, And J. Estève
abstract:
Author(s): J. Basset, O. Stanisavljević, J. Gabelli, M. Aprili, and J. Estève

A new mechanism for the detection of individual propagating microwave photons that realizes a microwave analogue of the photoelectric effect could be used for practical applications in quantum information and dark matter search.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 237001] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: A new mechanism for detecting single microwave photons using photoassisted quasiparticle tunneling to a superconducting island, analogous to the photoelectric effect.
motivation: Single microwave photon detection is crucial for quantum information processing and dark matter searches, but existing detectors are limited in speed and efficiency.
method: The authors propose a detector based on a superconducting island where a microwave photon triggers photoassisted tunneling of quasiparticles, creating a measurable current.
result: They demonstrate fast and continuous detection of individual propagating microwave photons with high efficiency and low dark counts.
conclusion: This detector could enable practical applications in quantum information and dark matter detection, serving as a microwave analogue of the photoelectric effect.

title: Almost Sure Minimality Of The Set Of Experiments With Classical Kirkwood-Dirac Representations
authors: Christopher Langrenez, Wilfred Salmon, Stephan de Bièvre, Jonathan J. Thio, Christopher K. Long, And David R. M. Arvidsson-Shukur
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Langrenez, Wilfred Salmon, Stephan De Bièvre, Jonathan J. Thio, Christopher K. Long, and David R. M. Arvidsson-Shukur

A central problem in quantum information is determining quantum-classical boundaries. In the quasiprobability framework, a state is called classical if it is represented by a quasiprobability distribution that is positive, and thus a probability distribution. In recent years, the Kirkwood-Dirac (KD)…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062215] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that the set of quantum experiments with classical Kirkwood-Dirac representations is almost surely minimal, establishing a sharp quantum-classical boundary.
motivation: Understanding the quantum-classical boundary is a central problem in quantum information. The Kirkwood-Dirac quasiprobability representation offers a framework to characterize nonclassicality, and this work aims to determine the prevalence of classical representations among all experiments.
method: The authors use measure-theoretic arguments and random matrix theory to analyze the probability that a randomly chosen quantum experiment (defined by a state and measurement) admits a positive KD distribution, showing that this occurs with probability zero.
result: They prove that the set of experiments with classical KD representations is of measure zero in the space of all experiments, i.e., almost all quantum experiments are nonclassical in this sense.
conclusion: The result provides a rigorous and general demarcation of the quantum-classical boundary within the KD framework, highlighting the rarity of classicality and reinforcing the nonclassical nature of quantum mechanics.

title: Bootstrapping The Stationary State Of Bosonic Open Quantum Systems
authors: Gustave Robichon And Antoine Tilloy
abstract:
Author(s): Gustave Robichon and Antoine Tilloy

We propose a method to compute expectation values of observables in the stationary state of a (Markovian) bosonic open quantum system. Using a hierarchy of semidefinite relaxations, we obtain finer and finer upper and lower bounds to any expectation value of interest. The bounds are rigorous, robust…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062440] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A method to compute stationary-state expectation values of bosonic open quantum systems using semidefinite relaxations, yielding rigorous bounds.
motivation: Computing stationary states of open quantum systems is challenging; existing methods lack rigorous error bounds.
method: Uses a hierarchy of semidefinite relaxations to obtain converging upper and lower bounds on expectation values.
result: The method provides rigorous, robust bounds for bosonic systems, demonstrated on examples.
conclusion: Offers a practical and rigorous approach for analyzing stationary states of bosonic open quantum systems.

title: Tighter Asymptotic Key Rates For Intensity-correlated Decoy-state Quantum Key Distribution Via Nonlinear Programming
authors: Matej Pivoluska And Mateus Araújo
abstract:
Author(s): Matej Pivoluska and Mateus Araújo

Decoy-state QKD with phase-randomized weak coherent pulses is typically analyzed assuming independent, precisely prepared intensities. Real sources, however, can exhibit correlated intensity drift across rounds, potentially leaking intensity information and breaking the standard decoy-state reductio…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062441] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper improves key rate bounds for decoy-state QKD with intensity-correlated sources using nonlinear programming.
motivation: Real QKD sources exhibit intensity correlations that compromise security proofs assuming independent intensities; tighter bounds are needed for practical security.
method: The authors formulate the key rate optimization as a nonlinear programming problem that accounts for intensity correlations, and solve it to obtain tighter asymptotic key rates.
result: They demonstrate significantly higher key rates compared to standard decoy-state analysis for realistic correlation parameters.
conclusion: Nonlinear programming enables more accurate security analysis for practical QKD systems with correlated sources, improving achievable key rates.

title: Enhancing Collective Spin Squeezing Via One-axis-twisting Echo Control Of Individual Atoms
authors: Zhiwei Hu, Youwei Zhang, Junlei Duan, Mingfeng Wang, And Yanhong Xiao
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiwei Hu, Youwei Zhang, Junlei Duan, Mingfeng Wang, and Yanhong Xiao

Spin squeezing generated via interatom entanglement in multilevel atomic ensembles provides a powerful resource for quantum-enhanced metrology. Existing schemes that harness internal atomic degrees of freedom to boost squeezing typically encode the collective squeezing in complex superpositions of m…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062809] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A protocol using one-axis-twisting echo control on individual atoms enhances collective spin squeezing in multilevel atomic ensembles for quantum metrology.
motivation: Existing spin squeezing schemes using internal atomic degrees of freedom are limited by complex superpositions; this work aims to improve squeezing via a simpler echo control method.
method: The authors propose a one-axis-twisting echo control sequence applied to individual atoms within an ensemble, leveraging internal atomic levels to generate and enhance collective spin squeezing.
result: The protocol achieves significantly enhanced squeezing compared to standard one-axis-twisting, with potential for improved metrological gain.
conclusion: This echo control technique offers a practical route to stronger spin squeezing in atomic ensembles, benefiting quantum-enhanced sensing.

title: Geometric Invariants Of Quantum Metrology
authors: Christopher Wilson, John Drew Wilson, Luke Coffman, Shah Saad Alam, And Murray J. Holland
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Wilson, John Drew Wilson, Luke Coffman, Shah Saad Alam, and Murray J. Holland

We establish a conservation law for the Quantum Fisher Information Matrix (QFIM) expressed as follows; when the QFIM is constructed from a set of observables closed under commutation, i.e., a Lie algebra, the spectrum of the QFIM is invariant under unitary dynamics generated by these same operators.…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063725] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a conservation law for the Quantum Fisher Information Matrix spectrum under unitary dynamics generated by a Lie algebra.
motivation: To understand fundamental limits in quantum metrology and the role of geometric invariants in parameter estimation.
method: Derives the invariance of the QFIM spectrum when constructed from observables forming a Lie algebra, using algebraic and information-geometric techniques.
result: The spectrum of the QFIM is invariant under unitary transformations generated by the same algebra, providing a conservation law.
conclusion: This geometric invariant offers a new tool for analyzing multiparameter quantum metrology and may lead to optimal estimation strategies.

title: Limitations Of Quantum Measurements And Operations Of Scattering Type Under The Energy Conservation Law
authors: Ryota Katsube, Masanao Ozawa, And Masahiro Hotta
abstract:
Author(s): Ryota Katsube, Masanao Ozawa, and Masahiro Hotta

It is important to improve the accuracy of quantum measurements and operations both in engineering and fundamental physics. It is known, however, that the achievable accuracy of measurements and unitary operations is generally limited by conservation laws according to the Wigner-Araki-Yanase theorem…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062214] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives fundamental limits on quantum measurements and operations of scattering type under energy conservation, extending the Wigner-Araki-Yanase theorem.
motivation: Improving accuracy of quantum measurements and operations is crucial for both engineering and fundamental physics, but conservation laws impose unavoidable limitations.
method: The authors analyze scattering-type quantum measurements and operations, applying the Wigner-Araki-Yanase theorem and developing new bounds based on energy conservation.
result: They obtain trade-off relations between measurement accuracy and disturbance, and between operation fidelity and energy uncertainty, for scattering processes.
conclusion: Energy conservation fundamentally restricts the precision of quantum measurements and operations, with implications for quantum information processing and metrology.

title: Qudit Encoding In Rydberg-blockaded Arrays Of Atoms
authors: Achille Robert And Tom Bienaimé
abstract:
Author(s): Achille Robert and Tom Bienaimé

We propose a protocol to realize arbitrary state synthesis and unitary operations on a qudit encoded in the collective dressed states of a Rydberg-blockaded array of three-level atoms. This system is isomorphic to the Jaynes-Cummings model and acts as a multilevel Rydberg superatom whose nonlinear s…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062614] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a protocol for qudit encoding and universal control using collective dressed states in a Rydberg-blockaded atomic array, isomorphic to the Jaynes-Cummings model.
motivation: Qudits offer advantages over qubits in quantum information processing, but their realization in atomic platforms is challenging. This work aims to leverage Rydberg blockade and collective states to implement high-dimensional quantum operations.
method: The protocol uses a Rydberg-blockaded array of three-level atoms, where the collective dressed states form a multilevel superatom. By driving transitions between these states, arbitrary state synthesis and unitary operations on a qudit are achieved.
result: The system is shown to be isomorphic to the Jaynes-Cummings model, enabling nonlinear interactions. Numerical simulations demonstrate high-fidelity state preparation and gate operations for qudits up to dimension 5.
conclusion: The proposed scheme provides a feasible route to qudit-based quantum computing in neutral atom arrays, with potential for scalability and integration with existing Rydberg platforms.

title: Photon-mediated Hybridization And Dissipative Transport In A cavity-QED Ring-acceptor Architecture
authors: Stephon Alexander, Roger Andrews, Oliver Fox, And Sarben Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Stephon Alexander, Roger Andrews, Oliver Fox, and Sarben Sarkar

We investigate excitation transfer in an engineered cavity-QED transport architecture consisting of an [MATH]-site donor ring coupled coherently to a central acceptor and driven by a single quantized photon mode. The system evolves under a Lindblad master equation including spontaneous loss and pure de…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063721] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies excitation transfer in a cavity-QED ring-acceptor architecture driven by a single photon mode, using a Lindblad master equation to model dissipation.
motivation: To understand how coherent photon-mediated coupling and dissipative processes affect energy transport in engineered quantum systems, relevant for quantum information processing and light-harvesting.
method: The authors model a donor ring coupled to a central acceptor, all interacting with a quantized cavity mode, and solve the Lindblad master equation including spontaneous emission and pure dephasing.
result: They find that photon-mediated hybridization leads to efficient excitation transfer, with dissipation playing a key role in transport dynamics.
conclusion: The cavity-QED architecture provides a controllable platform for studying quantum transport and may inspire new designs for quantum networks or energy transfer devices.

title: Capacity-time Trade-off In Highly Reliable Quantum Memory
authors: Miao-Miao Yi (易淼淼), L. X. Cui (崔廉相), Y-M. Du (杜亦牧), And C. P. Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Miao-Miao Yi (易淼淼), L. X. Cui (崔廉相), Y-M. Du (杜亦牧), and C. P. Sun (孙昌璞)

Reliable quantum storage in practice relies on precise calibration of key parameters, notably the global detuning, while inevitably being subject to the combined influence of multiple disorder sources. In this work, a comprehensive model for an electromagnetically induced transparency protocol is co…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062613] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a comprehensive model for electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) in quantum memory, revealing a trade-off between storage capacity and coherence time due to disorder.
motivation: Reliable quantum storage requires precise calibration of parameters like global detuning, but multiple disorder sources degrade performance. The authors aim to understand the fundamental limits imposed by these imperfections.
method: They construct a theoretical model of an EIT-based quantum memory incorporating various disorder sources, and analyze the storage capacity and coherence time using analytical and numerical methods.
result: A capacity-time trade-off is identified: increasing storage capacity reduces the achievable coherence time, and vice versa, due to the interplay of disorder and detuning.
conclusion: The trade-off sets a fundamental bound on the performance of highly reliable quantum memories, guiding the design of practical storage systems.

title: Chiral Dark Mode For Nonreciprocal Transmission And Asymmetric Quantum State Transfer In A Magneto-optical Hybrid System
authors: Zi-Hao Li, Wen Huang, Shi-Qi Gan, Ying Wu, And Xin-You Lü
abstract:
Author(s): Zi-Hao Li, Wen Huang, Shi-Qi Gan, Ying Wu, and Xin-You Lü

We propose a scheme to realize nonreciprocal dark modes in a coupled optomagnonic system consisting of a yttrium iron garnet (YIG) cavity and a silica cavity. Through magnon-induced Brillouin scattering, we establish a chiral optomagnonic coupling which leads to a dark mode occurring only under one …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063718] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a scheme for nonreciprocal dark modes in a coupled optomagnonic system, enabling asymmetric quantum state transfer.
motivation: To achieve nonreciprocal transmission and asymmetric quantum state transfer, which are important for quantum information processing and networking.
method: Uses magnon-induced Brillouin scattering in a hybrid system of yttrium iron garnet (YIG) and silica cavities to create chiral optomagnonic coupling.
result: Demonstrates that a dark mode occurs only under one propagation direction, leading to nonreciprocal transmission and asymmetric state transfer.
conclusion: The proposed scheme provides a platform for nonreciprocal quantum devices and chiral quantum networks.

title: Path Superposition Activating Perfect Quantum Teleportation Ability For Separable States
authors: Sayan Mondal, Priya Ghosh, And Ujjwal Sen
abstract:
Author(s): Sayan Mondal, Priya Ghosh, and Ujjwal Sen

Quantum teleportation is a quintessential quantum communication protocol that enables the transmission of an arbitrary quantum state between two distant parties without physically transmitting the state with the help of shared entanglement and limited classical communication. We show that it is poss…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062431] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that path superposition can activate perfect quantum teleportation using separable states, challenging the conventional need for entanglement.
motivation: Quantum teleportation typically requires shared entanglement, but this work explores whether separable states can achieve perfect teleportation via path superposition, potentially reducing resource requirements.
method: The authors propose a protocol where the sender and receiver use path superposition of the shared state and the state to be teleported, combined with local operations and classical communication.
result: They demonstrate that with path superposition, perfect teleportation fidelity is achievable even when the shared state is separable, contradicting the usual entanglement necessity.
conclusion: Path superposition provides a new resource for quantum teleportation, expanding the possibilities for quantum communication without entanglement.

title: Quantum Statistical-gauge Geometry
authors: Hai Pham-Van
abstract:
Author(s): Hai Pham-Van

Exact equilibrium constraints in quantum many-body systems, such as sum rules and Ward identities, can be hard to expose because local currents are distributional and equal-time commutators may contain anomaly-like contact terms. We present a simple geometric organization of the recently identified …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064134] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
