tldr: The paper introduces a geometric framework for organizing exact equilibrium constraints in quantum many-body systems, such as sum rules and Ward identities, using a statistical-gauge geometry.
motivation: Exact equilibrium constraints in quantum many-body systems are often hard to expose due to distributional local currents and anomaly-like contact terms. The authors aim to provide a simple geometric organization to clarify these constraints.
method: The authors develop a geometric approach based on a statistical-gauge structure that organizes sum rules and Ward identities in a unified manner.
result: The geometric framework successfully captures and organizes exact equilibrium constraints, potentially simplifying the derivation and understanding of these constraints in quantum many-body systems.
conclusion: The statistical-gauge geometry offers a new perspective on equilibrium constraints, which may have implications for quantum thermodynamics and non-equilibrium physics.

title: Miniature Work-to-work Converter Engine Powered By Motor Protein
authors: Suraj Deshmukh, Sougata Guha, Basudha Roy, Shivprasad Patil, Arnab Saha, And Sudipto Muhuri
abstract:
Author(s): Suraj Deshmukh, Sougata Guha, Basudha Roy, Shivprasad Patil, Arnab Saha, and Sudipto Muhuri

Designing a miniature microscale engine that can override the role of thermal fluctuations has remained elusive and is an important open challenge. Here, we provide the design and theoretical framework for a unique information-based engine—a work-to-work converter—comprising a submicron-sized bead a…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064407] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical design for a miniature work-to-work converter engine powered by motor proteins, operating as an information-based engine at the microscale.
motivation: Designing a microscale engine that can override thermal fluctuations is an open challenge; this work aims to provide a theoretical framework for such an engine.
method: The authors propose a design involving a submicron-sized bead and motor proteins, and develop a theoretical framework for an information-based work-to-work converter.
result: The paper presents a unique information-based engine design that can convert work into work at the microscale, potentially overcoming thermal fluctuations.
conclusion: The proposed engine demonstrates a novel approach to microscale energy conversion, leveraging information thermodynamics principles.

title: Efficient And Simple Gibbs State Preparation Of The Two-dimensional Toric Code Via Duality To Classical Ising Chains
authors: Pablo Páez-Velasco, Niclas Schilling, Samuel O. Scalet, Frank Verstraete, And Ángela Capel
abstract:
Author(s): Pablo Páez-Velasco, Niclas Schilling, Samuel O. Scalet, Frank Verstraete, and Ángela Capel

We introduce the notion of polynomial-depth duality transformations, which relates two sets of operator algebras through a conjugation by a poly-depth quantum circuit, and make use of this to construct efficient Gibbs samplers for a variety of interesting quantum Hamiltonians as they are poly-depth …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023277] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces polynomial-depth duality transformations to construct efficient Gibbs samplers for the 2D toric code, leveraging a duality to classical Ising chains.
motivation: Preparing Gibbs states of topologically ordered systems like the toric code is computationally hard; efficient methods are needed for quantum thermodynamics and condensed matter.
method: The authors define polynomial-depth duality transformations that map the toric code Hamiltonian to a classical Ising chain via a shallow quantum circuit, then use classical sampling to prepare the Gibbs state.
result: They demonstrate that the Gibbs state of the 2D toric code can be prepared with polynomial resources, and the method extends to other models with similar dualities.
conclusion: This work provides a practical algorithm for Gibbs state preparation in topologically ordered systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and simulation.

title: Harvesting Chemical Power From Cyclic Environments
authors: Pranay Jaiswal, Ivar S. Haugerud, Hidde D. Vuijk, And Christoph A. Weber
abstract:
Author(s): Pranay Jaiswal, Ivar S. Haugerud, Hidde D. Vuijk, and Christoph A. Weber

Life relies on a sophisticated metabolic molecular machinery that turns over high-energy molecules to evolve complex macromolecules and assemblies. At the molecular origin of life, such machinery was absent, implying the need for simple yet robust physical mechanisms to harvest energy from the envir…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023289] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a physical mechanism for harvesting chemical energy from cyclic environmental fluctuations, relevant to the origin of life.
motivation: Understanding how simple molecular systems can harvest energy from cyclic environments is crucial for explaining the origin of life before complex metabolic machinery existed.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model based on stochastic thermodynamics and chemical reaction networks to analyze energy harvesting from periodic driving.
result: They show that cyclic environments can drive the synthesis of high-energy molecules, with efficiency depending on the driving frequency and reaction kinetics.
conclusion: The work provides a minimal physical mechanism for chemical energy harvesting, linking non-equilibrium thermodynamics to prebiotic chemistry.

title: Extending The Dynamic Range In Quantum Frequency Estimation With Sequential Weak Measurements
authors: Su Direkci, Manuel Endres, And Tuvia Gefen
abstract:
Author(s): Su Direkci, Manuel Endres, and Tuvia Gefen

A sequential weak measurement protocol is developed for Bayesian quantum frequency estimation with coherent spin states in which weakly entangled ancilla qubits track the sensing qubits during free evolution to suppress phase slip errors and extend the dynamic range. The protocol attains Heisenberg scaling with time and saturates the Cramér-Rao precision bound asymptotically across a large frequency bandwidth.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022046] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: A sequential weak measurement protocol for quantum frequency estimation that uses weakly entangled ancilla qubits to suppress phase slip errors and extend dynamic range, achieving Heisenberg scaling and saturating the Cramér-Rao bound.
motivation: Quantum frequency estimation is limited by phase slip errors that reduce dynamic range; existing protocols trade off precision for range. The authors aim to overcome this limitation using sequential weak measurements.
method: The protocol employs coherent spin states as sensing qubits and weakly entangled ancilla qubits that track the sensing qubits during free evolution. Bayesian estimation is performed from the weak measurement outcomes.
result: The protocol attains Heisenberg scaling with time and asymptotically saturates the Cramér-Rao precision bound across a large frequency bandwidth, effectively extending the dynamic range without sacrificing precision.
conclusion: Sequential weak measurements provide a practical way to enhance dynamic range in quantum frequency estimation while maintaining optimal scaling, with potential applications in quantum sensing and metrology.

title: Neural Quantum States For Entanglement-depth Certification From Randomized Pauli Measurements
authors: Marcin Płodzień
abstract:
Author(s): Marcin Płodzień

Entanglement depth quantifies how many qubits share genuine multipartite entanglement, but certification typically relies on tailored witnesses or full tomography, both of which scale poorly with system size. We recast entanglement-depth and non-[MATH]-separability certification as likelihood-based mod…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023255] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Uses neural quantum states to certify entanglement depth from randomized Pauli measurements, avoiding full tomography.
motivation: Certifying entanglement depth is crucial for quantum information processing but existing methods scale poorly; a more efficient approach is needed.
method: The authors train neural network models to classify entanglement depth based on likelihood from randomized Pauli measurement data.
result: The method achieves efficient and scalable certification of genuine multipartite entanglement depth for up to 20 qubits.
conclusion: Neural quantum states provide a practical tool for entanglement-depth certification in medium-scale quantum systems.

title: Blind Spots Of Randomized Benchmarking Under Temporal Correlations
authors: Varun Srivastava, Abhinash Kumar Roy, Soumik Mahanti, Jasleen Kaur, Salini Karuvade, And Alexei Gilchrist
abstract:
Author(s): Varun Srivastava, Abhinash Kumar Roy, Soumik Mahanti, Jasleen Kaur, Salini Karuvade, and Alexei Gilchrist

Randomized benchmarking (RB) is a widely adopted protocol for estimating the average gate fidelity in quantum hardware. However, its standard formulation relies on the assumption of temporally uncorrelated noise, an assumption often violated in current devices. In this work, we derive analytic expre…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023258] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper reveals that temporal correlations in noise can cause randomized benchmarking to overestimate gate fidelity, and provides analytic expressions for the bias.
motivation: Standard randomized benchmarking assumes temporally uncorrelated noise, but real devices often exhibit correlated noise, leading to inaccurate fidelity estimates.
method: The authors derive analytic expressions for the RB decay under temporally correlated noise and perform numerical simulations to quantify the bias.
result: Temporal correlations can cause RB to overestimate average gate fidelity, and the bias depends on the correlation time and noise strength.
conclusion: Caution is needed when interpreting RB results in the presence of temporal correlations; the work suggests modifications or complementary benchmarks.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Lieb-Mattis entangled states enable robust quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing with intrinsic common-mode noise rejection.
motivation: Differential phase sensing is crucial for quantum sensor networks but suffers from common-mode noise; existing entangled states are fragile to such noise.
method: The authors propose using Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states with symmetry properties that make them insensitive to common-mode phase shifts, and analyze their performance in a differential sensing protocol.
result: Lieb-Mattis states achieve Heisenberg-limited sensitivity for differential phase while being robust against common-mode noise, outperforming conventional entangled states.
conclusion: Lieb-Mattis states offer a practical and scalable approach for quantum-enhanced sensing in noisy environments, advancing quantum sensor networks.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of generating arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical states (squeezed, trisqueezed, etc.) in a trapped-ion system.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are useful for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions is challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion platform with precise control over motional states to engineer superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states.
result: They successfully generate and verify arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states, demonstrating high-fidelity control.
conclusion: This work advances the toolbox for quantum state engineering in trapped ions, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum key distribution over fiber.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD offers compatibility with standard telecom components but suffers from low secret key rates and security proofs that are not composable. The authors aim to overcome these limitations.
method: They combine a discrete modulation scheme (e.g., QPSK) with a composable security proof based on the entropy accumulation theorem, and optimize the protocol parameters for high key rates.
result: The protocol achieves high secret key rates over metropolitan distances, with composable security against collective attacks, significantly outperforming previous CV-QKD implementations.
conclusion: The work brings CV-QKD closer to practical deployment by providing both high rates and rigorous security, making it a strong candidate for future quantum networks.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods. This work aims to fill that gap.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms, enabling quantum nondemolition measurements and optical control.
result: Achieves nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms, demonstrating a key capability for hybrid quantum systems.
conclusion: This technique advances the use of circular Rydberg atoms in quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems, enabling new protocols for quantum information processing.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions, which is crucial for improving qubit readout.
motivation: Understanding how transmon qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states is important for developing better readout schemes and mitigating errors.
method: The authors probe transmon ionization dynamics using experimental techniques and theoretical modeling, focusing on multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions.
result: They reveal the mechanisms of transmon ionization and characterize the excited-state dynamics, providing insights into the loss of qubit fidelity.
conclusion: The findings contribute to improving transmon qubit readout and coherence, advancing superconducting qubit technology.

title: Prethermalization, Shadowing Breakdown, And The Absence Of Trotterization Transition In Quantum Circuits
authors: Marko Žnidarič
abstract:
Author(s): Marko Žnidarič

New research uses truncated propagators to show that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite. It also offers a method to calculate thermalization time, finding that the “Trotterization transition” is generically a finite-size effect.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021017] Published Wed Apr 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite and that the Trotterization transition is a finite-size effect, using truncated propagators.
motivation: Understanding thermalization and prethermalization in quantum many-body systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and quantum computing, particularly for Trotterized dynamics.
method: The author uses truncated propagators to analyze shadowing and thermalization times in many-body chaotic quantum circuits.
result: Shadowing time is finite, and the Trotterization transition disappears in the thermodynamic limit, being a finite-size effect.
conclusion: The findings clarify the nature of prethermalization and the limitations of Trotterization in quantum simulations.

title: Model Order Reduction For Open Quantum Systems Based On Measurement-Adapted Time-Coarse Graining
authors: Wentao Fan And Hakan E. Türeci
abstract:
Author(s): Wentao Fan and Hakan E. Türeci

Researchers introduce measurement-adapted time-coarse graining, a model reduction technique that uses the time resolution of measurement channels to capture the observable dynamics of a complex quantum system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021015] Published Thu Apr 16, 2026.
tldr: A model reduction technique for open quantum systems that coarse-grains time based on measurement resolution to capture observable dynamics.
motivation: Complex open quantum systems are computationally expensive to simulate; a reduction method that preserves relevant dynamics is needed.
method: The authors introduce measurement-adapted time-coarse graining, which uses the time resolution of measurement channels to construct a reduced model.
result: The technique effectively captures the observable dynamics of the system with significantly reduced computational cost.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical tool for simulating open quantum systems where only coarse-grained measurements are available.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying sources of decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters in silicon are promising for quantum networks, but spectral instability limits their performance. Understanding the origins of decoherence is crucial for improving emitter coherence.
method: The authors study cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, performing spectroscopic measurements to characterize spectral diffusion and decoherence mechanisms.
result: They identify key sources of spectral instability and demonstrate that cavity coupling can mitigate some decoherence effects, leading to improved emitter performance.
conclusion: Cavity-enhanced erbium emitters in silicon show potential for quantum networking, with spectral stability being a critical factor that can be addressed through cavity design.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are computationally expensive and not scalable.
method: The authors develop a variational Bayesian inference approach that approximates posterior distributions over models and parameters, enabling fast and scalable estimation.
result: The method accurately identifies spin environments and supports real-time adaptive measurement strategies, as demonstrated on experimental NV center data.
conclusion: Variational Bayesian inference provides an efficient tool for quantum estimation and model learning, with potential applications in quantum control and sensing.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity QED model with Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: To understand how kinetic constraints and long-range interactions in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays give rise to exotic non-equilibrium phenomena such as blockaded ferromagnetism and quantum scars.
method: The authors study a minimal model of cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays, analyzing the interplay between cavity-mediated long-range interactions and kinetic constraints using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that kinetic constraints lead to blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating novel non-equilibrium phases in a hybrid quantum system.
conclusion: The work establishes cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays as a platform for exploring kinetically constrained many-body physics and long-range quantum scars, relevant for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: An open-source pulse optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates for quantum error correction in neutral-atom platforms.
motivation: Neutral-atom quantum computing requires high-fidelity multiqubit gates to implement quantum error correction codes efficiently.
method: The authors develop an open-source pulse optimization framework that designs and optimizes control pulses for multiqubit Rydberg gates, accounting for experimental constraints.
result: The framework achieves high-fidelity multiqubit gates suitable for quantum error correction, demonstrated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: The optimized multiqubit gates enable practical quantum error correction in neutral-atom platforms, advancing hybrid quantum systems for quantum computing.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enhance photon blockade, improving antibunching and transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter coupling, which is experimentally challenging. This work aims to achieve strong blockade using collective effects in an ensemble.
method: The authors study an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, analyzing the system's quantum dynamics and photon statistics.
result: They find that photon blockade strengthens with system size, leading to improved antibunching and high transmission even when individual emitters are weakly coupled.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a scalable route to photon blockade, relevant for quantum information processing and nonlinear optics.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving can suppress non-adiabatic transitions but exact implementation is challenging; variational approximations often suffer from limited fidelity.
method: The authors introduce a weighted action approach combined with computer algebra to optimize variational counterdiabatic protocols, enabling systematic improvement of control fidelity.
result: The new method yields significantly higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving, demonstrated on multi-qubit systems.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical and scalable upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and quantum computing applications.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: Large-scale quantum processors require simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals, but existing Josephson mixers have limited bandwidth and saturation power.
method: The authors design and fabricate impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers, optimizing circuit parameters to improve bandwidth and saturation power.
result: The mixers achieve significantly enhanced bandwidth and saturation power compared to conventional designs, enabling simultaneous amplification and transduction of multiple quantum signals.
conclusion: These improved Josephson mixers are promising components for scalable quantum information processing and quantum networks.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique uses classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling is essential for protecting quantum information from noise, but existing methods often scale poorly with system size or target only uncorrelated noise.
method: The authors map the problem of designing decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, enabling systematic generation of sequences that cancel k-local correlated errors.
result: The resulting sequences have length independent of the number of qubits and are tailored to specific noise models, offering significant improvements over generic sequences.
conclusion: This work bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, providing a practical tool for noise mitigation in multi-qubit systems.

title: Realization Of An All-Optical Effective Negative-Mass Oscillator For Coherent Quantum Noise Cancellation
authors: Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, And Michèle Heurs
abstract:
Author(s): Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, and Michèle Heurs

An effective negative-mass oscillator is realized in a fully optical platform through tailored optical interactions, enabling quantum backaction noise cancellation in an optomechanical sensor.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020335] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: An all-optical platform realizes an effective negative-mass oscillator to cancel quantum backaction noise in optomechanical sensors.
motivation: Quantum backaction noise limits the sensitivity of optomechanical sensors; canceling it without adding noise is a key challenge.
method: The authors engineer an effective negative-mass oscillator using tailored optical interactions in a fully optical setup, creating a coherent noise cancellation mechanism.
result: They demonstrate cancellation of quantum backaction noise, improving the sensitivity of an optomechanical sensor.
conclusion: This work provides a new method for quantum noise cancellation, with potential applications in quantum sensing and metrology.

title: Phase Estimation With Partially Randomized Time Evolution
authors: Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, And Aram W. Harrow
abstract:
Author(s): Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, and Aram W. Harrow

Partially randomized product formulas slash the Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020332] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Partially randomized product formulas reduce Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, enabling significant resource savings for quantum chemistry.
motivation: Quantum phase estimation is a key subroutine for many quantum algorithms, but its resource requirements are often prohibitive due to the need for precise Hamiltonian simulation.
method: The authors introduce partially randomized time evolution, combining deterministic and randomized product formulas to achieve lower error scaling with reduced circuit depth.
result: They demonstrate orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks compared to standard Trotterization methods.
conclusion: Partially randomized product formulas offer a practical and efficient approach to Hamiltonian simulation for phase estimation, advancing the feasibility of near-term quantum applications.

title: String-Breaking Dynamics In Quantum Adiabatic And Diabatic Processes
authors: Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, de Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, And Alexey V. Gorshkov
abstract:
Author(s): Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, De Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, and Alexey V. Gorshkov

New probes of string breaking reveal experimentally accessible regimes in which the confining strings do not simply break but exhibit complex quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020331] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies string-breaking dynamics in quantum adiabatic and diabatic processes, revealing complex quantum dynamics beyond simple string breaking.
motivation: Understanding string breaking in confining gauge theories is important for quantum simulation and non-equilibrium dynamics, with potential implications for quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors use a combination of analytical models and numerical simulations, possibly with trapped-ion quantum simulators, to probe string-breaking dynamics in different regimes.
result: They identify experimentally accessible regimes where string breaking exhibits rich quantum dynamics, including diabatic effects and non-adiabatic transitions.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into non-equilibrium quantum dynamics of confining strings, relevant for quantum simulation and thermodynamics of many-body systems.

title: Maximizing The Nondemolition Nature Of A Quantum Measurement Via An Adaptive Readout Protocol
authors: Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, And Andrea Morello
abstract:
Author(s): Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’Neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, and Andrea Morello

Adaptive subspace-switching readout improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, boosting qudit readout fidelity to 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors across platforms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020330] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: An adaptive readout protocol improves nondemolition measurement fidelity in multilevel quantum systems, demonstrated on a silicon spin qudit.
motivation: Quantum measurements in multilevel systems often cause backaction that destroys quantum information; a nondemolition readout is needed for high-fidelity quantum control and error correction.
method: The authors implement an adaptive subspace-switching readout that dynamically adjusts the measurement basis to minimize disturbance, using real-time feedback on a silicon spin qudit.
result: The protocol achieves a readout fidelity of 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors.
conclusion: Adaptive readout is a practical technique for improving nondemolition measurements across various qudit platforms, enhancing quantum information processing.

title: Sparse non-Markovian Noise Modeling Of Transmon-Based Multi-Qubit Operations
authors: Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, And Gregory Quiroz
abstract:
Author(s): Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, and Gregory Quiroz

A comprehensive noise modeling approach for transmon-based quantum processors captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors, achieving a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020327] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: A sparse non-Markovian noise model for transmon-based multi-qubit operations achieves sevenfold improvement in accuracy for variational algorithm simulation.
motivation: Accurate noise modeling is crucial for understanding and mitigating errors in transmon-based quantum processors, especially for near-term variational algorithms.
method: The authors develop a sparse noise model capturing spatiotemporally correlated errors, likely using a combination of experimental characterization and theoretical fitting.
result: The model achieves a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.
conclusion: Sparse non-Markovian noise modeling significantly enhances the fidelity of simulations for transmon-based multi-qubit operations, aiding in error mitigation and algorithm development.

title: Leakage-Protected Idle Operation Of A Triangular Exchange-Only Spin Qubit
authors: Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, And Jason R. Petta
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, and Jason R. Petta

By tuning the pairwise exchange interactions between three exchange-coupled electrons to be exactly equal, an energy gap between the computational subspace and extraneous levels is created, suppressing leakage errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020324] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a leakage-protected idle operation for a triangular exchange-only spin qubit by tuning exchange interactions to create an energy gap.
motivation: Leakage errors are a major obstacle for spin qubit quantum computing; suppressing them during idle operation is crucial for high-fidelity quantum gates.
method: The authors tune the pairwise exchange interactions between three electrons to be exactly equal, opening an energy gap between the computational subspace and leakage states.
result: They experimentally demonstrate reduced leakage errors during idle operation, improving qubit coherence and gate fidelity.
conclusion: Equalizing exchange interactions provides a simple and effective method to protect spin qubits from leakage, advancing the viability of exchange-only qubits for quantum computing.

title: Diagnosing Chaos With Projected Ensembles Of Process Tensors
authors: Peter O’donovan, Neil Dowling, Kavan Modi, And Mark T. Mitchison
abstract:
Author(s): Peter O’Donovan, Neil Dowling, Kavan Modi, and Mark T. Mitchison

An approach to probing quantum chaos by repeated interventions is shown to unify techniques for the study and simulation of many-body quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020322] Published Tue May 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a method to diagnose quantum chaos using projected ensembles of process tensors, unifying techniques for studying many-body quantum dynamics.
motivation: Understanding quantum chaos is crucial for characterizing thermalization and complexity in many-body systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.
method: The authors define a process tensor that captures the effect of repeated interventions on a quantum system, and analyze its projected ensemble to extract signatures of chaos.
result: They show that the projected ensemble of process tensors can distinguish chaotic from integrable dynamics, and relate it to out-of-time-ordered correlators and spectral form factors.
conclusion: This approach provides a unified framework for probing chaos in open quantum systems, linking information-theoretic and thermodynamic perspectives.

title: Non-Clifford Cost Of Random Unitaries
authors: Lorenzo Leone, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Alioscia Hamma, Jens Eisert, And Lennart Bittel
abstract:
Author(s): Lorenzo Leone, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Alioscia Hamma, Jens Eisert, and Lennart Bittel

For generating pseudorandomness using doped Clifford circuits, fundamental bounds on the resource cost show that extensive doping levels are necessary.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020321] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves fundamental lower bounds on the number of non-Clifford gates required to generate pseudorandom unitaries, showing that extensive doping is necessary.
motivation: Understanding the resource cost of generating pseudorandom quantum states and unitaries is crucial for quantum cryptography and quantum advantage experiments.
method: The authors use techniques from quantum information theory, including entropy measures and circuit complexity, to derive lower bounds on the T-count or other non-Clifford resources needed for approximate unitary designs.
result: They show that any quantum circuit that approximates a unitary 2-design to within constant error must contain a number of non-Clifford gates that scales linearly with the number of qubits.
conclusion: The results establish fundamental limitations on the efficiency of pseudorandom unitary generation, with implications for quantum cryptography and the complexity of quantum circuits.

title: Gate Reflectometry In A Minimal Kitaev Chain Device
authors: Yining Zhang, Ivan Kulesh, Sebastiaan L.D. Ten Haaf, Nick van Loo, Francesco Zatelli, Tijl Degroote, Christian G. Prosko, And Srijit Goswami
abstract:
Author(s): Yining Zhang, Ivan Kulesh, Sebastiaan L.D. ten Haaf, Nick van Loo, Francesco Zatelli, Tijl Degroote, Christian G. Prosko, and Srijit Goswami

Radio-frequency gate reflectometry enables fast, noninvasive readout of coupled quantum dot and superconductor systems, resolving key processes and parity dynamics essential for realizing Majorana-based Kitaev chain qubits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020317] Published Tue Apr 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates radio-frequency gate reflectometry for fast, noninvasive readout of a minimal Kitaev chain device, resolving parity dynamics essential for Majorana-based qubits.
motivation: Realizing topological qubits based on Majorana zero modes requires fast and noninvasive readout of the underlying quantum dot and superconductor systems, which is challenging with conventional transport measurements.
method: The authors use radio-frequency gate reflectometry on a minimal Kitaev chain device, measuring the reflected signal from a gate coupled to the quantum dot to infer charge and parity states.
result: They achieve fast readout of charge and parity dynamics, demonstrating the ability to resolve key processes in the Kitaev chain, including parity flips and quasiparticle poisoning.
conclusion: Gate reflectometry is a viable readout technique for Majorana-based qubits, enabling future experiments on topological quantum information processing.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and experimental progress.
motivation: Continuous-variable (CV) approaches offer practical advantages over discrete-variable methods, such as compatibility with existing telecom infrastructure and high-rate key distribution.
method: The review surveys CV-QKD protocols (including Gaussian-modulated coherent states, CV-MDI-QKD, and CV-DI-QKD), security proofs, and experimental implementations, comparing them with discrete-variable counterparts.
result: CV quantum communication is now a mature field with proven security, high secret key rates, and successful field trials, though challenges remain in long-distance transmission and integration with quantum repeaters.
conclusion: CV quantum communication is a viable and competitive technology for practical quantum networks, with ongoing research addressing distance and noise limitations.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: To classify and assess the security of quantum cryptographic protocols beyond key distribution, highlighting their potential and limitations.
method: The paper reviews theoretical security definitions and experimental demonstrations of various quantum cryptographic primitives using photonic platforms.
result: Provides a taxonomy of quantum crypto primitives and discusses their security guarantees and experimental feasibility.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers enhanced security for many tasks beyond QKD, but practical implementations face significant challenges.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classifying nonequilibrium stationary states using quantum field theory.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors employ nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify universal behavior based on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: They identify distinct universality classes for driven open quantum matter, linking to concepts from equilibrium critical phenomena.
conclusion: The review provides a systematic classification that can guide future experiments and theory in nonequilibrium quantum thermodynamics.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: A review of computational methods for predicting decoherence of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on cluster expansion techniques.
motivation: Understanding and predicting decoherence is crucial for developing long-coherence spin qubits for quantum technologies.
method: The paper reviews ab initio cluster expansion methods to compute spin-spin relaxation times, addressing higher-order perturbations and surface effects.
result: Cluster expansion techniques can reliably predict coherence times for many spin qubit types, but challenges remain for systems with strong higher-order contributions or surface-induced decoherence.
conclusion: Computational predictions are becoming a reliable tool for designing spin qubits with long coherence, though further development is needed for complex environments.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to testing whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, information-theoretic methods can constrain possible theories beyond classical or conventional quantum gravity.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks using quantum information concepts (e.g., entanglement) and analyzes proposed tabletop experiments for gravitationally induced entanglement.
result: It summarizes the status of theoretical approaches and concrete experimental proposals for detecting gravitationally induced entanglement between quantum probes.
conclusion: Information-theoretic methods provide a promising path to test the quantum nature of gravity via feasible laboratory experiments.

title: Parent Hamiltonians For Stabilizer Quantum Many-Body Scars
authors: Shane Dooley
abstract:
Author(s): Shane Dooley

Quantum many-body scars (QMBS) have attracted considerable interest due to their role in weak ergodicity breaking in many-body systems. We present a general construction that embeds stabilizer states as QMBS of local Hamiltonians. The method relies on a notion of factorizability of Pauli strings on …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240402] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A general construction to embed stabilizer states as quantum many-body scars in local Hamiltonians.
motivation: Quantum many-body scars provide a mechanism for weak ergodicity breaking, and embedding stabilizer states as scars could enable controlled non-thermal behavior.
method: The construction uses factorizability of Pauli strings to design parent Hamiltonians whose eigenstates include stabilizer states as scars.
result: Stabilizer states can be realized as exact eigenstates (scars) of local Hamiltonians, with the method generalizing to any stabilizer state.
conclusion: This work provides a systematic way to embed known quantum states as scars, potentially useful for quantum information tasks like state preparation and memory.

title: Retrocausal Capacity Of A Quantum Channel: Communicating Through Noisy Closed Timelike Curves
authors: Kaiyuan Ji, Seth Lloyd, And Mark M. Wilde
abstract:
Author(s): Kaiyuan Ji, Seth Lloyd, and Mark M. Wilde

We study the capacity of a quantum channel for retrocausal communication, where messages are transmitted backward in time, from a sender in the future to a receiver in the past, through a noisy postselected closed timelike curve mathematically represented by the channel. We completely characterize t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230801] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper characterizes the retrocausal capacity of a quantum channel for communication through noisy closed timelike curves.
motivation: Understanding the fundamental limits of quantum communication in exotic spacetime scenarios, such as closed timelike curves, which may provide insights into the nature of quantum information and causality.
method: The authors model the noisy postselected closed timelike curve as a quantum channel and derive its retrocausal capacity using information-theoretic techniques.
result: They completely characterize the retrocausal capacity, showing it is given by a formula involving the channel's entanglement-assisted capacity and other quantum information measures.
conclusion: The work establishes a rigorous framework for retrocausal quantum communication and reveals connections between quantum information theory and spacetime structure.

title: Application And Quantum Properties Of Superpositions Of Oppositely Squeezed States
authors: Hiroo Azuma, William J. Munro, And Kae Nemoto
abstract:
Author(s): Hiroo Azuma, William J. Munro, and Kae Nemoto

We show that superpositions of oppositely squeezed states—non-Gaussian Schrödinger-cat-like states—exhibit enhanced nonclassical features and provide an entanglement advantage in the small-squeezing regime. These states possess photon-number structures distinct from conventional coherent-state cat s…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063728] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Superpositions of oppositely squeezed states are shown to have enhanced nonclassical features and entanglement advantage in the small-squeezing regime.
motivation: To explore non-Gaussian states that exhibit stronger quantum properties than conventional cat states, potentially useful for quantum information processing.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the photon-number statistics, Wigner functions, and entanglement properties of superpositions of oppositely squeezed states.
result: These states display distinct nonclassical features and provide an entanglement advantage in the small-squeezing regime compared to standard coherent-state cat states.
conclusion: Superpositions of oppositely squeezed states are promising non-Gaussian resources for quantum information tasks requiring entanglement and nonclassicality.

title: Optimal Control Of Open-quantum-system Dynamics Predicted By Long Short-term Memory
authors: Jun-Dong Zhong And Zhao-Ming Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Jun-Dong Zhong and Zhao-Ming Wang

The realization of high-fidelity quantum control is crucial for quantum information processing, particularly in noisy environments where control strategies must simultaneously achieve precise manipulation and effective noise suppression. Conventional optimal control designs typically require numeric…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062442] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Uses long short-term memory (LSTM) networks to predict optimal control pulses for open quantum systems, achieving high-fidelity control in noisy environments.
motivation: Conventional optimal control for open quantum systems is computationally expensive; machine learning offers a faster alternative.
method: Trains an LSTM network on optimal control solutions from gradient-based methods to predict control pulses for new initial states and noise parameters.
result: The LSTM predicts control pulses with fidelities comparable to numerically optimized ones, with orders of magnitude speedup.
conclusion: Machine learning can efficiently generate high-fidelity quantum control for open systems, aiding practical quantum information processing.

title: Increasing Entanglement Concentration And The Role Of Measurement Imaginarity
authors: Indranil Biswas, Subrata Bera, Ujjwal Sen, Indrani Chattopadhyay, And Debasis Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Indranil Biswas, Subrata Bera, Ujjwal Sen, Indrani Chattopadhyay, and Debasis Sarkar

The role of complex numbers in quantum theory extends beyond mathematical convenience, having recently been formalized as a resource under the framework of the resource theory of imaginarity. Operationally, imaginarity translates into using more resources in linear optical setups. In this work, we i…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062439] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates how the imaginarity of measurements affects entanglement concentration, showing that using complex measurements can increase the success probability of extracting maximally entangled states.
motivation: Entanglement concentration is a key task in quantum information processing, and understanding the role of complex numbers (imaginarity) as a resource can lead to more efficient protocols.
method: The authors analyze the entanglement concentration protocol using measurements with varying degrees of imaginarity, deriving bounds and success probabilities based on the resource theory of imaginarity.
result: They find that increasing the imaginarity of measurements can enhance the success probability of entanglement concentration, and they characterize the trade-off between imaginarity and entanglement yield.
conclusion: Imaginarity is a useful resource for entanglement concentration, and the results provide a deeper understanding of the operational significance of complex numbers in quantum information.

title: Demonstration Of The Universal Intrinsic Higher-rank Spin Tensor Hall Effect With A Trapped Ion
authors: Chang Liu, Yue Li, Xingyu Zhao, Xi-Wang Luo, And Yiheng Lin
abstract:
Author(s): Chang Liu, Yue Li, Xingyu Zhao, Xi-Wang Luo, and Yiheng Lin

The spin Hall effect enables pure spin-current generation without charge transport. Notably, its intrinsic contribution, originating from spin-orbit coupling, can exhibit universal values that are robust against parameter fluctuations. Recent extensions of this effect to high-spin systems predict ri…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062616] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of a universal intrinsic higher-rank spin tensor Hall effect using a trapped ion system.
motivation: To realize and characterize higher-rank spin tensor Hall effects in a controlled quantum platform, extending the spin Hall effect to high-spin systems.
method: Trapped ion quantum simulation with engineered spin-orbit coupling to observe the intrinsic spin tensor Hall effect.
result: Observation of universal higher-rank spin tensor Hall effect robust against parameter fluctuations.
conclusion: Trapped ions provide a versatile platform for studying higher-rank spin transport phenomena, with potential applications in spintronics and quantum information.

title: Tunable Bundle Emissions Of $n$-phonon And Photon-phonon Pairs Via The Barnett Effect
authors: Zhe-Qi Yang, Lei Chen, And Zhi-Rong Zhong
abstract:
Author(s): Zhe-Qi Yang, Lei Chen, and Zhi-Rong Zhong

We theoretically propose a scheme for the generation of [MATH]-phonon and photon-phonon pair bundle emissions in a cavity magnomechanics system. By utilizing the Barnett effect under resonant driving, [MATH]-phonon and photon-phonon super Rabi oscillations can be achieved. Through the system's dissipative…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063722] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a cavity magnomechanics scheme to generate n-phonon and photon-phonon pair bundle emissions via the Barnett effect.
motivation: To achieve controllable multi-phonon and hybrid photon-phonon quantum states for quantum information processing.
method: Uses a cavity magnomechanical system with resonant driving and the Barnett effect to induce super Rabi oscillations, then leverages dissipative dynamics to produce bundle emissions.
result: Demonstrates tunable generation of n-phonon bundles and photon-phonon pairs with controlled statistics.
conclusion: The scheme provides a new method for generating nonclassical states in hybrid quantum systems, relevant for quantum networks and sensing.

title: Entanglement Dynamics Of Separable Squeezed States In Finite-memory Structured Reservoir
authors: Austen Couvertier And Ting Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Austen Couvertier and Ting Yu

Entanglement in continuous-variable Gaussian systems is a key resource, and common reservoirs can both suppress and generate correlations. Existing work focused on preentangled states or Markovian baths, leaving open whether separable squeezed inputs entangle in structured environments or under modu…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063724] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies entanglement generation from separable squeezed states in a finite-memory structured reservoir, extending previous work on Markovian baths.
motivation: Understanding how structured environments can generate entanglement from initially separable states is important for continuous-variable quantum information processing.
method: The authors analyze the dynamics of two squeezed states coupled to a common non-Markovian reservoir with finite memory, using exact analytical methods.
result: They find that entanglement can be generated and controlled by tuning the squeezing parameters and reservoir memory, with non-Markovian effects enhancing entanglement.
conclusion: Structured reservoirs can serve as a resource for entanglement generation from separable squeezed inputs, offering new possibilities for quantum information tasks.

title: Beyond Qubits: Multilevel Quantum Sensing For Dark Matter
authors: Xiaolin Ma, Volodymyr Takhistov, Norikazu Mizuochi, And Ernst David Herbschleb
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaolin Ma, Volodymyr Takhistov, Norikazu Mizuochi, and Ernst David Herbschleb

Searching for ultralight dark matter requires detecting extremely weak oscillating fields, where quantum sensing is especially promising. The authors show that spin-1 nitrogen vacancy centers in diamond can harness multilevel quantum states to combine enhanced signal response with common mode noise suppression, improving sensitivity to axion-electron dark matter interactions.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060802] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: NV centers in diamond with multilevel quantum states enhance sensitivity for detecting ultralight dark matter.
motivation: Ultralight dark matter detection requires extremely sensitive quantum sensors; NV centers offer a promising platform.
method: The authors propose using spin-1 NV centers with multilevel quantum states to combine enhanced signal response with common-mode noise suppression.
result: The multilevel approach improves sensitivity to axion-electron dark matter interactions compared to conventional qubit-based sensing.
conclusion: Multilevel quantum sensing with NV centers is a viable and improved method for dark matter detection.

title: Coherent Perfect Absorption Of Anti-modes In An Indirect Coupled Magnon-polariton System
authors: Chenyang Lu, Jiguang Yao, Jiongjie Wang, Jiang Xiao, And Can-Ming Hu
abstract:
Author(s): Chenyang Lu, Jiguang Yao, Jiongjie Wang, Jiang Xiao, and Can-Ming Hu

In this work, we report coherent perfect absorption (CPA) of anti-modes in an indirectly coupled magnon–polariton system. By examining both single and indirectly coupled cases, we experimentally distinguish the modal decay rate [MATH] from the effective decay rate [MATH]. At CPA, ${γ}_{\m…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224431] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of coherent perfect absorption of anti-modes in an indirectly coupled magnon-polariton system.
motivation: To understand and control absorption in hybrid magnon-polariton systems, which are relevant for quantum information processing and transduction.
method: Experimental setup with a cavity magnon-polariton system where two magnon modes are indirectly coupled via a cavity photon mode; measurement of modal and effective decay rates.
result: Distinguished modal decay rate from effective decay rate and observed coherent perfect absorption of anti-modes.
conclusion: The work provides insight into decay dynamics in coupled magnon-polariton systems and may enable applications in quantum memory and signal processing.

title: Absorbing State Dynamics Of Stochastic Gradient Descent
authors: Guanming Zhang And Stefano Martiniani
abstract:
Author(s): Guanming Zhang and Stefano Martiniani

Stochastic gradient descent (SGD) is a fundamental tool in stochastic optimization that is widely used in machine learning. Here, we study SGD through the lens of particle dynamics, introducing a framework that links its behavior to well-established models in nonequilibrium statistical physics. We i…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062103] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper models stochastic gradient descent as a nonequilibrium absorbing state phase transition, linking machine learning optimization to statistical physics.
motivation: Understanding the dynamics of SGD is crucial for improving optimization in machine learning, and the absorbing state framework provides a new theoretical perspective.
method: The authors map SGD to a particle system with an absorbing state and analyze its critical behavior using scaling arguments and numerical simulations.
result: They identify a continuous phase transition between absorbing and active phases, with critical exponents consistent with directed percolation universality.
conclusion: SGD dynamics can be understood as a nonequilibrium phase transition, offering insights into convergence and generalization.

title: Making non-Markovian Master Equations Accessible With Approximate Environments
authors: Gerardo Suárez And Michał Horodecki
abstract:
Author(s): Gerardo Suárez and Michał Horodecki

Accurate and efficient simulation of open quantum systems remains a significant challenge, particularly for non-Markovian dynamics. We demonstrate the profound utility of expressing the environmental correlation function as a sum of damped sinusoidals within master equations. While not strictly requ…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064121] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to make non-Markovian master equations more tractable by approximating the environment correlation function as a sum of damped sinusoidals.
motivation: Simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems is computationally challenging; the authors aim to provide a practical approximation that retains essential physics while reducing complexity.
method: The authors express the environmental correlation function as a sum of damped sinusoidals, which allows them to derive a master equation that is easier to solve numerically.
result: They demonstrate that this approximation accurately captures non-Markovian dynamics for a range of parameters, significantly reducing computational cost.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a practical tool for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems, making it more accessible for applications in quantum thermodynamics and related fields.

title: Indefinite Causal Order In Cavity Quantum Electrodynamics
authors: Luis Octavio Castaños-Cervantes, Lorenzo M. Procopio, And Tim J. Bartley
abstract:
Author(s): Luis Octavio Castaños-Cervantes, Lorenzo M. Procopio, and Tim J. Bartley

Indefinite causal order (ICO) has the potential to be a new resource for quantum information processing. In most of its experiments, ICO has been investigated in a photonic platform. Here, we investigate ICO in a cavity quantum electrodynamics system composed of two cavities. Our results show that I…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023295] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates indefinite causal order (ICO) in a cavity quantum electrodynamics system, demonstrating its potential as a resource for quantum information processing.
motivation: ICO has been studied mainly in photonic platforms; exploring it in cavity QED could enable new quantum information protocols and test fundamental aspects of quantum mechanics.
method: The authors model two cavities coupled via a quantum switch, analyzing the dynamics and the emergence of ICO through the resulting quantum correlations.
result: They show that ICO can be realized in cavity QED, with the system exhibiting non-classical correlations and potential advantages for quantum communication.
conclusion: Cavity QED provides a viable platform for ICO, opening avenues for quantum information tasks that exploit indefinite causal order.

title: Metabolic Quantum Limit To The Information Capacity Of Magnetoencephalography
authors: E. Gkoudinakis, S. Li, And I. K. Kominis
abstract:
Author(s): E. Gkoudinakis, S. Li, and I. K. Kominis

Magnetoencephalography (MEG) measures the magnetic fields generated by neural currents using quantum sensors such as superconducting quantum interference devices and atomic magnetometers. Here, we combine the energy resolution limit of magnetic sensing with the metabolic power available to neural cu…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023267] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Combines the energy resolution limit of magnetic sensing with metabolic power to derive a quantum limit on the information capacity of magnetoencephalography.
motivation: To understand the fundamental physical limits on the information that can be extracted from neural activity via MEG, constrained by both quantum sensing and biological energy budgets.
method: Applies the energy resolution limit from quantum metrology and the metabolic power available to neural currents to derive an upper bound on the information capacity of MEG.
result: Derives a metabolic quantum limit that sets a fundamental bound on the information capacity of MEG, linking quantum sensing limits to biological constraints.
conclusion: The work establishes a new type of quantum limit in neuroscience, showing that metabolic power and quantum sensing resolution together constrain the information obtainable from brain activity.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing and simulation, but loading and imaging them with high fidelity and low loss remains challenging. This work aims to overcome these challenges using EIT.
method: The authors employ electromagnetically induced transparency to enable nondestructive imaging and continuous loading of atom arrays. They use a finite magnetic field to create a lambda system and achieve high-contrast imaging with minimal atom loss.
result: They achieve high-fidelity imaging and loading of atom arrays, demonstrating the effectiveness of EIT for this purpose. The method allows for continuous operation and high survival rates of atoms during imaging.
conclusion: EIT-based imaging and loading is a powerful technique for neutral-atom arrays, enabling high-fidelity operations essential for quantum information processing and simulation.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, enabling near-optimal quantum simulation of linear differential equations.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity constraints and the need for efficient dilation methods.
method: The paper introduces a dilation approach that uses a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice to encode the nonunitary evolution, leveraging moment-matching techniques to achieve near-optimal query complexity.
result: The framework provides a systematic way to construct unitary dilations with minimal ancillary qubits and circuit depth, achieving near-optimal scaling for simulating linear differential equations.
conclusion: This work advances quantum simulation of nonunitary processes, with potential applications in open quantum systems and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise correlations in qubit platforms is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle in the intermediate-frequency regime.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot readout data to extract noise cross-correlations, enabling measurement in previously inaccessible frequency ranges.
result: The method successfully extracts noise cross-correlations, demonstrating its effectiveness in bridging the intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.
conclusion: This technique provides a new tool for noise spectroscopy in quantum devices, aiding in the understanding and mitigation of decoherence sources.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and high-rate codes reduces logical overhead for quantum simulation.
motivation: To enable megaquop-scale quantum simulation on neutral-atom platforms by reducing the space and time overhead of fault-tolerant quantum error correction.
method: Proposes a transversal architecture combining small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate quantum codes, optimized for neutral-atom hardware constraints.
result: Significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation are demonstrated.
conclusion: The architecture makes large-scale quantum simulation feasible on neutral-atom hardware with practical resource requirements.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes a theoretical link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in parametrized quantum circuits, providing estimates of loss function concentration to mitigate barren plateaus.
