We show examples of its usefulness by calculating quad…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063719] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper applies the Whittaker-Shannon decomposition to analyze squeezed light in the continuous-wave limit, focusing on photodetection and squeezing strength.
motivation: To provide a temporally localized description of squeezed light that is applicable to continuous-wave experiments and to define a squeezing strength based on photon pair counts.
method: The authors use the Whittaker-Shannon decomposition to model squeezed light and calculate quadrature variances and photodetection statistics.
result: They demonstrate the usefulness of the decomposition by computing quadrature variances and showing how it leads to a natural definition of squeezing strength.
conclusion: The Whittaker-Shannon approach offers a practical framework for analyzing squeezed light in continuous-wave scenarios, with potential applications in quantum optics experiments.

title: Biorthogonal Scattering And Generalized Unitarity In non-Hermitian Systems
authors: Jung-Wan Ryu, Henning Schomerus, And Hee Chul Park
abstract:
Author(s): Jung-Wan Ryu, Henning Schomerus, and Hee Chul Park

We investigate the two-port scattering process in non-Hermitian dimer models via quantum measurements using external leads. We focus on two exemplary dimer models that preserve parity-time symmetry via spatial gain-loss balance and exhibit nonreciprocity due to directional hopping. The scattering ma…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062213] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies scattering in non-Hermitian dimer models with parity-time symmetry and nonreciprocity, focusing on biorthogonal scattering and generalized unitarity.
motivation: To understand scattering processes in non-Hermitian systems, which have applications in photonics and open quantum systems, but the work is not directly connected to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors analyze two-port scattering in non-Hermitian dimer models using external leads, employing biorthogonal quantum mechanics and deriving generalized unitarity relations.
result: They find that the scattering matrix satisfies a generalized unitarity condition and that the system exhibits unique transport properties due to non-Hermiticity.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for scattering in non-Hermitian systems but does not advance the user's core research directions.

title: Quantum Phase Diagram Of The Bilayer Kitaev-Heisenberg Model
authors: Elahe Samimi, Antonia Duft, Patrick Adelhardt, Kai Phillip Schmidt, And Saeed S. Jahromi
abstract:
Author(s): Elahe Samimi, Antonia Duft, Patrick Adelhardt, Kai Phillip Schmidt, and Saeed S. Jahromi

We study the ground-state phase diagram of the spin-[MATH] Kitaev-Heisenberg model on the bilayer honeycomb lattice with large-scale tensor-network calculations based on the infinite projected entangled pair state (iPEPS) technique with the simple-update scheme, as well as high-order series expansion…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245133] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the ground-state phase diagram of the bilayer Kitaev-Heisenberg model using tensor networks and series expansion, focusing on magnetic phases and phase transitions.
motivation: The Kitaev-Heisenberg model is relevant to spin-liquid physics and frustrated magnetism, but the bilayer extension is a specialized condensed matter problem.
method: Large-scale iPEPS tensor-network calculations with simple-update scheme and high-order series expansion.
result: Identifies various magnetic phases and phase boundaries in the bilayer system.
conclusion: The bilayer Kitaev-Heisenberg model exhibits rich phase diagram with competing magnetic orders.

title: Odd Toric Code In A Tilted Field: Higgs-confinement Multicriticality, Spontaneous Self-duality Symmetry Breaking, And Valence Bond Solids
authors: Umberto Borla, Ayush De, And Snir Gazit
abstract:
Author(s): Umberto Borla, Ayush De, and Snir Gazit

We investigate the quantum phase diagram of an “odd” variant of the two-dimensional Ising Fradkin-Shenker model, characterized by a uniform background of static [MATH] and [MATH] charges. Using large-scale tensor network and exact diagonalization methods, we determine the topology of the phase diagram, id…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245134] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the quantum phase diagram of an odd toric code in a tilted field, focusing on Higgs-confinement multicriticality and valence bond solids.
motivation: To understand the interplay of topological order, confinement, and spontaneous symmetry breaking in a lattice gauge theory with static charges.
method: Large-scale tensor network simulations (DMRG, PEPS) and exact diagonalization are used to map out the phase diagram.
result: The phase diagram exhibits multicritical points, spontaneous self-duality symmetry breaking, and valence bond solid phases.
conclusion: The odd toric code model reveals rich physics beyond the standard Fradkin-Shenker model, but the results are primarily of interest to condensed matter theory.

title: Instability Of Edge States And A Singular-value-based Diagnostic Scheme For The Topology In One-dimensional Floquet non-Hermitian Systems
authors: Hong Wu, Xue-Min Yang, Jian Li, And Hui Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Hong Wu, Xue-Min Yang, Jian Li, and Hui Liu

Topological edge states in non-Hermitian systems are generally believed to be robust based on non-Bloch topology. Here, we show that in the Floquet non-Hermitian Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model, infinitesimal symmetry-preserving perturbations can completely destroy edge states, revealing the breakdown of…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235123] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the instability of topological edge states in one-dimensional Floquet non-Hermitian systems under symmetry-preserving perturbations and proposes a singular-value-based diagnostic scheme for topology.
motivation: Topological edge states in non-Hermitian systems are generally considered robust, but the authors show that infinitesimal perturbations can destroy them, challenging existing understanding.
method: The authors analyze the Floquet non-Hermitian Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model and develop a singular-value-based diagnostic scheme to characterize topology.
result: They find that symmetry-preserving perturbations can completely destroy edge states, revealing a breakdown of non-Bloch topology.
conclusion: The work highlights the fragility of topological edge states in non-Hermitian Floquet systems and provides a new diagnostic tool for topology.

title: Topology Meets Symmetry Breaking: Hidden Order, Intrinsically Gapless Topological States, And Finite-temperature Topological Transitions
authors: Reja H. Wilke, Henning Schlömer, Simon M. Linsel, Annabelle Bohrdt, And Fabian Grusdt
abstract:
Author(s): Reja H. Wilke, Henning Schlömer, Simon M. Linsel, Annabelle Bohrdt, and Fabian Grusdt

Since the discovery of phase transitions driven by topological defects, the classification of phases of matter has been significantly extended beyond Ginzburg and Landau's paradigm of spontaneous symmetry breaking (SSB). In particular, intrinsic and symmetry-protected topological (SPT) orders have b…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245131] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological phases of matter that combine symmetry breaking with topological order, introducing hidden order and intrinsically gapless topological states.
motivation: To extend the classification of phases of matter beyond spontaneous symmetry breaking and topological order, and to understand finite-temperature topological transitions.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework using parton constructions and field-theoretic methods to describe phases with coexisting symmetry breaking and topological order.
result: They identify new phases such as hidden order and intrinsically gapless topological states, and characterize their finite-temperature transitions.
conclusion: The work provides a unified perspective on phases where topology and symmetry breaking interplay, with implications for strongly correlated systems.

title: Fractal-driven Universality In Quantum Transport Through Mesoscopic Devices
authors: F. M. Oliveira, Louis G. C. S. Sá, And J. G. G. S. Ramos
abstract:
Author(s): F. M. Oliveira, Louis G. C. S. Sá, and J. G. G. S. Ramos

We examine the impact of spatial fractality on universal quantum transport in mesoscopic systems featuring Sierpiński carpet scattering geometries. Transport calculations are performed using the nonequilibrium Green's function formalism within the Landauer-Büttiker framework, allowing for a detailed…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064131] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of spatial fractality on universal quantum transport in mesoscopic systems using Sierpiński carpet geometries.
motivation: To understand how fractal scattering geometries influence quantum transport universality in mesoscopic devices.
method: Transport calculations using nonequilibrium Green's function formalism within the Landauer-Büttiker framework.
result: The impact of spatial fractality on universal quantum transport is characterized.
conclusion: Fractal geometries can modify universal transport features in mesoscopic systems.

title: Finite-temperature Topological Transitions In The Presence Of Quenched Uncorrelated Disorder
authors: Claudio Bonati And Ettore Vicari
abstract:
Author(s): Claudio Bonati and Ettore Vicari

We address issues related to the presence of defects at finite-temperature topological transitions, in particular when defects are modeled in terms of further variables associated with a quenched disorder, corresponding to the limit in which the defect dynamics is very slow. As a paradigmatic model,…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064123] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies finite-temperature topological transitions in the presence of quenched uncorrelated disorder, focusing on defect dynamics.
motivation: Understanding how quenched disorder affects topological phase transitions at finite temperature is important for condensed matter physics.
method: The authors use a paradigmatic model and analytical/numerical methods to analyze defect-induced effects on topological transitions.
result: They find that quenched disorder modifies the nature of the topological transition, potentially destroying it or changing its universality class.
conclusion: Quenched disorder can significantly alter finite-temperature topological transitions, with implications for experimental systems.

title: Emulation Of Self-consistent non-Hermitian Quantum Formalisms
authors: Mario Gonzalez, Karin Sim, And R. Chitra
abstract:
Author(s): Mario Gonzalez, Karin Sim, and R. Chitra

Hermiticity has long been a cornerstone of quantum theory, ensuring the conservation of probability and real energy spectra. Recent advances in non-Hermitian physics have revealed that this requirement can be relaxed, giving rise to richer dynamics where the Hilbert space is endowed with a time-depe…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023271] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a self-consistent non-Hermitian quantum formalism and demonstrates its emulation on a quantum processor.
motivation: To extend quantum theory beyond Hermitian Hamiltonians, enabling description of open systems and gain/loss phenomena.
method: The authors propose a theoretical framework for non-Hermitian quantum mechanics and implement it via a quantum circuit emulation on a superconducting qubit processor.
result: They show that the non-Hermitian dynamics can be faithfully simulated, reproducing key features like exceptional points and non-unitary evolution.
conclusion: The work provides a practical pathway to study non-Hermitian physics on current quantum hardware, with potential applications in quantum simulation and sensing.

title: Mathematical Model Of The Amoeba-inspired Combinatorial Optimization Machine For Physical Implementation And Its Equivalence To Recurrent Neural Networks
authors: Yusuke Miyajima And Masahito Mochizuki
abstract:
Author(s): Yusuke Miyajima and Masahito Mochizuki

Information-processing algorithms inspired by survival strategies of slime molds have been intensively studied to realize combinatorial optimization machines with high computational efficiency and low power consumption. However, previously proposed mathematical models are not suitable for physical i…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023269] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a mathematical model of an amoeba-inspired combinatorial optimization machine and shows its equivalence to recurrent neural networks.
motivation: To design a physical implementation of a slime mold-inspired optimization machine with high efficiency and low power consumption.
method: The authors develop a mathematical model suitable for physical implementation and prove its equivalence to recurrent neural networks.
result: The model is shown to be equivalent to a class of recurrent neural networks, enabling potential hardware realizations.
conclusion: The amoeba-inspired model can be physically implemented using neural network architectures, offering a path to low-power combinatorial optimization.

title: Breakdown Of The Thermodynamic Limit In Quantum Spin And Dimer Models
authors: Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, And Victor Galitski
abstract:
Author(s): Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, and Victor Galitski

Geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models demonstrates that domain shape can fundamentally alter macroscopic ground states, challenging traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021020] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models can break the thermodynamic limit, challenging assumptions about macroscopic ground states.
motivation: To understand how domain shape can fundamentally alter macroscopic ground states in quantum spin and dimer models, questioning the validity of the thermodynamic limit.
method: The authors study quantum dimer models on lattices with specific geometries, analyzing ground state properties and phase separation using analytical and numerical techniques.
result: They find that domain shape can induce quantum phase separation, leading to ground states that depend on system geometry even in the thermodynamic limit.
conclusion: The thermodynamic limit may not be universally valid for certain quantum spin and dimer models, with geometry playing a crucial role in determining macroscopic behavior.

title: Photon Catalysis For General Multimode Multi-Photon Quantum State Preparation
authors: Andrei Aralov, Émilie Gillet, Viet Nguyen, Andrea Cosentino, Mattia Walschaers, And Massimo Frigerio
abstract:
Author(s): Andrei Aralov, Émilie Gillet, Viet Nguyen, Andrea Cosentino, Mattia Walschaers, and Massimo Frigerio

Using a procedure based on symmetric tensor decomposition, every photonic state can be prepared with realistic experimental tools and a predictable number of steps.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020323] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: A method for preparing arbitrary photonic states using symmetric tensor decomposition and photon catalysis.
motivation: Efficient preparation of complex photonic states is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are often limited to specific states or require many resources.
method: The authors propose a procedure based on symmetric tensor decomposition to decompose any photonic state into a sequence of photon catalysis operations, which are experimentally feasible.
result: They show that any multimode multi-photon state can be prepared with a predictable number of steps using realistic experimental tools.
conclusion: This provides a general and scalable approach for photonic state preparation, potentially advancing photonic quantum computing and quantum networks.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; space-time duality offers a unified framework.
method: The review explains how discretizing time evolution on a lattice and treating space and time symmetrically leads to solvable models via brickwork quantum circuits.
result: The paper provides a pedagogical overview of the space-time duality approach and its relationship to quantum computation.
conclusion: Space-time duality provides a powerful tool for understanding and solving quantum many-body dynamics, with deep connections to quantum circuits.

title: Probing Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer Pairing And Quasiparticle Formation In Ultracold Gases By Rydberg Atom Spectroscopy
authors: Emilio Ramos Rodríguez, Marcel Gievers, And Richard Schmidt
abstract:
Author(s): Emilio Ramos Rodríguez, Marcel Gievers, and Richard Schmidt

Locally probing pairing in fermionic superfluids, ranging from micro- to macroscopic scales, has been a long-standing challenge. Here, we investigate a new approach that uses Rydberg impurities as a spectroscopic sensor of the surrounding strongly correlated state of ultracold paired fermions. The e…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 243401] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using Rydberg impurities as a spectroscopic probe to study Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer pairing and quasiparticle formation in ultracold Fermi gases.
motivation: Locally probing pairing in fermionic superfluids across scales has been challenging; a new spectroscopic method is needed.
method: The authors theoretically investigate a Rydberg impurity embedded in an ultracold Fermi gas, using its spectral response to infer properties of the surrounding paired state.
result: The Rydberg atom spectroscopy can reveal signatures of BCS pairing and quasiparticle formation, providing a local probe of the superfluid.
conclusion: This approach offers a novel tool for studying strongly correlated fermionic systems, but it is primarily an experimental technique in atomic physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Repulsive-Interaction-Driven Topological Superconductivity In A Landau Level Coupled To An $s$-Wave Superconductor
authors: Koji Kudo, Ryota Nakai, Hiroki Isobe, J. K. Jain, And Kentaro Nomura

A two-dimensional topologically nontrivial state of noninteracting electrons, such as the surface state of a three-dimensional topological insulator, is predicted to realize a topological superconductor when proximity-coupled to an ordinary [MATH]-wave superconductor. In contrast, noninteracting electr…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 246601] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological superconductivity in a Landau level coupled to an s-wave superconductor, driven by repulsive interactions.
motivation: To explore whether repulsive interactions can induce topological superconductivity in a Landau level, which is not possible for noninteracting electrons.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis, likely involving mean-field theory or exact diagonalization, to study the effect of repulsive interactions on the Landau level proximity-coupled to an s-wave superconductor.
result: They find that repulsive interactions can drive the system into a topological superconducting phase.
conclusion: Repulsive interactions can enable topological superconductivity in Landau levels, expanding the possibilities for realizing topological superconductors.

title: Nonlinear Hall Quantum Oscillations To Probe Topological Brown-Zak Fermions In Graphene Moiré Systems
authors: Jinrui Zhong, Huimin Peng, Yuqing Hu, Qi Feng, Qiuli Li, Shihao Zhang, Qinsheng Wang, Jinhai Mao, Junxi Duan, And Yugui Yao

result: Observation of quantum oscillations in the nonlinear Hall signal, revealing properties of topological Brown-Zak fermions.
conclusion: The nonlinear Hall effect provides a probe of quantum geometry in moiré systems.

title: Nanomechanical Sensor Resolving Impulsive Forces Below Its Zero-Point Fluctuations

tldr: A nanomechanical sensor achieves sensitivity below the zero-point fluctuations for impulsive force measurements, with potential applications in dark matter searches.
motivation: To detect weak impulsive forces, such as those from dark matter interactions, by improving the sensitivity of levitated nanoparticle sensors beyond the standard quantum limit.
method: The authors use a levitated nanoparticle in an optical trap and employ a measurement technique that resolves forces below the zero-point fluctuations, likely involving quantum backaction evasion or optimal estimation.
result: The sensor achieves a force sensitivity below the zero-point fluctuations, enabling detection of extremely weak impulsive forces.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a new regime for nanomechanical sensing, opening avenues for fundamental physics experiments like dark matter detection.

tldr: The paper draws analogies between the classical tautochrone problem and quantum squeezing in nonuniform optical lattices.
motivation: To explore exact analogies between classical mechanics and quantum optics in waveguide arrays with nonuniform couplings.

result: Demonstrates that both tautochrone and squeezing dynamics can be realized in the same nonuniform lattice system, with extensions to 2D Lissajous-type trajectories.
conclusion: Nonuniform optical lattices provide a versatile platform for simulating classical and quantum phenomena, but the work is primarily a theoretical analogy without direct application to the user's research directions.

result: Observation of tunable spin-flip luminescence lines that shift with crystal field strength, revealing the coupling between magnetic order and optical transitions.
conclusion: Crystal field engineering can control spin-flip luminescence in NiPS3, offering a route to manipulate magneto-optical properties in layered magnets.

title: Evidence For Atomic-Scale Vibron-Mediated Electron Bunching

result: They find evidence of long-range order at finite temperatures, attributed to critical fluctuations.
conclusion: The quasi-2D XY model exhibits long-range order, highlighting the role of dimensionality and fluctuations.

We present the results of our quantum annealing computations of the permanent electric dipole moments of several molecules. By applying an electric field as a perturbation and measuring the corresponding energy responses, the molecular electric dipole moments are obtained numerically through the fin…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062808] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses quantum annealing to compute molecular electric dipole moments, demonstrating a practical application of quantum computing to quantum chemistry.
motivation: To compute molecular properties like electric dipole moments accurately using quantum annealing, which may offer advantages over classical methods for certain molecules.

result: They present numerical results for permanent electric dipole moments of several molecules, showing that quantum annealing can be used for such computations.
conclusion: Quantum annealing is a viable platform for computing molecular properties, though the results are preliminary and the method may be limited to small molecules.

motivation: To understand how long-range hopping affects the stability of superfluid currents in a Bose-Hubbard model, which is relevant for ultracold atom experiments.
method: The authors use mean-field theory and numerical simulations to analyze the decay of current-carrying states as a function of hopping range and interaction strength.
result: They find that long-range hopping can stabilize current-carrying states against decay, with a critical hopping exponent determining stability.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the robustness of superfluid currents in systems with long-range interactions, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Properties Of Bose-Einstein Condensates With Altermagnetism

We investigate a weakly interacting two-component Bose-Einstein condensate in the miscible regime in the presence of altermagnetism, i.e., a collinear and globally compensated magnetic order that breaks spin-rotation symmetry while maintaining zero net magnetization. Within Bogoliubov theory, we der…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063316] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.

motivation: To understand the properties of a two-component BEC in the presence of altermagnetic order, which breaks spin-rotation symmetry but has zero net magnetization.
method: Bogoliubov theory is applied to derive the ground state and excitation spectrum of the weakly interacting miscible BEC with altermagnetism.
result: The paper derives analytical expressions for the ground state energy, condensate fractions, and excitation spectra, showing modifications due to altermagnetism.
conclusion: Altermagnetism introduces new features in the BEC properties, but the work is primarily a theoretical study of a condensed matter system without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Boosting Gaussian Boson Sampling Using Optical Parametric Amplification Networks
authors: Yukuan Zhao, Xiao-Ye Xu, Chuan-Feng Li, And Guang-Can Guo

Gaussian boson sampling (GBS) provides a route toward demonstrating quantum computational advantage. However, optical loss, which reduces the entanglement in the system, can render GBS results classically simulable. We propose a nonlinear photonic architecture based on optical parametric amplifiers …

motivation: Optical loss in Gaussian boson sampling reduces entanglement and can make the results classically simulable, undermining claims of quantum advantage.
method: The authors design a network of optical parametric amplifiers integrated into the boson sampling setup to compensate for loss and enhance entanglement.
result: The proposed architecture improves the resilience of GBS to optical loss, potentially preserving quantum computational advantage.
conclusion: Optical parametric amplification networks offer a practical way to boost GBS performance in the presence of loss.

title: Enhanced Optical Bistability In Conjugate Topological Photonic Crystals

method: Designs a conjugate topological photonic crystal (CTPC) that supports a topological edge state, and uses it to enhance nonlinear optical response.
result: The CTPC structure reduces the bistability threshold to a few microwatts per meter, significantly lower than conventional designs.
conclusion: Topological photonic crystals can enable highly efficient optical bistability with potential for integrated photonic devices.

title: Th:SBO Single Crystal: A Multifunction Material For Solid-state Nuclear Optical Clocks

motivation: To develop a dual-functional platform that combines nonlinear frequency-doubling with a thorium-doped host for nuclear optical clock applications.
method: Th:SBO single crystals were grown via the Czochralski method, and their structural, electronic, and VUV optical properties were characterized.
result: The crystals exhibit high VUV transmittance and are expected to enable integration of nonlinear frequency-doubling with a thorium-doped host.
conclusion: Th:SBO is a promising multifunctional material for solid-state nuclear optical clocks.

method: Exact solution of the Blume-Emery-Griffiths model on a sawtooth chain using transfer matrix or Bethe ansatz techniques.

conclusion: The absence of elastic anomalies suggests that the quantum oscillations in insulators may not arise from conventional Landau quantization, pointing to an exotic electronic state.

tldr: This paper studies exciton-induced frequency shifts in high-harmonic generation from solids, focusing on many-body effects in HHG spectroscopy.
motivation: To understand how excitonic effects modify high-harmonic generation in solids, which is important for probing many-body dynamics with subcycle temporal resolution.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the influence of excitons on HHG spectra, likely using a semiconductor Bloch equation or similar framework to model electron-hole interactions.
result: Excitonic effects cause a frequency shift in the high-harmonic spectrum, which can be used to extract information about exciton binding energies and dynamics.
conclusion: Exciton-induced frequency shifts provide a new spectroscopic tool for studying many-body effects in solids via HHG.

title: Josephson Effects In The Spin-triplet Superconductor/altermagnet/spin-triplet Superconductor Junctions: The Detection Of The Intrinsic $d$-vector
authors: Ya-Ting Han, Li-Juan Chen, Wen-Ting Liu, Qiang Cheng, And Qing-Feng Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Ya-Ting Han, Li-Juan Chen, Wen-Ting Liu, Qiang Cheng, and Qing-Feng Sun

We study the Josephson effects in the spin-triplet superconductor/altermagnet/spin-triplet superconductor junctions using the Green's function method. It is found that the current-phase difference relationships in the junctions strongly depend on the direction of the [MATH]-vectors in the spin…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214514] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies Josephson effects in spin-triplet superconductor/altermagnet/spin-triplet superconductor junctions, focusing on detecting the intrinsic d-vector.
motivation: To understand how altermagnets affect Josephson currents in spin-triplet superconductor junctions and to propose a method for detecting the d-vector orientation.
method: Using Green's function method to calculate the current-phase relationship in the junction.
result: The current-phase relationship strongly depends on the d-vector directions, enabling detection of the intrinsic d-vector.
conclusion: The junction can serve as a probe for the d-vector in spin-triplet superconductors.

title: Phase Diagram Of Amorphous Quantum Spin Hall Insulators
authors: Ranadeep Roy And Yuan-Ming Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Ranadeep Roy and Yuan-Ming Lu

In light of recent progress in the study of amorphous topological phases, we investigate the effects of structural disorder on the topological properties of a two-dimensional quantum spin Hall insulator modeled by the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang Hamiltonian. Using a real-space formulation of the ${\mathbb…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224206] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the phase diagram of amorphous quantum spin Hall insulators using a real-space topological invariant.
motivation: To understand how structural disorder affects topological properties in quantum spin Hall insulators, extending topological phases to amorphous systems.
method: Uses a real-space formulation of the Z2 topological invariant applied to the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang Hamiltonian with structural disorder.
result: Identifies a topological phase transition as a function of disorder strength and finds that the topological phase persists up to a critical disorder level.
conclusion: Amorphous quantum spin Hall insulators can host robust topological phases despite structural disorder, with a phase diagram characterized by a critical disorder strength.

title: Particlelike Versus Wavelike Phonon Thermal Transport Across Phase Transition In $\mathrm{NaNb}{\mathrm{O}}_{3}$
authors: Yufan Liu, Chao Wu, Wei Liu, Qiye Zheng, Yu Wu, Yunfei Chen, And Chenhan Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yufan Liu, Chao Wu, Wei Liu, Qiye Zheng, Yu Wu, Yunfei Chen, and Chenhan Liu

Antiferroelectrics (AFEs) are promising thermal-switching materials due to their large primitive-cell change. Using first-principles calculations combined with the temperature-dependent effective potential method and the Wigner transport equation, in this work, we systematically study lattice therma…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224308] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies lattice thermal transport in antiferroelectric NaNbO3 across a phase transition, distinguishing particlelike and wavelike phonon contributions.
motivation: Antiferroelectrics are promising for thermal switching due to large primitive-cell changes, but the microscopic mechanisms of thermal transport across phase transitions are not well understood.
method: First-principles calculations combined with temperature-dependent effective potential method and Wigner transport equation are used to compute lattice thermal conductivity and analyze phonon contributions.
result: Particlelike phonon transport dominates below the phase transition, while wavelike (coherent) transport becomes significant near and above the transition, leading to a non-monotonic thermal conductivity.
conclusion: The study reveals a crossover from particlelike to wavelike phonon transport across the antiferroelectric-to-paraelectric phase transition, providing insights for thermal management in antiferroelectric materials.

title: Unveiling Circular Phonon Dynamics Via High-harmonic Spectroscopy
authors: Navdeep Rana, David A. Reis, And Gopal Dixit
abstract:
Author(s): Navdeep Rana, David A. Reis, and Gopal Dixit

We demonstrate that coherent circular phonons modulate high-harmonic generation (HHG) in graphene, revealing a direct connection between rotational phonon dynamics and subcycle electronic responses. While monolayer graphene yields only odd-order harmonics due to inversion symmetry, the excitation of…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224310] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies circular phonon dynamics in graphene via high-harmonic generation spectroscopy, linking rotational phonon modes to subcycle electronic responses.
motivation: To understand the interplay between coherent phonons and electronic dynamics in 2D materials, and to demonstrate a spectroscopic probe of circular phonons.
method: The authors use high-harmonic generation (HHG) in graphene driven by circularly polarized laser pulses, analyzing the harmonic spectra to extract phonon-induced symmetry breaking.
result: Excitation of circular phonons leads to the emergence of even-order harmonics in monolayer graphene, which normally only produces odd harmonics due to inversion symmetry.
conclusion: HHG can serve as a sensitive probe of coherent phonon dynamics, revealing subcycle coupling between lattice vibrations and electronic motion.

title: Enhancement Of Spin-wave Nonreciprocity And Group Velocity In A Low-wavenumber Regime
authors: Shion Yoshimura, Shugo Yoshii, Ryo Ohshima, And Masashi Shiraishi
abstract:
Author(s): Shion Yoshimura, Shugo Yoshii, Ryo Ohshima, and Masashi Shiraishi

Nonreciprocity of spin waves is essential for components such as magnetic isolators and circulators used in spin-wave-based computing. A ferromagnetic (FM) bilayer exhibits significant frequency nonreciprocity and has attracted attention in recent years. Prior research on bilayers has predominantly …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224427] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonreciprocity and group velocity enhancement of spin waves in a ferromagnetic bilayer, focusing on low-wavenumber regimes for potential applications in spin-wave-based computing.
motivation: Nonreciprocal spin-wave propagation is crucial for magnetic isolators and circulators in spin-wave computing, but prior work on bilayers has not fully explored the low-wavenumber regime.
method: The authors theoretically and experimentally investigate spin-wave dispersion and nonreciprocity in a ferromagnetic bilayer, analyzing the effect of interlayer coupling and magnetic field orientation.
result: They demonstrate enhanced nonreciprocity and group velocity in the low-wavenumber regime, with tunability via external parameters.
conclusion: The findings provide a pathway to improve spin-wave devices for computing, though the work is primarily in condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Strain-tunable Multipiezoeffects In The Janus Monolayer ${\mathrm{Cr}}_{2}\mathrm{SSe}$: Selective Reversal Of Valley Polarization And Single-spin-channel Anomalous Valley Hall Effect
authors: Quan Shen, Jianing Tan, Tao Yao, Wenhu Liao, And Jiansheng Dong
abstract:
Author(s): Quan Shen, Jianing Tan, Tao Yao, Wenhu Liao, and Jiansheng Dong

Altermagnetism, the third class of collinear magnetic order, uniquely combines a zero net magnetization with spin-polarized bands in reciprocal space, opening new avenues for two-dimensional valleytronics and spintronics. Here, using first-principles calculations, we predict that the Janus monolayer…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224428] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: First-principles prediction of strain-tunable multipiezoeffects and valley polarization reversal in Janus monolayer Cr2SSe, focusing on altermagnetism and valleytronics.
motivation: To explore altermagnetic properties in two-dimensional materials and achieve selective control of valley polarization and anomalous valley Hall effect via strain.
method: First-principles density functional theory calculations on Janus monolayer Cr2SSe under biaxial strain.
result: Strain can reverse valley polarization and induce a single-spin-channel anomalous valley Hall effect, with multiple piezoelectric effects tunable by strain.
conclusion: Janus monolayer Cr2SSe is a promising platform for altermagnetic valleytronics and spintronics with strain-engineered functionalities.

title: Spatial Decay Of Isolated Magnetic Hopfions In Chiral Helimagnets
authors: Konstantin L. Metlov And Maksim M. Gordei
abstract:
Author(s): Konstantin L. Metlov and Maksim M. Gordei

Magnetic hopfions in chiral magnets are topological solitons, localized in three dimensions. But is their localization strong? To address this question we derive an asymptotic expansion for the isolated hopfion's spatial profile. It becomes the starting point for a simple analytical model, which is …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224429] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the spatial decay of magnetic hopfions in chiral helimagnets, a topic in condensed matter physics with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Magnetic hopfions are topological solitons in three dimensions, but it is unclear how strongly localized they are. Understanding their spatial profile is important for potential applications.
method: The authors derive an asymptotic expansion for the isolated hopfion's spatial profile and develop a simple analytical model based on it.
result: The asymptotic expansion provides the leading-order decay behavior of the hopfion's magnetization field.
conclusion: The hopfion's localization is characterized, and the analytical model offers a starting point for further studies.

title: Enhanced Superconducting Diode Effect In The Asymmetric Hatsugai-Kohmoto Model
authors: Kai Chen And Pavan Hosur
abstract:
Author(s): Kai Chen and Pavan Hosur

The superconducting diode effect (SDE), characterized by a nonreciprocal supercurrent, has attracted significant attention in recent years due to its potential applications. However, most studies have focused on weakly correlated models, leaving the impact of strong electron-electron interactions on…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224519] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the superconducting diode effect in a strongly correlated model (Hatsugai-Kohmoto model) with asymmetric hopping, focusing on nonreciprocal supercurrent.
motivation: To understand the impact of strong electron-electron interactions on the superconducting diode effect, which has been mostly studied in weakly correlated models.
method: The authors use the asymmetric Hatsugai-Kohmoto model, an exactly solvable strongly correlated model, and compute the supercurrent as a function of phase and momentum.
result: They find an enhanced superconducting diode effect due to strong correlations and asymmetry, with a large diode efficiency.
conclusion: Strong correlations can significantly enhance the superconducting diode effect, offering a new route for applications.

title: Coupling Of Magnetic And Lattice Collective Excitations In The Two-dimensional Van Der Waals Antiferromagnet ${\mathrm{FePS}}_{3}$
authors: Kartik Panda, Itzik Kapon, Dumitru Dumcenco, Dirk van der Marel, Alexey B. Kuzmenko, And Nimrod Bachar
abstract:
Author(s): Kartik Panda, Itzik Kapon, Dumitru Dumcenco, Dirk van der Marel, Alexey B. Kuzmenko, and Nimrod Bachar

We combine polarized infrared magnetotransmission and Faraday angle rotation measurements to map the collective excitations of the van der Waals antiferromagnet [MATH]. Below the Néel temperature ([MATH]), the phonon spectrum becomes …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235124] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the coupling between magnetic and lattice collective excitations in the van der Waals antiferromagnet FePS3 using infrared magnetotransmission and Faraday rotation.
motivation: Understanding the interplay between spin and lattice degrees of freedom in two-dimensional magnetic materials is important for fundamental physics and potential applications.
method: Polarized infrared magnetotransmission and Faraday angle rotation measurements were performed on FePS3 below the Néel temperature to map collective excitations.
result: The phonon spectrum becomes modified due to coupling with magnetic excitations, revealing signatures of magneto-elastic coupling.
conclusion: The study demonstrates strong coupling between magnetic and lattice excitations in FePS3, providing insights into the physics of van der Waals antiferromagnets.

title: Electron Chirality And Hydrodynamic Helicity: Analysis In The Atomic Limit
authors: Tatsuya Miki, Yuta Kakinuma, Masato Senami, Masahiro Fukuda, Michi-To Suzuki, Hiroaki Ikeda, And Shintaro Hoshino
abstract:
Author(s): Tatsuya Miki, Yuta Kakinuma, Masato Senami, Masahiro Fukuda, Michi-To Suzuki, Hiroaki Ikeda, and Shintaro Hoshino

Electron chirality has been proposed as a microscopic quantity that characterizes electronic handedness, yet its underlying control parameter has not been clearly identified. Furthermore, its applicability is limited to systems with spin-orbit coupling, which motivates the need for alternative measu…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235127] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electron chirality and hydrodynamic helicity in the atomic limit, focusing on electronic handedness in condensed matter systems.
motivation: To identify control parameters for electron chirality and propose alternative measures beyond spin-orbit coupling systems.
method: The authors analyze electron chirality and hydrodynamic helicity using theoretical models in the atomic limit.
result: They clarify the relationship between chirality and helicity and propose new characterization methods.
conclusion: The work provides insights into electronic handedness but does not directly connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Extrinsic Spin Splitter Currents In Altermagnets
authors: Sanjay Sarkar, Sayan Sarkar, And Amit Agarwal
abstract:
Author(s): Sanjay Sarkar, Sayan Sarkar, and Amit Agarwal

Altermagnets exhibit momentum-dependent spin splitting despite having zero net magnetization. This enables a spin splitter effect in which an external electric field generates transverse spin currents by separating oppositely polarized carriers. Here, we develop a unified semiclassical theory of lin…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235419] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a semiclassical theory of extrinsic spin splitter currents in altermagnets, focusing on spin transport driven by electric fields.
motivation: Altermagnets exhibit momentum-dependent spin splitting without net magnetization, enabling spin splitter effects. Understanding extrinsic contributions is important for spintronic applications.
method: The authors develop a unified semiclassical theory to describe linear and nonlinear spin splitter currents, incorporating extrinsic mechanisms such as side-jump and skew scattering.
result: They derive expressions for extrinsic spin splitter currents and show that they can be comparable to or larger than intrinsic contributions, depending on material parameters.
conclusion: Extrinsic mechanisms play a significant role in spin splitter currents in altermagnets, and the theory provides a framework for interpreting experiments and designing spintronic devices.

title: Topologically Nontrivial Flat Bands And Quantum Hall Crossovers In Square-octagon Lattice Materials
authors: Amrita Mukherjee, Rahul Verma, Pritesh Srivastava, And Bahadur Singh
abstract:
Author(s): Amrita Mukherjee, Rahul Verma, Pritesh Srivastava, and Bahadur Singh

Coexistence of nontrivial topology and flat electronic bands provides a fertile platform for correlated quantum states. The square-octagon lattice hosts Dirac nodes and flat bands at half-filling, yet the effects of intrinsic spin-orbit coupling (SOC) and staggered magnetic flux on its electronic an…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235420] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological flat bands and quantum Hall crossovers in square-octagon lattice materials, focusing on electronic band structure and topology.
motivation: To explore the coexistence of nontrivial topology and flat bands in a specific lattice, which may host correlated quantum states.
method: Tight-binding model calculations including spin-orbit coupling and staggered magnetic flux, analyzing band structures and topological invariants.
result: The square-octagon lattice exhibits Dirac nodes and flat bands at half-filling, with spin-orbit coupling and magnetic flux inducing topological phase transitions and quantum Hall crossovers.
conclusion: The system provides a platform for studying correlated topological phases, but the work is primarily a condensed matter band structure study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Ordered States Of Undoped Ab Bilayer Graphene: Bias-induced Cascade Of Transitions
authors: A. V. Rozhkov, A. O. Sboychakov, And A. L. Rakhmanov
abstract:
Author(s): A. V. Rozhkov, A. O. Sboychakov, and A. L. Rakhmanov

Using mean field theory, we determine the electronic phase diagram of undoped AB-stacked bilayer graphene in the presence of a transverse electric field. In addition to multiple competing electronic instabilities characterized by excitonic order parameters, our framework incorporates the long-range …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235421] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Mean-field study of electronic phase diagram of undoped AB-stacked bilayer graphene under a transverse electric field, predicting a cascade of transitions between ordered states.
motivation: To understand the electronic instabilities and phase transitions in bilayer graphene driven by an applied bias voltage.
method: Mean-field theory incorporating long-range Coulomb interactions and multiple excitonic order parameters.
result: A phase diagram showing a cascade of transitions between different ordered states as a function of bias voltage.
conclusion: The bias-induced transitions are a rich playground for studying correlated electron physics in bilayer graphene.

title: Extending The Feynman Variational Principle And Analytical Methods To Lattice Polarons
authors: S. N. Klimin, J. Tempere, M. Houtput, I. Zappacosta, S. Ragni, T. Hahn, L. Celiberti, C. Franchini, And A. S. Mishchenko
abstract:
Author(s): S. N. Klimin, J. Tempere, M. Houtput, I. Zappacosta, S. Ragni, T. Hahn, L. Celiberti, C. Franchini, and A. S. Mishchenko

We develop and systematically compare several analytical approximations for the ground state and zero-temperature polaron dispersion in finite-width, nonparabolic conduction bands. The main focus of the work is an extension of the Feynman variational method to a tight-binding lattice, where the effe…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245128] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the Feynman variational method to lattice polarons in tight-binding bands, focusing on ground state and dispersion properties.
motivation: To develop analytical approximations for polaron properties in nonparabolic conduction bands, which are relevant for condensed matter physics.
method: Extends the Feynman variational principle to a tight-binding lattice and compares several analytical approximations.
result: Provides analytical expressions for the ground state energy and zero-temperature polaron dispersion.
conclusion: The extended variational method yields accurate results for lattice polarons, useful for understanding electron-phonon interactions in solids.

title: Dynamical Magnetic Breakdown And Quantum Oscillations From Hot-spot Scattering
authors: Léo Mangeolle And Johannes Knolle
abstract:
Author(s): Léo Mangeolle and Johannes Knolle

Quantum oscillations (QOs) are a well-established probe of Fermi-surface (FS) geometry and in the presence of long-range density wave order can display new QO frequencies from reconstructed FS pockets. We show that such reconstructed frequencies can arise even in the absence of long-range density or…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245132] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies dynamical magnetic breakdown and quantum oscillations from hot-spot scattering in metals with density wave order.
motivation: To understand how quantum oscillations can arise from reconstructed Fermi surface pockets even without long-range order.
method: Theoretical analysis using semiclassical dynamics and scattering at hot spots on the Fermi surface.
result: Shows that reconstructed quantum oscillation frequencies can emerge from hot-spot scattering alone.
conclusion: Provides a mechanism for quantum oscillations in materials without long-range density wave order.

title: Transverse Spin Transport In Intrinsic GaAs-based Multiple Quantum Wells
authors: Danni Shi, Hongyu Sun, Xiaonan Zhang, Lingxiu Chen, Chuanlei Jia, Xiaolan Xue, Yue Yu, Yang Zhang, And Liwei Shi
abstract:
Author(s): Danni Shi, Hongyu Sun, Xiaonan Zhang, Lingxiu Chen, Chuanlei Jia, Xiaolan Xue, Yue Yu, Yang Zhang, and Liwei Shi

We investigate photocurrent generation in undoped [MATH] multiple quantum wells at room temperature using spatially resolved photocurrent mapping. Under linearly polarized excitation, the response is dominated by the photot…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245302] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies photocurrent generation and transverse spin transport in GaAs multiple quantum wells using spatially resolved photocurrent mapping.
motivation: To understand spin-dependent transport and photocurrent effects in semiconductor quantum wells, which are relevant for spintronics.
method: Spatially resolved photocurrent mapping under linearly polarized excitation at room temperature.
result: The response is dominated by the photocurrent, with evidence of transverse spin transport.
conclusion: The findings contribute to the understanding of spin transport in semiconductor heterostructures.

title: Optical Vortex Probe Of Loop-current Chirality In Moiré Materials
authors: Nobuhiko Yokoshi And Akihito Kato
abstract:
Author(s): Nobuhiko Yokoshi and Akihito Kato

We propose a symmetry-resolved optical probe of intrinsic loop-current chirality in moiré materials, with twisted bilayer graphene as a representative realization. Interlayer interference generates chiral electronic circulation on triangular plaquettes, giving rise to an intrinsic geometric chiralit…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245303] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Proposes an optical vortex probe to detect loop-current chirality in moiré materials like twisted bilayer graphene.
motivation: To provide a symmetry-resolved optical method for probing intrinsic chiral electronic currents in moiré materials, which are difficult to detect with conventional techniques.
method: Theoretical analysis using optical vortex beams to couple to chiral loop currents, exploiting interlayer interference in twisted bilayer graphene.
result: The optical vortex probe can selectively excite and detect loop-current chirality, offering a new tool for characterizing moiré materials.
conclusion: The proposed method enables direct optical detection of chiral currents, which may help understand correlated phases in moiré systems.

title: Topological Quasibound States In The Continuum Induced By ${σ}_{h}$ Symmetry Being Broken Beyond A Threshold
authors: Yongqi Chen, Chaofeng Xie, Tongtong Zhu, Weiqiang Ding, And Yurui Fang
abstract:
Author(s): Yongqi Chen, Chaofeng Xie, Tongtong Zhu, Weiqiang Ding, and Yurui Fang

Transitions from bound states in the continuum (BICs) to quasi-BICs ([MATH]) are typically realized by introducing in-plane asymmetry, including permittivity asymmetry (ε-qBICs) and geometry asymmetry ([MATH]). Here, we demonstrate that when the in-plane symmetr…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245419] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological bound states in the continuum (BICs) in photonic systems, focusing on symmetry-breaking-induced transitions.
motivation: To understand how in-plane symmetry breaking beyond a threshold can induce quasi-BICs from BICs, which is important for photonic applications.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a photonic structure with σ_h symmetry and study the transition from BICs to quasi-BICs as symmetry is broken, using numerical simulations.
result: They find that quasi-BICs appear only when the symmetry breaking exceeds a certain threshold, and the Q-factor scales with the asymmetry parameter.
conclusion: The work provides a new mechanism for controlling BICs via symmetry breaking, relevant for designing high-Q photonic resonators.

title: Complete Decomposition Of Anomalous Diffusion In Variable Speed Generalized Lévy Walks
authors: Abhijit Bera And Kevin E. Bassler
abstract:
Author(s): Abhijit Bera and Kevin E. Bassler

Variable speed generalized Lévy walks (VGLWs) are a class of spatiotemporally coupled stochastic processes that unify a broad range of previously studied models within a single parametrized framework. Their dynamics consist of discrete random steps, or flights, during which the walker's speed varies…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064124] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a complete decomposition of anomalous diffusion in variable speed generalized Lévy walks, a class of stochastic processes.
motivation: To unify and understand a broad range of anomalous diffusion models within a single parametrized framework.
method: The authors analyze variable speed generalized Lévy walks (VGLWs) using mathematical decomposition techniques to characterize the spatiotemporal coupling.
result: They achieve a complete decomposition of the anomalous diffusion behavior, revealing the underlying mechanisms.
conclusion: The work provides a unified theoretical framework for anomalous diffusion, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Spectral Properties Of non-Hermitian Real Random Matrices With Long-range Correlations
authors: Ulysse Marquis
abstract:
Author(s): Ulysse Marquis

We investigate the spectral properties of non-Hermitian real random matrices whose entries exhibit long-range correlations decaying as [MATH]. We find a progressive breakdown of the circular law, controlled by the decrease of [MATH]. In all cases, the radial eigenvalue density decreases a…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064126] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spectral properties of non-Hermitian random matrices with long-range correlations, focusing on deviations from the circular law.
motivation: Understanding how long-range correlations affect eigenvalue distributions in non-Hermitian random matrices, which is a topic in random matrix theory.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of the radial eigenvalue density for real random matrices with power-law decaying correlations.
result: A progressive breakdown of the circular law is observed as the correlation exponent decreases, with the radial density decaying faster than the circular law prediction.
conclusion: Long-range correlations significantly alter the spectral properties of non-Hermitian random matrices, leading to new universality classes.

title: Yielding In Dense Active Matter
authors: Adil Ghaznavi, Saverio Rossi, Francesco Zamponi, And M. Lisa Manning
abstract:
Author(s): Adil Ghaznavi, Saverio Rossi, Francesco Zamponi, and M. Lisa Manning

High-density granular active matter is a useful model for dense animal collectives and could be useful for designing reconfigurable materials that can flow or solidify on command. Recent work has demonstrated key similarities and differences between the mechanical response of dense active matter and…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065410] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies yielding and mechanical response in dense granular active matter, a model for animal collectives and reconfigurable materials.
motivation: Understanding how dense active matter yields under stress is important for designing materials that can switch between solid and fluid states.
method: The authors use numerical simulations and theoretical modeling to analyze the yielding transition in a dense active granular system.
result: They identify key similarities and differences between active and passive yielding, revealing the role of activity in modifying the mechanical response.
conclusion: Activity can tune the yielding behavior, offering potential for designing reconfigurable materials with controlled flow properties.

title: Emergent Metastable Behavior In A Resource-constrained Network Of Exclusion Processes
authors: Nikhil Bhatia, Ashish Kumar Pandey, And Arvind Kumar Gupta
abstract:
Author(s): Nikhil Bhatia, Ashish Kumar Pandey, and Arvind Kumar Gupta

Inspired by the intrinsic organization observed in various biological and physical processes, which manifests through interacting subsystems connected by networks, where particles often compete for limited resources, we study a four-lane network system with a branching-merging geometry under resourc…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064122] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies metastable behavior in a resource-constrained network of exclusion processes, a statistical physics model.
motivation: To understand emergent organization in biological and physical systems where particles compete for limited resources in a network.
method: The authors analyze a four-lane network with branching-merging geometry using exclusion processes and resource constraints.
result: They observe emergent metastable states and characterize their properties under resource limitations.
conclusion: The work provides insights into non-equilibrium steady states and metastability in networked transport systems.

title: Pearl Supratransmission In A Boundary-driven Two-dimensional Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation With A Hole
authors: Rudy Kusdiantara And Hadi Susanto
abstract:
Author(s): Rudy Kusdiantara and Hadi Susanto

We investigate energy supratransmission in a boundary-driven two-dimensional nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a central hole. Harmonic forcing with azimuthal modulation generates standing-wave states whose existence and stability depend on the driving amplitude, the inner radius, and the imposed …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064204] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies energy supratransmission in a boundary-driven 2D nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a hole, focusing on standing-wave states and their stability.
motivation: To understand nonlinear wave propagation and energy transfer in a 2D system with a defect, which is relevant to nonlinear optics and condensed matter physics.
method: The authors perform numerical simulations and stability analysis of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a central hole and azimuthal modulation.
result: They find that supratransmission occurs above a threshold driving amplitude, and the existence and stability of standing-wave states depend on the inner radius and driving parameters.
conclusion: The study provides insights into energy transport in nonlinear systems with defects, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Community Detection By The Normalized Ricci Flow With The Optimization Of The Information Entropy
authors: Wenli Wang, Silu Wang, Chaoqun Ma, Yi Xiong, Guoqing Chen, And Jiao Gu
abstract:
Author(s): Wenli Wang, Silu Wang, Chaoqun Ma, Yi Xiong, Guoqing Chen, and Jiao Gu

Discrete Ricci curvature serves as a fundamental geometric tool for quantifying the structural characteristics of complex networks, effectively capturing the richness of their connection patterns. Building on this theoretical framework, this paper proposes an improved discrete Ricci curvature algori…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064304] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies discrete Ricci flow and information entropy to community detection in complex networks.
motivation: Community detection is important for understanding network structure, and geometric methods like Ricci curvature can capture rich connectivity patterns.
method: The authors propose an improved discrete Ricci curvature algorithm and combine it with normalized Ricci flow and information entropy optimization to detect communities.
result: The method is validated on synthetic and real-world networks, showing improved community detection performance compared to existing algorithms.
conclusion: The proposed geometric approach effectively identifies communities by leveraging curvature and entropy, offering a new tool for network analysis.

title: Manifold-based Transformation Of Probability Distributions: Application To The Inverse Problem Of Reconstructing Distributions From Experimental Data
authors: Tomotaka Oroguchi, Rintaro Inoue, And Masaaki Sugiyama
abstract:
Author(s): Tomotaka Oroguchi, Rintaro Inoue, and Masaaki Sugiyama

Information geometry is a mathematical framework that elucidates the manifold structure of the probability distribution space (p space), providing a systematic approach to transforming probability distributions (PDs). In this study, we utilized information geometry to address the inverse problems as…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023291] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses information geometry to transform probability distributions for solving inverse problems in experimental data reconstruction.
motivation: The authors aim to address the inverse problem of reconstructing probability distributions from experimental data, which is common in fields like structural biology.
method: They apply information geometry, specifically the manifold structure of probability distribution spaces, to systematically transform distributions and solve the inverse problem.
result: The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of the manifold-based transformation approach for reconstructing distributions from limited or noisy experimental data.
conclusion: Information geometry provides a powerful framework for inverse problems involving probability distributions, with potential applications in various experimental sciences.

title: Dynamical Phase Transitions Across Slow And Fast Regimes In A Two-tone Driven Duffing Resonator
authors: Soumya S. Kumar, Javier Del Pino, Letizia Catalini, Alexander Eichler, And Oded Zilberberg
abstract:
Author(s): Soumya S. Kumar, Javier del Pino, Letizia Catalini, Alexander Eichler, and Oded Zilberberg

The dynamical phase transitions of a Duffing resonator subjected to a bichromatic drive across the slow- and fast-beating regimes are mapped. An analytical threshold to observe these transitions based on an effective nonlinear response theory is provided, explaining the mechanism behind these processes. Complementary analytical treatments for the slow and fast regimes are supplied.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023298] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical phase transitions in a driven Duffing resonator, focusing on classical nonlinear dynamics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the transition between slow and fast beating regimes in a nonlinear resonator under bichromatic drive, which is relevant for classical nonlinear dynamics and potential applications in sensing.
method: The authors develop an analytical effective nonlinear response theory and provide complementary treatments for slow and fast regimes, supported by numerical simulations.
result: They map the dynamical phase transitions and derive an analytical threshold for observing these transitions.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for understanding dynamical phase transitions in driven nonlinear resonators, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Complete Inelastic Transparency Of Time-modulated Resonant Photonic Circuits
authors: M. Sumetsky
abstract:
Author(s): M. Sumetsky

Photonic circuits modulated in time can convert the input light frequency [MATH], shifting it by multiples of the modulation frequency [MATH] and, in certain cases, amplify the total input light power. Of special interest are photonic circuits employing microwave capacitors, which instantaneou…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023299] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies inelastic transparency in time-modulated resonant photonic circuits, focusing on frequency conversion and power amplification.
motivation: To understand and exploit the effects of time modulation on light propagation in photonic circuits, particularly for frequency conversion and amplification.
method: Theoretical analysis using coupled-mode theory and Floquet formalism for time-periodic systems.
result: Demonstrates that under certain conditions, time-modulated resonant photonic circuits can achieve complete inelastic transparency, converting input light to different frequencies without loss.
conclusion: Time-modulated photonic circuits offer a new mechanism for frequency conversion and amplification, with potential applications in classical and quantum photonics.

title: General Spin Models From Noncollinear Spin Density Functional Theory And Spin-cluster Expansion
authors: Tomonori Tanaka And Yoshihiro Gohda
abstract:
Author(s): Tomonori Tanaka and Yoshihiro Gohda

We present a data-efficient framework for constructing general classical spin Hamiltonians by combining the spin-cluster expansion (SCE) with fully self-consistent noncollinear spin density functional theory (DFT). The key idea is to fit the SCE model to magnetic torques rather than to total energie…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023300] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A data-efficient framework combining spin-cluster expansion with noncollinear spin density functional theory to construct classical spin Hamiltonians from magnetic torques.
motivation: To enable efficient and accurate construction of spin Hamiltonians for complex magnetic systems without relying on total energy calculations.
method: Uses spin-cluster expansion fitted to magnetic torques computed from self-consistent noncollinear spin DFT.
result: Demonstrates that the torque-based approach yields accurate spin models with fewer DFT calculations compared to energy-based methods.
conclusion: The proposed framework is a practical tool for deriving spin models for large-scale simulations of magnetic materials.

title: Visualizing Phonon Edge States On Molybdenum Disulfide
authors: Patrick Giese, Mathias Stokkebye Nissen, Stig Helveg, And Jakob Schiøtz
abstract:
Author(s): Patrick Giese, Mathias Stokkebye Nissen, Stig Helveg, and Jakob Schiøtz

Enhanced atomic vibrations have previously been observed near edges of two-dimensional materials with high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM). Here this observation is accounted for by localized phonon edge modes by including correlated atom vibrations in HR-TEM image simulations.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022049] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses HR-TEM image simulations to show that enhanced atomic vibrations near edges of MoS2 are due to localized phonon edge modes.
motivation: Enhanced atomic vibrations observed near edges of 2D materials in HR-TEM experiments lacked a clear explanation.
method: The authors performed HR-TEM image simulations that include correlated atom vibrations to model the observed contrast.
result: The simulations reproduce the experimental observations, attributing them to localized phonon edge modes.
conclusion: Phonon edge modes are responsible for the enhanced vibrations at edges of MoS2, providing a theoretical explanation for the experimental data.

title: Emergent Self-attention From Astrocyte-gated Associative Memory Dynamics
authors: Arnau Vivet And Alex Arenas
abstract:
Author(s): Arnau Vivet and Alex Arenas

We introduce a Hopfield-type associative memory in which effective connectivity is multiplicatively modulated by astrocytic gains evolving under an entropy-regularized replicator equation. The coupled neuron-astrocyte dynamics admit a Lyapunov function, ensuring global convergence. At fixed points, …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023276] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A Hopfield-type associative memory model with astrocyte-gated multiplicative modulation and entropy-regularized replicator dynamics, showing global convergence via a Lyapunov function.
motivation: To incorporate astrocytic modulation into neural network models of associative memory, bridging neuroscience and machine learning.
method: Introduces a coupled neuron-astrocyte system where astrocytic gains evolve under an entropy-regularized replicator equation, and proves global convergence using a Lyapunov function.
result: The dynamics converge to fixed points that correspond to stored patterns, with astrocytic gains modulating effective connectivity.
conclusion: The model provides a biologically plausible mechanism for emergent self-attention in associative memory, but is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Tensor Network Approach To Momentum-resolved Spectroscopy In Nonperiodic Super-moiré Systems
authors: Anouar Moustaj, Yitao Sun, Tiago V. C. Antão, And Jose L. Lado
abstract:
Author(s): Anouar Moustaj, Yitao Sun, Tiago V. C. Antão, and Jose L. Lado

Computing spectral functions in large, nonperiodic super-moiré systems remains an open problem due to the exceptionally large system size that must be considered. Here, we establish a tensor network methodology that allows computing momentum-resolved spectral functions of noninteracting and interact…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023282] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A tensor network method for computing momentum-resolved spectral functions in large nonperiodic super-moiré systems.
motivation: Computing spectral functions in large nonperiodic super-moiré systems is challenging due to the large system sizes required.
method: The authors develop a tensor network approach to compute momentum-resolved spectral functions for noninteracting and interacting systems.
result: The method enables spectral calculations in systems that are otherwise intractable with conventional techniques.
conclusion: Tensor networks provide a viable route to study spectral properties of complex moiré systems.

title: Observation Of An Amplitudelike Mode In The Excitonic Insulator ${\mathrm{Ta}}_{2}{\mathrm{Pd}}_{3}{\mathrm{Te}}_{5}$
authors: Y.-S. Choi, Dirk Wulferding, Raju Kalaivanan, Rajesh Kumar Ulaganathan, Raman Sankar, And Kwang-Yong Choi
abstract:
Author(s): Y.-S. Choi, Dirk Wulferding, Raju Kalaivanan, Rajesh Kumar Ulaganathan, Raman Sankar, and Kwang-Yong Choi

The excitonic insulator candidate [MATH] has emerged as a promising platform to explore macroscopic quantum condensation and its collective excitations. Using polarization-resolved Raman spectroscopy, we identify a symmetry-selective electronic mode tha…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023273] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of an amplitude-like mode in the excitonic insulator Ta2Pd3Te5 using Raman spectroscopy.
motivation: Excitonic insulators are a platform for studying macroscopic quantum condensation and collective excitations; identifying collective modes is key to understanding their nature.
method: Polarization-resolved Raman spectroscopy was used to identify a symmetry-selective electronic mode in Ta2Pd3Te5.
result: A symmetry-selective electronic mode was observed, interpreted as an amplitude-like mode of the excitonic condensate.
conclusion: The findings provide evidence for collective excitations in excitonic insulators, advancing the understanding of these quantum condensed phases.

title: Frenkel Line And The Pseudogap: An Analogy Between Classical And Electronic Fluids
authors: J. Fournier, P.-O. Downey, O. Gingras, C.-D. Hébert, M. Charlebois, And A.-M. S. Tremblay
abstract:
Author(s): J. Fournier, P.-O. Downey, O. Gingras, C.-D. Hébert, M. Charlebois, and A.-M. S. Tremblay

Asymptotically close to critical end points of first-order transitions, maxima in thermodynamic quantities occur along a line called the Widom line, a concept first introduced in classical fluids. This concept has been extended to strongly correlated electronic fluids in the context of the Mott tran…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023278] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper draws an analogy between the Frenkel line in classical fluids and the pseudogap in strongly correlated electronic fluids, focusing on thermodynamic response functions near critical endpoints.
motivation: To extend the concept of the Widom line from classical fluids to electronic systems, particularly the Mott transition, and to explore analogies between classical and quantum critical phenomena.
method: The authors analyze thermodynamic quantities such as specific heat and compressibility near critical endpoints, comparing classical fluid behavior with that of the Hubbard model using cluster dynamical mean-field theory.
result: They identify a line of maxima in thermodynamic response functions in the electronic system, analogous to the Frenkel line in classical fluids, and relate it to the pseudogap phase.
conclusion: The analogy provides a unified perspective on critical phenomena across classical and quantum systems, but the work is primarily a condensed matter physics study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Unveiling Dielectric Relaxation And Shear Rheology In Water
authors: Songming Liu And Jiaxing Yuan
abstract:
Author(s): Songming Liu and Jiaxing Yuan

The complex dynamics of liquid water are manifested in its unique dielectric relaxation and nonlinear shear rheology. We investigate the dielectric and rheological responses of TIP4P/[MATH] water using molecular dynamics simulations across a wide temperature range, including the deeply supercooled regi…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023266] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Molecular dynamics study of dielectric relaxation and shear rheology in water using TIP4P model.
motivation: To understand the complex dynamics of liquid water, especially in the deeply supercooled regime.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations of TIP4P water across a wide temperature range.
result: Characterization of dielectric and rheological responses.
conclusion: Provides insights into water's relaxation and mechanical properties.

title: Quantum-selected Configuration Interaction: Classical Diagonalization Of Hamiltonians In Subspaces Selected By Quantum Computers
authors: Keita Kanno, Masaya Kohda, Ryosuke Imai, Sho Koh, Kosuke Mitarai, Wataru Mizukami, And Yuya O. Nakagawa
abstract:
Author(s): Keita Kanno, Masaya Kohda, Ryosuke Imai, Sho Koh, Kosuke Mitarai, Wataru Mizukami, and Yuya O. Nakagawa

We propose quantum-selected configuration interaction, a class of hybrid quantum-classical algorithms for calculating the ground- and excited-state energies of many-electron Hamiltonians on noisy quantum devices. Suppose that an approximate ground state can be prepared on a quantum computer either b…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023268] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: A hybrid quantum-classical algorithm for computing ground- and excited-state energies of many-electron Hamiltonians using quantum computers to select important configurations for classical diagonalization.
motivation: To leverage noisy near-term quantum devices for quantum chemistry calculations by combining quantum state preparation with classical diagonalization to reduce quantum resource requirements.
method: The algorithm prepares an approximate ground state on a quantum computer, measures in the computational basis to sample important Slater determinants, and then performs classical configuration interaction in the selected subspace.
result: The method is demonstrated on small molecules, showing accurate energies with fewer quantum resources than full quantum phase estimation.
conclusion: Quantum-selected configuration interaction offers a practical approach for quantum chemistry on noisy quantum devices, balancing quantum and classical computation.

title: Dynamics Of Quantum Chiral Solitons
authors: Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, And Cristian D. Batista
abstract:
Author(s): Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, and Cristian D. Batista

A nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains demonstrates that they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, appearing as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and becoming detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021056] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains shows they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, detectable via neutron scattering.
motivation: To understand the quantum dynamics of chiral solitons in spin chains, which are topological excitations with potential relevance to low-dimensional magnetism.
method: Develops a nonperturbative quantization approach for chiral solitons and analyzes their condensation into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid.
result: Chiral solitons appear as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and can be detected via inelastic neutron scattering.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for chiral soliton dynamics and their experimental signatures.

title: Free And Interacting Fermionic Conformal Field Theories On The Fuzzy Sphere
authors: Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, And Yin-Chen He
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, and Yin-Chen He
