Researchers use noncommutative “fuzzy” spheres to study three-dimensional fermionic conformal field theories, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021055] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses fuzzy sphere regularization to study free and interacting fermionic conformal field theories in three dimensions, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.
motivation: To develop a non-perturbative method for studying strongly coupled conformal field theories using the fuzzy sphere as a regularization scheme.
method: The authors employ the fuzzy sphere, a noncommutative geometry, to regularize fermionic CFTs and perform numerical simulations.
result: They find evidence of emergent supersymmetry in the interacting theory and compute critical exponents.
conclusion: The fuzzy sphere is a viable tool for studying fermionic CFTs and may reveal new physics such as emergent supersymmetry.

title: General Approach To Solving Spin Moiré Superstructures
authors: Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. Debeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, And Joseph G. Checkelsky
abstract:
Author(s): Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. DeBeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, and Joseph G. Checkelsky

Mapping of spin textures in EuAg
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021054] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a general approach to solving spin moiré superstructures, demonstrating three distinct magnetic phases in EuAg4Sb2 and establishing a design framework for spin-based vortex lattices.
motivation: Spin moiré superstructures offer a platform for manipulating information via spin textures, but a general theoretical framework for their solution is lacking.
method: The authors combine neutron scattering, magnetization measurements, and theoretical modeling to map the magnetic phase diagram of EuAg4Sb2 and identify three tunable magnetic phases.
result: Three distinct magnetic phases are revealed, including a spin moiré superstructure, and a design framework for spin-based vortex lattices is established.
conclusion: This work provides a general approach to engineering spin moiré superstructures, enabling future applications in information manipulation via spin textures.

title: Fate Of Topological Dirac Magnons In Van Der Waals Ferromagnets At Finite Temperature
authors: Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, And Alexander Mook
abstract:
Author(s): Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, and Alexander Mook

Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures demonstrates that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point, providing a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021053] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: Theoretical study of topological magnon gaps in van der Waals ferromagnets at finite temperature.
motivation: To understand the stability of topological magnon gaps near the Curie point for spintronic applications.
method: Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures.
result: Topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point.
conclusion: Provides a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.

title: Are Neural Networks Collision Resistant?
authors: Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, And Riccardo Zecchina
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, and Riccardo Zecchina

A study of the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network shows that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions, a result of direct relevance for the definition of new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021051] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network, showing that efficient algorithms fail, which is relevant for cryptography based on machine learning.
motivation: To understand whether neural networks can serve as collision-resistant hash functions for cryptographic protocols.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of finding collisions in a one-layer neural network using theoretical and algorithmic approaches.
result: Efficient algorithms are shown to fail to find collisions, suggesting that such neural networks may be collision resistant.
conclusion: Simple neural networks could be used as building blocks for cryptographic protocols, but the work is primarily about computational complexity and cryptography, not quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Predicting Physical Links In Networks
authors: Shuai Li, Wei Chen, And Jan Nagler
abstract:
Author(s): Shuai Li, Wei Chen, and Jan Nagler

A physics-informed framework allows for inferring general causal links across a wide range of networked dynamics systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021048] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A physics-informed framework for inferring causal links in networked dynamical systems.
motivation: Understanding causal relationships in complex networks is crucial but challenging; existing methods often lack physical grounding.
method: The authors develop a framework that incorporates physical principles to infer causal links from time-series data of network dynamics.
result: The framework successfully predicts physical links across various networked systems, outperforming standard causal inference methods.
conclusion: Physics-informed approaches can significantly improve causal link prediction in networks, with potential applications in diverse fields.

title: General Framework Enabling Polarity-Tunable Time-Reversal Symmetric Superconducting Diode Effects In Gate-Defined Homojunctions
authors: Hongwei Zhang, Chunsheng Wang, Ran Wang, Senyang Pan, Hengning Wang, Jiaqiang Cai, Yonglai Liu, Zhe Qu, Xiangde Zhu, Wei Ning, Chuanying Xi, Jinglei Zhang, Ning Hao, Guolin Zheng, And Mingliang Tian
abstract:
Author(s): Hongwei Zhang, Chunsheng Wang, Ran Wang, Senyang Pan, Hengning Wang, Jiaqiang Cai, Yonglai Liu, Zhe Qu, Xiangde Zhu, Wei Ning, Chuanying Xi, Jinglei Zhang, Ning Hao, Guolin Zheng, and Mingliang Tian

Local protonic gating in
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021046] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a time-reversal symmetric superconducting diode effect in gate-defined homojunctions using local protonic gating.
motivation: To achieve magnetic-field-free control of nonreciprocal critical currents in superconducting devices.
method: Local protonic gating is applied to homojunctions to induce a superconducting diode effect without breaking time-reversal symmetry.
result: Polarity-tunable superconducting diode effect is observed, enabling control of nonreciprocal critical currents.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for superconducting diodes that may be useful for low-dissipation electronics.

title: Anyon Superfluidity Of Excitons In Quantum Hall Bilayers
authors: Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, And Ashvin Vishwanath
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, and Ashvin Vishwanath

Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers reveals that topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids, offering a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021044] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically predicts anyonic exciton superfluidity in quantum Hall bilayers, a topological condensed matter phenomenon.
motivation: To explore exotic collective quantum states arising from topological criticality in quantum Hall bilayers.
method: Theoretical analysis using topological field theory and mean-field approaches.
result: Topological criticality enables anyonic exciton superfluids with robust properties.
conclusion: Quantum Hall bilayers provide a platform for engineering anyonic superfluids, advancing topological quantum matter.

title: Probing Quantum Anomalous Hall States In Twisted Bilayer ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$ Via Attractive Polaron Spectroscopy
authors: Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, And Mohammad Hafezi
abstract:
Author(s): Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, and Mohammad Hafezi

Magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted WSe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021037] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses magneto-optical spectroscopy to probe quantum anomalous Hall states in twisted bilayer WSe2, demonstrating electric-field control of magnetic order.
motivation: To investigate the quantum anomalous Hall phase in twisted bilayer WSe2 and understand the interplay between topology and magnetism.
method: Magneto-optical spectroscopy, specifically attractive polaron spectroscopy, is used to probe the electronic structure and magnetic ordering.
result: Observation of a spontaneous quantum anomalous Hall phase and electric-field-induced switching between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic orders.
conclusion: Twisted bilayer WSe2 is a promising platform for studying topological phases with tunable magnetism.

title: Liquid-Gas Criticality Of Hyperuniform Fluids
authors: Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, And Qun-Li Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, and Qun-Li Lei

Where ordinary fluids show wild fluctuations and critical opalescence, hyperuniform fluids of spinning particles stay unusually calm yet highly susceptible at the liquid–vapor critical point.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021032] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the liquid-gas criticality of hyperuniform fluids, focusing on density fluctuations and critical opalescence suppression.
motivation: Hyperuniform fluids exhibit suppressed density fluctuations at large scales, and understanding their critical behavior at the liquid-vapor transition is of fundamental interest in statistical physics.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and possibly simulations to investigate the critical properties of hyperuniform fluids composed of spinning particles.
result: They find that hyperuniform fluids remain unusually calm (suppressed fluctuations) yet highly susceptible at the critical point, contrasting with ordinary fluids.
conclusion: The work reveals novel critical behavior in hyperuniform fluids, extending the understanding of phase transitions in systems with constrained fluctuations.

title: Stealthy-Hyperuniform Wave Dynamics In Two-Dimensional Photonic Crystals
authors: Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, And Mikael C. Rechtsman
abstract:
Author(s): Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, and Mikael C. Rechtsman

While disordered stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be largely transparent within a particular range of wavelengths, new experiments on large-scale silicon photonic crystals reveal unexpected residual scattering driven by radiative loss.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021028] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies wave dynamics in disordered stealthy hyperuniform photonic crystals, revealing unexpected residual scattering due to radiative loss.
motivation: Stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be transparent in certain wavelength ranges, but experiments show residual scattering that needs explanation.
method: Large-scale experiments on silicon photonic crystals combined with theoretical analysis of radiative loss mechanisms.
result: Unexpected residual scattering is driven by radiative loss, contradicting the expectation of near-perfect transparency.
conclusion: The findings highlight limitations of stealthy hyperuniformity for photonic applications and suggest design modifications.

title: Ballistic Spin Valve In Graphene Realized Via Electron Optics
authors: Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, And Ivan J. Vera-Marun
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, and Ivan J. Vera-Marun

Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene reveals gate-tunable ballistic spin transport, providing a mechanism for coherent spin control through spin-dependent electron optics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021029] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates ballistic spin transport and spin valve effect in graphene using transverse magnetic focusing, a condensed matter physics result with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To realize coherent spin control in graphene via electron optics, enabling gate-tunable ballistic spin transport.
method: Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene devices to observe spin-dependent electron trajectories.
result: Observation of gate-tunable ballistic spin transport and a spin valve effect.
conclusion: Graphene can serve as a platform for coherent spin control through electron optics, with potential for spintronic applications.

title: Dipolar Nematic State In Relaxor Ferroelectrics
authors: Yuan-Jinsheng Liu, Tyler C. Sterling, And Shi Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yuan-Jinsheng Liu, Tyler C. Sterling, and Shi Liu

A nematic ordering underpins the behavior of relaxor ferroelectrics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021022] Published Wed Apr 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a dipolar nematic state in relaxor ferroelectrics, focusing on condensed matter physics without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Relaxor ferroelectrics exhibit complex ordering; understanding the nematic state may clarify their properties.
method: The authors likely use experimental or theoretical condensed matter techniques to characterize the dipolar nematic phase.
result: They identify a dipolar nematic state and describe its properties.
conclusion: The work advances understanding of relaxor ferroelectrics but does not relate to the user's research interests.

title: Excitations Across The Equilibrium And Photoinduced “Hidden” States Of Magnetoresistive Manganites
authors: Shiyu Fan, Feng Jin, Taehun Kim, Umesh Kumar, Zixun Zhang, Vivek Bhartiya, Jiemin Li, Brandon Yalin, Yanhong Gu, Mingqiang Gu, Wen Hu, Claudio Mazzoli, G. Lawrence Carr, Osor S. Barišić, Andrey S. Mishchenko, Valentina Bisogni, Sobhit Singh, Wenbin Wu, And Jonathan Pelliciari
abstract:
Author(s): Shiyu Fan, Feng Jin, Taehun Kim, Umesh Kumar, Zixun Zhang, Vivek Bhartiya, Jiemin Li, Brandon Yalin, Yanhong Gu, Mingqiang Gu, Wen Hu, Claudio Mazzoli, G. Lawrence Carr, Osor S. Barišić, Andrey S. Mishchenko, Valentina Bisogni, Sobhit Singh, Wenbin Wu, and Jonathan Pelliciari

Ultrafast photoexcitation in /3Ca1/3MnO3 generates a long-lived hidden phase with unique polaronic and phononic excitations that do not exist under standard equilibrium conditions.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021018] Published Thu Apr 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies photoinduced hidden phases and excitations in magnetoresistive manganites using ultrafast spectroscopy.
motivation: To understand the nature of photoinduced hidden phases in strongly correlated electron systems, which may have implications for novel electronic phases.
method: Combines resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) and ultrafast optical pump-probe spectroscopy to probe excitations across equilibrium and hidden states.
result: Identifies unique polaronic and phononic excitations in the hidden phase that are absent in equilibrium, indicating a distinct lattice and electronic configuration.
conclusion: The hidden phase exhibits a different polaronic and phononic structure, suggesting a new metastable state with potential for controlling material properties via light.

title: More Is Less In Unpercolated Active Solids
authors: Jack Binysh, Guido Baardink, Jonas Veenstra, Corentin Coulais, And Anton Souslov
abstract:
Author(s): Jack Binysh, Guido Baardink, Jonas Veenstra, Corentin Coulais, and Anton Souslov

By combining experiments with robotic metamaterials and theory, this work shows that increasing microscopic activity can counterintuitively cause a solid’s macroscale active response to vanish when active units are too sparse for the active forces to percolate through the structure.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021012] Published Mon Apr 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies active solids where increasing microscopic activity can suppress macroscopic response due to lack of percolation.
motivation: To understand how sparse active units affect the collective mechanical response of active solids.
method: Combines experiments with robotic metamaterials and theoretical modeling.
result: Increasing activity can counterintuitively reduce the macroscopic active response when active units are too sparse to percolate.
conclusion: The percolation of active forces is crucial for macroscopic activity; more activity can lead to less effect if units are sparse.

title: Provable Quantum Speedups For Computing Persistence In Topological Data Analysis
authors: Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, And Ryu Hayakawa
abstract:
Author(s): Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, and Ryu Hayakawa

A quantum algorithm achieving exponential speedup for a topological data analysis problem is proposed, potentially driving new practical applications in quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020361] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a quantum algorithm for topological data analysis with exponential speedup, but it is not aligned with the user's research interests.
motivation: Topological data analysis is a classical machine learning technique; the authors aim to demonstrate quantum advantage in this domain.
method: The algorithm uses quantum computing to compute persistence diagrams, a key tool in topological data analysis.
result: The algorithm achieves exponential speedup over classical methods for certain instances.
conclusion: This work suggests potential practical applications for quantum computing in data analysis, but it is not directly relevant to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Grand Challenge Of Quantum Applications
authors: Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. Mcclean, Thomas O’brien, And Nicholas C. Rubin
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. McClean, Thomas O’Brien, and Nicholas C. Rubin

A proposed five-stage framework outlines the path to useful quantum computing, detailing the scientific milestones required to bridge the gap between theory and real-world utility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020101] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A high-level perspective piece proposing a five-stage framework for achieving useful quantum computing, focusing on scientific milestones rather than technical results.
motivation: To outline a roadmap bridging the gap between current quantum computing capabilities and real-world applications.
method: Conceptual framework based on expert opinion and analysis of the field's progress.
result: A five-stage framework with milestones for quantum utility.
conclusion: The framework provides a structured path but does not present new technical contributions.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:
Author(s): Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew DeCross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, and Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial, serving as a benchmark for quantum computers.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a topological invariant with applications in knot theory and quantum gravity, and its approximation is a candidate for quantum advantage.
method: The authors design an end-to-end quantum algorithm that maps the Jones polynomial evaluation to a quantum circuit, including state preparation, unitary evolution, and measurement.
result: They demonstrate the algorithm on a trapped-ion quantum processor, showing that it can approximate the Jones polynomial for small knots and providing evidence of quantum advantage.
conclusion: The work establishes a practical benchmark for quantum computers and suggests that topological invariants like the Jones polynomial are promising for demonstrating quantum advantage.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge in 2D magnetism, which has revealed new phenomena and challenged established theories.
method: The paper is a review that surveys experimental and theoretical progress in 2D van der Waals magnetic materials.
result: The review covers ferromagnets, antiferromagnets, topology, quantum dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons, spintronics, and magneto-optical phenomena.
conclusion: The field is rapidly evolving, with potential for new applications and deeper understanding of low-dimensional magnetism.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from geometric frustration and interference effects.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, synthesizing findings from multiple studies.
result: Kagome metals exhibit a wealth of exotic states including topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, unconventional superconductivity, and orbital antiferromagnetism.
conclusion: The kagome lattice provides a rich platform for exploring correlated electron physics and may lead to new electronic states.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation.
motivation: Spin glasses serve as a model system for complex disordered systems, and understanding their dynamics has broad applications.
method: The review synthesizes experimental results, theoretical models, and large-scale numerical simulations.
result: The paper tracks progress in the field and highlights the synergy between experiment, theory, and simulation.
conclusion: Spin-glass dynamics remain a rich area for future research, with opportunities for further synergy across approaches.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on material candidates and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a type of quantum spin liquid with potential applications in topological quantum computing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental realizations in candidate materials, discussing their magnetic and topological properties.
result: Summarizes key candidate materials and their observed signatures of Kitaev spin liquid behavior, including chiral edge modes.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids remain an active area of research with promising materials, but definitive experimental confirmation is still ongoing.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to neural network data, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding coordinated activity in large neural networks is a key challenge in neuroscience.
method: The authors review recent progress in using maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques to analyze simultaneous recordings from thousands of neurons.
result: These methods uncover reproducible collective behaviors in neural populations.
conclusion: Statistical physics provides a powerful framework for modeling neural networks, with predictive power comparable to other areas of physics.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, focusing on nonradiative transitions and their applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a key photophysical process affecting the efficiency of light-emitting devices and solar energy conversion, yet its theoretical description remains challenging.
method: The review surveys various theoretical models, including nonadiabatic dynamics, Fermi's golden rule, and mixed quantum-classical approaches, to describe internal conversion.
result: The paper summarizes the strengths and limitations of current methods and identifies open questions in the field.
conclusion: Improved theoretical methods are needed to accurately predict internal conversion rates, which will aid in designing better photonic and energy-harvesting materials.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review of quantum aspects of magnetic skyrmions, covering their formation and quantum features.
motivation: To survey quantum-mechanical properties of skyrmions, which are topological spin textures with potential applications in spintronics.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion quantum interactions and quantum features.
result: Summarizes current understanding of quantum effects in skyrmion systems.
conclusion: Skyrmions exhibit quantum properties that may be harnessed for future technologies, but the field is still developing.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the Standard Model, including possible mediators and connections to dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and dark energy and to probe fundamental symmetries through spin-dependent forces.
method: Review of theoretical models for exotic boson-mediated spin-dependent interactions and experimental techniques (e.g., atomic magnetometry, torsion balances) used to search for them.
result: Summarizes current constraints on coupling constants and mass ranges for various exotic bosons, and outlines future experimental directions.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain a promising avenue for discovering new physics, but no definitive evidence has been found yet.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium reviewing synthetic quantum matter in fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions, focusing on simulation of condensed matter and gravity phenomena.
motivation: To explore quantum many-body physics in nonstandard geometries that enable simulation of topological phenomena and models of gravity and cosmology.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical implementations in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems, including fractal lattices, curved spaces, and synthetic dimensions.
result: Summarizes progress in realizing exotic geometries and their potential for simulating topological and gravitational physics.
conclusion: Synthetic quantum matter in nonstandard geometries is a promising avenue for quantum simulation, but the paper is a broad review without deep technical contributions to the user's specific interests.

title: Continuous Family Of Conformal Field Theories And Exactly Marginal Operators
authors: Shota Komatsu, Yuya Kusuki, Marco Meineri, And Hirosi Ooguri
abstract:
Author(s): Shota Komatsu, Yuya Kusuki, Marco Meineri, and Hirosi Ooguri

Does a conformal manifold imply the existence of exactly marginal operators? We answer this question affirmatively under the assumption that there exists a conformal interface with certain properties connecting nearby conformal field theories. We show that the exactly marginal operator that connects…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 241603] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that a conformal manifold implies the existence of exactly marginal operators, given a conformal interface connecting nearby CFTs.
motivation: To establish a general condition under which exactly marginal operators exist in conformal field theories, which is a fundamental question in quantum field theory and string theory.
method: The authors use conformal interfaces and bootstrap techniques to show that the existence of a conformal manifold forces the presence of exactly marginal operators.
result: They prove that under the assumption of a conformal interface with certain properties, exactly marginal operators must exist, connecting nearby CFTs.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous link between conformal manifolds and marginal operators, deepening the understanding of moduli spaces in CFT.

title: Universal Phonon-Mediated Superconductivity In Compressed Metal Monochalcogenides Beyond Anderson Localization
authors: Ertuğrul Karaca, Fang Hong, And Daniel Errandonea
abstract:
Author(s): Ertuğrul Karaca, Fang Hong, and Daniel Errandonea

High-pressure superconductivity in metal monochalcogenides has been ascribed to disorder-driven Anderson localization [
tldr: This paper studies phonon-mediated superconductivity in compressed metal monochalcogenides using density-functional perturbation theory and Migdal-Eliashberg calculations.
motivation: To understand the mechanism of high-pressure superconductivity in these materials, which was previously attributed to disorder-driven Anderson localization.
method: First-principles density-functional perturbation theory and Migdal-Eliashberg calculations.
result: Superconductivity in BiSe, PbSe, PbS, and HgS is phonon-mediated and not due to Anderson localization.
conclusion: The superconductivity in these compressed metal monochalcogenides is conventional phonon-mediated, contradicting the earlier Anderson localization hypothesis.

title: Duality Between Correlation Functions And Wilson Loops In Gauge Theory From Effective Field Theory
authors: Hao Chen, Pier Francesco Monni, Zhaoyan Pang, Gherardo Vita, And Hua Xing Zhu
abstract:
Author(s): Hao Chen, Pier Francesco Monni, Zhaoyan Pang, Gherardo Vita, and Hua Xing Zhu

In this Letter, we initiate a systematic study of the [MATH]-point correlation functions (CFs) in gauge theories in the sequential light-cone (SLC) limit. Focusing on QCD, we formulate a factorization theorem for the CF of four vector currents in this limit using tools from soft-collinear effective fie…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 241601] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies correlation functions and Wilson loops in gauge theories using effective field theory, focusing on QCD in the sequential light-cone limit.
motivation: To understand the structure of multi-point correlation functions in gauge theories and their relation to Wilson loops, which is important for high-energy physics and QCD.
method: The authors use soft-collinear effective field theory (SCET) to derive a factorization theorem for the four-point correlation function of vector currents in the sequential light-cone limit.
result: They establish a duality between correlation functions and Wilson loops in this limit, providing a systematic framework for computing such observables.
conclusion: The work advances the theoretical understanding of gauge theory correlation functions and may have implications for precision QCD calculations.

title: Room-Temperature Intrinsic Nonlinear Planar Hall Effect In ${\mathrm{TaIrTe}}_{4}$
authors: Chang Jiang, Fan Yang, Yu Zhao, Jinshan Yang, Peng Yu, Huiying Liu, Yuda Zhang, Zehao Jia, Xiangyu Cao, Li Tian, Jingyi Yan, Zheng Liu, Zhongkai Liu, Xian-Lei Sheng, Cong Xiao, Shengyuan A. Yang, Shaoming Dong, And Faxian Xiu
abstract:
Author(s): Chang Jiang, Fan Yang, Yu Zhao, Jinshan Yang, Peng Yu, Huiying Liu, Yuda Zhang, Zehao Jia, Xiangyu Cao, Li Tian, Jingyi Yan, Zheng Liu, Zhongkai Liu, Xian-Lei Sheng, Cong Xiao, Shengyuan A. Yang, Shaoming Dong, and Faxian Xiu

A room-temperature intrinsic nonlinear planar Hall effect in the nonmagnetic topological semimetal TaIrTe
[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236302] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of an intrinsic nonlinear planar Hall effect in the nonmagnetic topological semimetal TaIrTe4 at room temperature, driven by a Berry-connection-polarizability dipole.
motivation: To explore nonlinear transport phenomena in topological semimetals and understand the role of Berry curvature in generating nonlinear Hall effects without magnetic ordering.
method: Experimental measurement of the nonlinear planar Hall effect in TaIrTe4 under an in-plane magnetic field, combined with theoretical analysis based on Berry-connection-polarizability dipole.
result: A room-temperature intrinsic nonlinear planar Hall effect is observed, attributed to an orbital mechanism involving the Berry-connection-polarizability dipole.
conclusion: The findings reveal a new mechanism for nonlinear Hall effects in nonmagnetic topological semimetals, with potential for room-temperature applications.

title: Observation Of Switchable Chiral Magnons In An Altermagnet
authors: Zheyuan Liu, Hodaka Kikuchi, Zijun Wei, Shinichiro Asai, Mechthild Enderle, Ursula B. Hansen, Vasile O. Garlea, Manh D. Le, Gøran J. Nilsen, Igor A. Zaliznyak, And Takatsugu Masuda
abstract:
Author(s): Zheyuan Liu, Hodaka Kikuchi, Zijun Wei, Shinichiro Asai, Mechthild Enderle, Ursula B. Hansen, Vasile O. Garlea, Manh D. Le, Gøran J. Nilsen, Igor A. Zaliznyak, and Takatsugu Masuda

Polarized inelastic neutron scattering gives the first unambiguous evidence of chirality of the split magnon bands in altermagnetic MnTe.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236705] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of switchable chiral magnons in the altermagnet MnTe using polarized inelastic neutron scattering.
motivation: Altermagnets are a newly discovered class of magnetic materials with unique spin-split bands, and understanding their magnon chirality is important for spintronics and magnonics.
method: The authors performed polarized inelastic neutron scattering experiments on single-crystal MnTe to measure the magnon dispersion and its chirality.
result: They observed clear splitting of magnon bands with opposite chirality, which can be switched by an external magnetic field.
conclusion: The results provide the first unambiguous evidence of chiral magnons in an altermagnet, opening new avenues for controlling spin currents.

title: Magneto-Optical Trapping Of A Metal Hydride Molecule
authors: Jinyu Dai, Benjamin Riley, Qi Sun, Debayan Mitra, And Tanya Zelevinsky
abstract:
Author(s): Jinyu Dai, Benjamin Riley, Qi Sun, Debayan Mitra, and Tanya Zelevinsky

Researchers have used laser cooling and trapping to isolate calcium monohydride, a key step toward producing ultracold atomic hydrogen.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233403] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the magneto-optical trapping of calcium monohydride (CaH) molecules, a step toward ultracold atomic hydrogen production.
motivation: Ultracold atomic hydrogen is important for precision measurements and quantum simulation, but direct laser cooling of hydrogen is challenging. Trapping a metal hydride like CaH provides a pathway to produce ultracold hydrogen via photodissociation.
method: The authors use laser cooling and magneto-optical trapping techniques on CaH molecules, leveraging their favorable electronic structure for efficient cooling.
result: Successful magneto-optical trapping of CaH is demonstrated, with characterization of trap lifetime and temperature.
conclusion: This work establishes a new platform for producing ultracold atomic hydrogen, enabling future studies in quantum science and precision measurements.

title: Role Of Anionic Lone-Pair-Like Electrons In Producing Minimum Lattice Thermal Conductivity
authors: Hongwei Ming, Jiahui Wang, Shike Xu, Bushra Jabar, Yunpeng Zheng, Zhong-Zhen Luo, And Zhigang Zou
abstract:
Author(s): Hongwei Ming, Jiahui Wang, Shike Xu, Bushra Jabar, Yunpeng Zheng, Zhong-Zhen Luo, and Zhigang Zou

Cationic lone-pair electrons are often associated with distinctive phonon properties (e.g., strong lattice anharmonicity) that lead to low lattice thermal conductivity ([MATH]). However, the reliance on specific cations (e.g., [MATH] or [MATH]) severely restri…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236301] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the role of anionic lone-pair-like electrons in achieving minimum lattice thermal conductivity in thermoelectric materials.
motivation: Cationic lone-pair electrons are known to cause low lattice thermal conductivity, but reliance on specific cations limits material design. The authors explore anionic lone-pair-like electrons as an alternative mechanism.
method: First-principles calculations and experimental measurements are used to study phonon properties and thermal conductivity in materials with anionic lone-pair-like electrons.
result: Anionic lone-pair-like electrons induce strong lattice anharmonicity and reduce lattice thermal conductivity to near-minimum values.
conclusion: Anionic lone-pair-like electrons can serve as a new design principle for thermoelectric materials with ultralow thermal conductivity.

title: Long-lived Metastable States In The $4{f}^{13}5d6s$ Configuration Of ${\mathrm{Yb}}^{+}$
authors: Z. E. D. Ackerman, A. Cadarso Quevedo, Ilango Maran, L. P. H. Gallagher, R. J. C. Spreeuw, J. C. Berengut, And R. Gerritsma
abstract:
Author(s): Z. E. D. Ackerman, A. Cadarso Quevedo, Ilango Maran, L. P. H. Gallagher, R. J. C. Spreeuw, J. C. Berengut, and R. Gerritsma

We study the occurrence of long-lived metastable states in the [MATH] electron configuration of [MATH]. By optical pumping of a single trapped ion on the [MATH] transition at 377.5 nm, we prepare a wide range of metastable electronic states…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062811] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies long-lived metastable states in the 4f13 5d 6s configuration of Yb+ ions using optical pumping and spectroscopy.
motivation: To identify and characterize metastable states in Yb+ that could be useful for precision measurements or quantum information applications.
method: Optical pumping of a single trapped Yb+ ion on a specific transition at 377.5 nm, followed by spectroscopy to probe the metastable states.
result: A wide range of metastable electronic states were prepared and their lifetimes measured, revealing long-lived states in the 4f13 5d 6s configuration.
conclusion: The identified metastable states may serve as resources for quantum computing or atomic clocks, but the paper is primarily an atomic physics characterization.

title: High-resolution Spectroscopy Of $^{162}\mathrm{Dy}$ Rydberg Levels
authors: G. Ferioli, P. Lombardi, P. Sekhar, E. Solé Cardona, N. Preti, C. Drevon, N. Antolini, L. Tanzi, G. Modugno, C. Gabbanini, F. Robicheaux, And A. Fioretti
abstract:
Author(s): G. Ferioli, P. Lombardi, P. Sekhar, E. Solé Cardona, N. Preti, C. Drevon, N. Antolini, L. Tanzi, G. Modugno, C. Gabbanini, F. Robicheaux, and A. Fioretti

The authors report on the high-resolution spectroscopy of over 700 Rydberg states in
[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062807] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: High-resolution spectroscopy of over 700 Rydberg states in dysprosium using two-color trap depletion spectroscopy.
motivation: To characterize Rydberg states in dysprosium for potential applications in quantum simulation and sensing.
method: Two-color trap depletion spectroscopy in a magneto-optical trap combined with multichannel quantum defect theory.
result: Measured and assigned over 700 Rydberg states, identified six perturbing states from higher ionization limits.
conclusion: Provides a benchmark for Rydberg state assignments in dysprosium, useful for future quantum experiments.

title: Exceptional Points In The Scattering Resonances Of A Sphere Dimer
authors: Emanuele Corsaro, Filippo Capolino, And Carlo Forestiere
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuele Corsaro, Filippo Capolino, and Carlo Forestiere

We investigate exceptional points of degeneracy (EPDs) in electromagnetic scattering of a sphere dimer from the electroquasistatic limit to the fully retarded regime. In the quasistatic limit, we prove that [MATH]-symmetric configurations, realized by spheres with complex-conjugate…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063520] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies exceptional points in electromagnetic scattering of a sphere dimer, focusing on quasistatic and retarded regimes.
motivation: Exceptional points in scattering systems have applications in sensing and wave control, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors analyze a sphere dimer model using electroquasistatic and fully retarded electromagnetic theory, proving existence of exceptional points under PT-symmetric conditions.
result: They demonstrate exceptional point degeneracies in the scattering resonances and characterize their behavior across frequency regimes.
conclusion: The work is a classical electromagnetic scattering study with no quantum or thermodynamic implications.

title: Alternative Representation Of Multichannel Rydberg Spectra: A Modified $K$-matrix And Lu-Fano Plot Applied To The Manganese Spectroscopy
authors: Justin D. Piel And Chris H. Greene
abstract:
Author(s): Justin D. Piel and Chris H. Greene

The well-known graphical representation called the Lu-Fano plot was originally developed for multichannel Rydberg spectroscopy, especially in quantum-defect theory. The present study shows some of the limitations of this traditional Lu-Fano plot that are desirable to improve on, when there are close…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062805] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a modified K-matrix and Lu-Fano plot for multichannel Rydberg spectroscopy, applied to manganese.
motivation: Traditional Lu-Fano plots have limitations when there are close channels; the authors aim to improve the graphical representation for multichannel Rydberg spectra.
method: They introduce a modified K-matrix formulation and an alternative Lu-Fano plot, and demonstrate it on manganese spectroscopy data.
result: The modified representation overcomes some limitations of the traditional Lu-Fano plot, providing clearer visualization of channel interactions.
conclusion: The alternative representation is a useful tool for analyzing multichannel Rydberg spectra, particularly in complex atoms like manganese.

title: Altermagnetism Of Ultrathin CrSb Slabs
authors: Brahim Marfoua, Mohammad Amirabbasi, And Marcus Ekholm
abstract:
Author(s): Brahim Marfoua, Mohammad Amirabbasi, and Marcus Ekholm

Altermagnets exhibit momentum-dependent spin splitting without net magnetization, combining characteristics of both ferromagnets and antiferromagnets, making them highly interesting for spintronics applications. CrSb is a prime candidate with a high Néel temperature ($∼700{0ex}…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214439] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies altermagnetism in ultrathin CrSb slabs, focusing on electronic structure and spintronic applications.
motivation: Altermagnets offer momentum-dependent spin splitting without net magnetization, promising for spintronics; CrSb has high Néel temperature.
method: First-principles calculations based on density functional theory (DFT) to investigate electronic and magnetic properties of CrSb slabs.
result: Ultrathin CrSb slabs exhibit altermagnetic behavior with spin splitting in the band structure.
conclusion: CrSb slabs are viable for spintronic devices, but the work is purely materials science without quantum information or thermodynamics connection.

title: Bilateral Hydrogenation-induced high-Chern-number Quantum Anomalous Hall State In Monolayer ${\mathrm{Cr}}_{2}{\mathrm{Ge}}_{2}{\mathrm{Te}}_{6}$
authors: Xiang Li, Xin-Wei Yi, Jing-Yang You, Jia-Wen Li, Qing-Han Yang, Gang Su, And Bo Gu
abstract:
Author(s): Xiang Li, Xin-Wei Yi, Jing-Yang You, Jia-Wen Li, Qing-Han Yang, Gang Su, and Bo Gu

The pursuit of high-temperature quantum anomalous Hall (QAH) insulators faces fundamental challenges, including narrow topological gaps and low Curie temperatures ([MATH]) in existing materials. Here, we propose a transformative strategy using bilateral hydrogenation to engineer a robust Q…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224430] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes bilateral hydrogenation to engineer a high-Chern-number quantum anomalous Hall state in monolayer Cr2Ge2Te6, focusing on topological properties and Curie temperature enhancement.
motivation: High-temperature quantum anomalous Hall insulators are sought after but limited by narrow gaps and low Curie temperatures; the authors aim to overcome these via chemical functionalization.
method: First-principles calculations are used to study the electronic structure and topological properties of hydrogenated monolayer Cr2Ge2Te6, including band structure, Chern number, and magnetic anisotropy.
result: Bilateral hydrogenation induces a high Chern number (C=2) QAH state with a large topological gap and enhanced Curie temperature compared to the pristine material.
conclusion: Hydrogenation is an effective strategy to realize robust QAH states in 2D magnets, potentially enabling high-temperature quantum anomalous Hall effect.

title: Tetrahedral Ferromagnetic Correlations And A Glassy-freezing Anomaly In The Breathing Pyrochlore Magnet ${\mathrm{AgInCr}}_{4}{\mathrm{S}}_{8}$ With Partial $A$-site Disorder
authors: Yuya Haraguchi, Masahiro Kitamura, Masaki Gen, Yusuke Nambu, Akira Matsuo, Koichi Kindo, Masaki Kondo, Masashi Tokunaga, And Hiroko Aruga Katori
abstract:
Author(s): Yuya Haraguchi, Masahiro Kitamura, Masaki Gen, Yusuke Nambu, Akira Matsuo, Koichi Kindo, Masaki Kondo, Masashi Tokunaga, and Hiroko Aruga Katori

We investigate the chromium breathing-pyrochlore sulfide [MATH], a chromium-based thiospinel, by synchrotron x-ray and neutron powder diffraction, dc magnetization, and heat capacity. Diffraction confirms the [MATH] breathing structure with alternating lar…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214437] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies magnetic correlations and glassy freezing in a breathing pyrochlore magnet with partial A-site disorder.
motivation: To understand the magnetic properties of the breathing pyrochlore AgInCr4S8, which exhibits tetrahedral ferromagnetic correlations and a glassy-freezing anomaly.
method: Synchrotron x-ray and neutron powder diffraction, dc magnetization, and heat capacity measurements.
result: Confirms breathing pyrochlore structure with alternating large/small tetrahedra; reveals ferromagnetic correlations within tetrahedra and a glassy freezing transition at low temperatures.
conclusion: The partial A-site disorder leads to a unique magnetic state combining ferromagnetic clusters and spin-glass-like freezing.

title: Mirror-time Reversal Symmetry Controlled Antiferromagnetic Tunnel Junctions
authors: Jing Sun, Xiaohong Zheng, Kang Jia, Xiaoli Fan, And Tengfei Cao
abstract:
Author(s): Jing Sun, Xiaohong Zheng, Kang Jia, Xiaoli Fan, and Tengfei Cao

Unconventional antiferromagnets with intrinsic spin splitting enable spin-polarized transport similar to ferromagnets with zero net magnetization, offering substantial potential applications in high-density, nonvolatile spintronic devices. However, achieving efficient electric-field controlled tunne…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214438] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies antiferromagnetic tunnel junctions controlled by mirror-time reversal symmetry, focusing on spintronic applications.
motivation: To achieve efficient electric-field controlled tunneling in antiferromagnetic spintronic devices for high-density nonvolatile memory.
method: The authors theoretically investigate spin-polarized transport in antiferromagnetic tunnel junctions using symmetry analysis and first-principles calculations.
result: They demonstrate that mirror-time reversal symmetry enables spin splitting and tunnel magnetoresistance, controllable by an electric field.
conclusion: The work provides a pathway for electric-field-controlled antiferromagnetic spintronics, but is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Observation Of Momentum Dependent Charge Density Wave Gap In ${\mathrm{EuTe}}_{4}$
authors: Iftakhar Bin Elius, Nathan Valadez, Gyanendra Dhakal, Volodymyr Buturlim, Sabin Regmi, Dante James, Peter Radanovich, Keng Tou Chu, Ellis Thompson, Matthew Yankowitz, Tetiana Romanova, Andrzej Ptok, Krzysztof Gofryk, Dariusz Kaczorowski, And Madhab Neupane

Charge density wave (CDW) phenomena in low-dimensional rare-earth chalcogenides have drawn considerable interest owing to their interplay with lattice instabilities, electronic correlations, and magnetism. [MATH], which contains both mono- and bilayer Te pseudosquare nets together wit…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235125] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of a momentum-dependent charge density wave gap in EuTe4 using ARPES and DFT.
motivation: To understand the interplay between charge density waves, lattice instabilities, and magnetism in rare-earth chalcogenides.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and density functional theory (DFT) calculations.
result: A momentum-dependent CDW gap is observed, with the gap size varying across the Brillouin zone.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into the electronic structure of EuTe4 and the nature of its CDW phase.

title: Sommerfeld Coefficient Enhancement And Magnetic Short-range Order In A Hyperkagome $3d$ Electron System
authors: Shin-Ichi Shamoto, Yukio Yasui, Kanako Yoshizawa, Yukio Noda, Miwako Takahashi, Yoshichika Ōnuki, Yoshinori Haga, Motoyuki Ishikado, Hiroki Yamauchi, Tsung-Cheng Huang, Min Kai Lee, And Lieh-Jeng Chang
abstract:
Author(s): Shin-ichi Shamoto, Yukio Yasui, Kanako Yoshizawa, Yukio Noda, Miwako Takahashi, Yoshichika Ōnuki, Yoshinori Haga, Motoyuki Ishikado, Hiroki Yamauchi, Tsung-Cheng Huang, Min Kai Lee, and Lieh-Jeng Chang

[MATH]-Mn shows a large Sommerfeld coefficient of 70 mJ [MATH], which is one of the largest values in [MATH]-electron systems. Although the origin has been attributed to the fluctuating magnetic moment, there are no material-dependent systematic studies in the [MATH]-electron…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235126] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Sommerfeld coefficient enhancement and magnetic short-range order in a hyperkagome 3d electron system, focusing on material-specific properties.
motivation: To understand the origin of the large Sommerfeld coefficient in a 3d electron system, which is attributed to fluctuating magnetic moments but lacks systematic study.
method: Experimental measurements and analysis of specific heat, magnetic susceptibility, and neutron scattering on a hyperkagome lattice material.
result: Observation of enhanced Sommerfeld coefficient and evidence of magnetic short-range order.
conclusion: The large Sommerfeld coefficient is linked to magnetic fluctuations and short-range order in this 3d electron system.

title: Low-energy Excitations In $A$-site Ordered ${\mathrm{SmBaMn}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{6}$
authors: Mirian Garcia Fernandez, Abhishek Nag, Stefano Agrestini, Sahil Tippireddy, Dirk Backes, Xiaoyang Chen, Urs Staub, Taka-Hisa Arima, And Kejin Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Mirian Garcia Fernandez, Abhishek Nag, Stefano Agrestini, Sahil Tippireddy, Dirk Backes, Xiaoyang Chen, Urs Staub, Taka-Hisa Arima, and Kejin Zhou

The electron in a solid can be considered a bound state of the three independent, fundamental degrees of freedom creating quasiparticles: spinons, carrying the electron spin; plasmons, carrying the collective charge mode; and orbitons, carrying its orbital degree of freedom. These fundamental degree…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235128] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies low-energy excitations in the A-site ordered manganite SmBaMn2O6 using resonant inelastic X-ray scattering, focusing on orbitons and their coupling to spin and charge degrees of freedom.
motivation: Understanding the interplay of spin, charge, and orbital degrees of freedom in strongly correlated electron systems is a fundamental goal in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors performed resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) measurements at the Mn L3 edge to probe orbital excitations and analyzed the spectra using theoretical models.
result: They observed multiple orbiton modes and identified their dispersion, revealing significant coupling between orbital, spin, and charge excitations.
conclusion: The study provides detailed insights into the orbital physics of SmBaMn2O6, highlighting the complex interplay of electronic degrees of freedom in manganites.

title: Pressure-induced $b1$ To $b2$ Phase Transition In CeN Studied By $ab Initio$ Correlation Matrix Renormalization Theory Calculations
authors: Jun Liu, Jianhua Zhang, Yongxin Yao, Kai-Ming Ho, And Cai-Zhuang Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Jun Liu, Jianhua Zhang, Yongxin Yao, Kai-Ming Ho, and Cai-Zhuang Wang

We apply correlation matrix renormalization theory (CMRT) to cerium nitride (CeN) under pressure. For [MATH] (NaCl-type) phase, CMRT gives an equation of state consistent with ambient pressure experiments. It produces electronic density-of-state (DOS) characterized by a sharp [MATH] quasiparticle resona…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245130] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a pressure-induced structural phase transition in CeN using correlation matrix renormalization theory, focusing on electronic structure and equation of state.
motivation: To understand the electronic and structural properties of CeN under pressure, particularly the b1 to b2 phase transition, using a computational method.
method: Correlation matrix renormalization theory (CMRT) is applied to calculate the equation of state, electronic density of states, and quasiparticle resonance for CeN in both b1 and b2 phases.
result: CMRT reproduces the ambient pressure equation of state and predicts the phase transition pressure; the electronic DOS shows a sharp f-electron quasiparticle resonance.
conclusion: CMRT is effective for studying correlated materials like CeN under pressure, and the results provide insights into the phase transition and electronic properties.

title: Algebraic To Exponential Decay Of Spatial Correlations In One-dimensional And Confined Hard-core Fluids: A Laplace-pole Analysis
authors: Ana M. Montero And Andrés Santos
abstract:
Author(s): Ana M. Montero and Andrés Santos

We derive the asymptotic behavior of the radial distribution function [MATH] for one-dimensional (1D) hard-rod systems and related quasi-one-dimensional geometries at high packing fractions using Laplace transform techniques and pole analysis. By identifying the poles and residues of the Laplace tra…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064133] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the asymptotic decay of spatial correlations in one-dimensional hard-rod fluids using Laplace transform pole analysis.
motivation: Understanding the decay of correlations in confined hard-core fluids is important for statistical mechanics of fluids, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors use Laplace transform techniques and pole analysis to derive the asymptotic behavior of the radial distribution function for 1D hard-rod systems and quasi-1D geometries at high packing fractions.
result: They show that spatial correlations decay algebraically or exponentially depending on the system parameters, determined by the poles of the Laplace transform.
conclusion: The work provides a detailed analytical characterization of correlation decay in classical hard-core fluids, but has no relevance to the user's research interests.

title: Universality And Ambiguity In Extremes Of Anomalous Diffusion
authors: Sean D. Lawley
abstract:
Author(s): Sean D. Lawley

Many biophysical processes begin when the fastest searcher finds a target out of many random searchers, which is called an extreme or fastest first passage time (fFPT). In some models (i) the fFPT vanishes logarithmically as the number of searchers grows and (ii) the fFPT can be faster for subdiffus…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064135] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the scaling of fastest first-passage times in anomalous diffusion processes, focusing on universality and ambiguity in extreme statistics.
motivation: Many biophysical processes depend on the fastest searcher among many, but the behavior of extreme first-passage times in anomalous diffusion is not fully understood.
method: The author analyzes mathematical models of subdiffusion and superdiffusion to derive asymptotic scaling laws for the fastest first-passage time as the number of searchers grows.
result: The fastest first-passage time vanishes logarithmically for some models but can be faster for subdiffusion, revealing ambiguity in the definition of anomalous diffusion extremes.
conclusion: The findings highlight the need for careful interpretation of extreme statistics in anomalous transport, with implications for biophysical search processes.

title: Pacemaker-induced Spiral Wave Chimeras On A Sphere Of Delay-coupled Oscillators: Switching Between Different Spiral-phase Kinks
authors: Chol-Ung Choe, Ryong-Son Kim, And Jin-Song Kang
abstract:
Author(s): Chol-Ung Choe, Ryong-Son Kim, and Jin-Song Kang

Two-dimensional systems of nonlocally coupled oscillators exhibit spiral wave chimeras, a phenomenon that has garnered significant attention in nonlinear dynamics. These chimeras are characterized by the simultaneous presence of synchronized spiral regions and desynchronized phase-randomized cores. …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064206] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spiral wave chimeras in delay-coupled oscillators on a sphere, focusing on switching between different spiral-phase kinks.
motivation: Spiral wave chimeras are a fascinating pattern in nonlinear dynamics, and understanding their behavior on curved surfaces like a sphere is of theoretical interest.
method: The authors use numerical simulations of a system of nonlocally coupled phase oscillators with time delay on a spherical geometry.
result: They observe that pacemaker-induced spiral wave chimeras can switch between different spiral-phase kink states depending on parameters.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the dynamics of chimera states on curved surfaces, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Regime Identification And Control Of Extremes In The Nonautonomous Lorenz Model With Chaos And Intransitivity
authors: Moyan Liu, Qin Huang, And Upmanu Lall
abstract:
Author(s): Moyan Liu, Qin Huang, and Upmanu Lall

Adaptive chaos control has been studied extensively for autonomous systems. For real-world, nonautonomous systems, such as planetary weather, observations of the system state in response to seasonally and diurnally varying forcing are available only at discrete times and locations. We consider a sto…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064207] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies regime identification and control of extremes in a nonautonomous Lorenz model with chaos and intransitivity, focusing on climate dynamics.
motivation: Real-world nonautonomous systems like planetary weather require adaptive chaos control methods that account for time-varying forcing and discrete observations.
method: A stochastic approach is used to identify regimes and control extremes in the nonautonomous Lorenz model, incorporating chaos and intransitivity.
result: The method successfully identifies regimes and controls extreme events in the model.
conclusion: The approach may be applicable to real-world climate systems for predicting and mitigating extreme weather events.

title: Resource And Population Dynamics In An Agent-environment Interaction Model
authors: Gaston Briozzo, Gustavo J. Sibona, And Fernando Peruani
abstract:
Author(s): Gaston Briozzo, Gustavo J. Sibona, and Fernando Peruani

In any ecosystem, the conditions of the environment and the characteristics of the species that inhabit it are entangled, coevolving in space and time. We introduce a model that couples active agents with a dynamic environment, interpreted as a nutrient source. Agents are persistent random walkers t…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064406] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper models the coevolution of active agents and a dynamic nutrient environment, focusing on population dynamics and resource consumption.
motivation: To understand the entangled coevolution of species and their environment in ecosystems.
method: The authors introduce a model coupling persistent random walkers (agents) with a dynamic environment that acts as a nutrient source, and analyze the resulting resource and population dynamics.
result: The model reveals complex feedback loops between agent movement and resource distribution, leading to emergent spatial patterns and population cycles.
conclusion: The study provides insights into how agent-environment interactions shape ecosystem dynamics, with potential applications in ecology and active matter.

title: Threshold And Quasistationary Distribution For The Susceptible-infectious-susceptible Model On Networks
authors: George T. Cantwell And Cristopher Moore
abstract:
Author(s): George T. Cantwell and Cristopher Moore

Giving nodes a memory of their susceptibility transition dynamically expands the state space in the susceptible-infectious-susceptible model. This enhanced pair approximation accurately determines epidemic thresholds and infection fractions across arbitrary networks.

tldr: This paper studies epidemic thresholds and quasistationary distributions for the SIS model on networks using an enhanced pair approximation.
motivation: Understanding epidemic spread on networks is important for public health, but the paper focuses on classical epidemiological modeling rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors introduce a memory of susceptibility transition to expand the state space and apply an enhanced pair approximation to analyze the SIS model on arbitrary networks.
result: The enhanced pair approximation accurately determines epidemic thresholds and infection fractions across various network topologies.
conclusion: The proposed approximation provides a more accurate description of epidemic dynamics on networks, but the work is purely classical and unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: Chromatic Percolation In Two-dimensional Multitype Particle Systems With Extended-range Homotypic Repulsion
authors: Tingting Yin, Yan Sui, Xueying Yuan, And Xian Kong
abstract:
Author(s): Tingting Yin, Yan Sui, Xueying Yuan, and Xian Kong

Cells in many tissues repel like neighbors over extended ranges, yet standard jamming models ignore this diversity. We introduce chromatic percolation—the percolation of like-type particles driven by extended-range homotypic repulsion in multitype assemblies—and map its relation to mechanical jammin…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065412] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces chromatic percolation in multitype particle systems with extended-range homotypic repulsion, linking percolation to mechanical jamming.
motivation: Standard jamming models ignore diversity in cell repulsion ranges; the authors aim to understand how homotypic repulsion drives percolation and jamming in multitype assemblies.
method: They define chromatic percolation as percolation of like-type particles under extended-range homotypic repulsion and map it to mechanical jamming using computational models.
result: The study reveals a relationship between chromatic percolation and jamming transitions in two-dimensional multitype systems.
conclusion: Chromatic percolation provides a framework to connect percolation theory with jamming in biological tissues and soft matter.

title: Supratransmission In Lattices With Purely Nonlinear Coupling
authors: Defri Ahmad, Tae-Yeon Kim, Andreas Schiffer, Jinkyu Yang, And Hadi Susanto

Author(s): Defri Ahmad, Tae-Yeon Kim, Andreas Schiffer, Jinkyu Yang, and Hadi Susanto

Supratransmission is examined in nonlinear lattices with purely nonlinear coupling, extending the phenomenon to systems that lack a linear passband. In contrast to standard lattices with mixed linear-nonlinear interactions, the present model has no linear spectrum, so energy propagation arises entir…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064205] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies supratransmission in nonlinear lattices with purely nonlinear coupling, where energy propagation occurs without a linear passband.
motivation: To understand energy transmission in nonlinear systems that lack linear spectrum, extending supratransmission to purely nonlinear couplings.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of a lattice model with purely nonlinear coupling, examining conditions for supratransmission.
result: Supratransmission is possible even without linear passband, with energy propagation driven solely by nonlinear interactions.
conclusion: Nonlinear coupling alone can support supratransmission, broadening the understanding of energy transport in nonlinear lattices.

title: Entropic Clustering Of Stickers Induces Aging In Biocondensates
authors: Hugo Le Roy And Paolo de Los Rios
abstract:
Author(s): Hugo Le Roy and Paolo De Los Rios

Biomolecular condensates are cellular phase-separated droplets that usually exhibit a viscoelastic mechanical response, a behavior rationalized by modeling the complex molecules that make up a condensate as stickers and spacers, which assemble into a network-like structure. Condensates usually exhib…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064405] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper models biomolecular condensates as sticker-spacer networks and shows that entropic clustering of stickers leads to aging behavior.
motivation: Biomolecular condensates exhibit viscoelastic mechanical response, but the microscopic origin of aging in these systems is not well understood.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model based on stickers and spacers, using statistical mechanics to study the dynamics of network formation and aging.
result: Entropic clustering of stickers naturally leads to aging, characterized by a time-dependent increase in the elastic modulus.
conclusion: The sticker-spacer model captures the aging behavior of biocondensates, providing a physical mechanism for their viscoelastic properties.

title: Most Probable Path And Invariant Sets In Noise-induced Transition To Turbulence
authors: Yoshiki Hiruta, Kento Yasuda, And Kenta Ishimoto
abstract:
Author(s): Yoshiki Hiruta, Kento Yasuda, and Kenta Ishimoto

Turbulence transition often arises from a subcritical transition between bistable states characterized by invariant sets of deterministic dynamical systems, and such transitions can be triggered by system noise as rare events. In this study, we employ the Onsager-Machlup (OM) formulation of stochast…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023303] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies noise-induced transitions to turbulence using the Onsager-Machlup formulation to find most probable paths and invariant sets.
motivation: Understanding turbulence transition from bistable states triggered by noise is a fundamental problem in fluid dynamics.
method: The authors apply the Onsager-Machlup path integral formalism to stochastic dynamical systems to compute most probable transition paths and identify invariant sets.
result: They characterize the most probable paths and invariant sets associated with noise-induced transitions to turbulence.
conclusion: The work provides insight into the role of noise in triggering turbulence transitions, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Current-induced Successive Structural Phase Transitions Beyond Thermal Equilibrium In Single-crystal ${\mathrm{VO}}_{2}$
authors: Shunsuke Kitou, Akitoshi Nakano, Masato Imaizumi, Yuiga Nakamura, Yuto Nakamura, Hideo Kishida, Taka-Hisa Arima, And Ichiro Terasaki
abstract:
Author(s): Shunsuke Kitou, Akitoshi Nakano, Masato Imaizumi, Yuiga Nakamura, Yuto Nakamura, Hideo Kishida, Taka-hisa Arima, and Ichiro Terasaki

Using synchrotron x-ray diffraction, optical microscopy, and Raman spectroscopy, current-induced structural phase transitions in single-crystal vanadium dioxide are investigated. [Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022050] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports current-induced structural phase transitions in VO2 single crystals, revealing nonequilibrium metallic phases not accessible under thermal equilibrium.
motivation: To understand how electric currents can drive structural phase transitions beyond thermal equilibrium, potentially enabling new pathways to control material properties.
method: Combined synchrotron x-ray diffraction, optical microscopy, and Raman spectroscopy to characterize structural changes in single-crystal VO2 under applied current.
result: Observation of successive transitions to two distinct metallic tetragonal phases, including a nonequilibrium structure with isotropic lattice expansion.
conclusion: Current-induced effects can produce structural phases inaccessible by heating alone, highlighting the role of non-thermal pathways in phase transitions.

title: Dynamical Learning In Deep Asymmetric Recurrent Neural Networks
authors: Davide Badalotti, Carlo Baldassi, Marc Mézard, Mattia Scardecchia, And Riccardo Zecchina
abstract:
Author(s): Davide Badalotti, Carlo Baldassi, Marc Mézard, Mattia Scardecchia, and Riccardo Zecchina
